##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.2 — The registry's upsert writes 6 of its 18 columns, so a re-registration cannot correct a policy line

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`, from the census's own question — *what would it take to correct one of these lines?*
- **The finding, derived rather than read.** `resolvers.rs::register` INSERTs **18** columns and its `ON CONFLICT (resolver_id) DO UPDATE SET` writes **6** — `schemes`, `egress_class`, `sandbox_level`, `version`, `security_evidence`, `max_bytes`. The other **11** keep their old value on a re-registration: `locator_patterns`, `media_types`, `abilities`, `authentication_classes`, all four `*_policy` columns, `snapshot_formats`, `derivation_formats`, `latency_range_ms`.
- 🔴 **So a corrected advertisement does not reach an existing row.** `sync_gated_entries` calls `register` on every startup while the gate is open, and only DELETEs when it closes — ship new code changing a deny-policy, restart with the gate still open, and the registry keeps publishing the old word.
- 🔴 **And it breaks a documented promise, which is what makes this more than an omission.** `api.rs::register_resolver`'s own doc comment says the operator *registers (**or replaces**)* an advertise, and `advertised_media_types`' own doc comment — `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/resolvers.rs:211`, citing `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_r2-acquisition-accept-set.md` — states that *a deployment that narrows a pack's advertisement narrows what that pack may acquire, in the same act*. ⚠️ **Attribution corrected by `.7.3.6.2`:** REPAIR-0266 put that sentence in the decision RECORD, which does not contain it — the record says the admitted set is *the ranked row's own `media_types`, read at resolution time*, and the *same act* promise is the code's. The finding is unchanged; the citation was wrong and a NAMED INSTANCE is graded exact. `media_types` is the field that decision is about, and it is one of the 11 the upsert drops — so the narrowing silently does not happen, while `advertised_media_types` keeps reading the wider set per resolution.
- Owns: deciding whether the upsert writes every column or refuses a partial replace, and reproducing the stale-row case before repairing it.
- Acceptance: a control registers a pack, re-registers it with a narrowed `media_types` and a changed policy line, and observes the OLD values still served — RED before the repair; after it, the re-registration is either complete or refused by name, with the decision recorded; the `2026-09-12` accept-set decision is re-read and either upheld or superseded; and the existing resolver suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0267.
- ⚠️ **The re-read changed the repair, and this is the load-bearing part of the leaf.** Re-reading the 2026-09-12 decision as the acceptance requires turned up a finding this leaf did not make and would have contradicted: `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.1.1` measured that `resolver_capabilities` has **no tenant column** and a single-column `resolver_id` key, while `register_resolver` admits on the caller's OWN `tenant_admin` grant — so any tenant's administrator can address any row, **the built-in `r0-https-fetcher`'s included**. That is an authority defect owned by `.7.1`, and it says the upsert's reach is too LARGE.
- ⛔ **So "make the upsert write all 18 columns" was REJECTED as the whole answer.** It would have handed an unbound principal eleven more columns on a site-global row — `media_types`, which decides what the acquisition leg admits, and all four advertised policies among them. A repair that satisfies a doc comment by enlarging the surface another leaf has to bind is not a repair. ⭐ `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 2: the cheapest oracle is the project's own history, and here it had already ruled the other way about the same mechanism.
- **The decision, split by CALLER because the two callers have two different trusts:**

| caller | may replace? | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sync_gated_entries`, at boot | **yes, completely** — all 17 non-key columns | the advertisement compiled into the binary is the truth; a drifted row loses to it |
| `POST /v1/resolvers` | **no** — `invalid_transition` (409), naming the row | the table has no tenant column, so any tenant admin addresses any row |

- 🔴 **REPRODUCED AT RUNTIME BEFORE THE REPAIR, both halves, each as its own control so neither RED hides behind the other's panic.** (1) `a_replace_is_complete_and_the_http_verb_does_not_perform_one` fails at `the startup sync restores the advertised subresource policy`, `left: "allow"`, `right: "deny"` — drift written into the row survived the boot sync. (2) `the_resolver_verb_refuses_to_replace_an_existing_advertise` fails with `left: 200`, `right: 409` and the product's own body as the evidence: **`{"registered":true,"resolver_id":"rsv-replace-probe"}`** for a re-registration that narrowed `media_types`, changed `subresource_policy`, and changed nothing at all. `test result: FAILED. 56 passed; 2 failed`.
- ⭐ **The first control drives the repair through a path a test can actually reach.** `register` is not exported from the crate root, and `gated_advertises()` is a private literal, so neither can be called directly. Instead: open the gate (the R3 row appears), write drift into the four columns the old upsert did not touch, re-run `sync_gated_entries`. That asserts a real product property — the boot sync is authoritative over the registry row — rather than a function's signature.
- ⛔ **`registered_at` is deliberately NOT in the update list.** It is when the resolver first appeared, and a re-registration does not make it new.
- ✅ **The refusal is a bound, not a blackout**, and the control says so: a DIFFERENT resolver still registers `200` in the same test, and the refused row is read back and asserted byte-for-byte unchanged — a refusal that half-applied would be worse than the no-op it replaces.
- ⚠️ **What is lost, stated rather than discovered.** An operator can no longer change a registered advertise through the API. That capability was never usable for its documented purpose — it could not narrow `media_types` and could not correct a policy line — while the part that did work was the part that should not have. Removing it removes a hazard and no working use case.
- ⭐ **It NARROWS `.7.1`'s surface and does not discharge it.** The replace half of `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.1.1`'s finding closes; creating a new site-global resolver on a tenant-admin grant is untouched, and that is the larger half. `docs/book/src/qualification-review.md`'s row is narrowed, not removed.
- 🔎 **An environment fact found on the way, and it is a consequence DOC-0060 did not name.** The first RED run reported **3** failures, not 2: `the_r2_acquisition_persists_the_served_document_s_own_evidence` and `the_r2_mismatch_refusal_persists_neither_snapshot_nor_derivation` panicked with *the extraction worker is absent at `target/debug/reasonbraid-extract`: this control cannot be reported either way without it*. ⭐ The controls are right to refuse rather than pass vacuously — but the debug-tree retirement left them unreportable, and the retirement's record says only that the next build is cold. **Run `cargo build --workspace --bins --locked` before the pg suites after a debug retirement.** Both pass once it has run.

RED before the repair: `56 passed; 2 failed`, rc=101, with the source files at HEAD and only the test file modified (`git status --short crates/`).

- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_a-replace-is-complete-and-the-verb-does-not-perform-one.md`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.3 — The advertisement and the enforcement are two constants a comment holds together

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`, whose reader census returned **0 reads** across the four `*_policy` fields in 34 field mentions on 32 lines.
- **The finding.** `.7.3.5` made the R3 worker deny what the registry advertises, and hard-wrote the behaviour into the worker: a `Document` request for a requested URL continues, everything else fails. Nothing derives that behaviour from the advertised words, and nothing compares them: `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --readers` classifies every occurrence of each field in tracked Rust and returns **0 reads** across all four `*_policy` fields, with `read` as the default for anything no rule explains, so the claim can only be under-stated. The underlying population, so a reader can check the instrument is hiding nothing: `git grep -c -E 'redirect_policy|archive_policy|subresource_policy|javascript_policy' -- crates | awk -F: '{n+=$2} END {print n}'` → **32 LINES**. ⚠️ The census reports **34** because its unit is a *field mention*, not a line, and one line names three of the four (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/resolvers.rs:28`, the INSERT's column list): 32 + 2 = 34. Both numbers are right and they answer different questions; the field-mention count is the one the claim is about. The two are joined by a comment (`crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs:331`) naming `gated_advertises`.
- ⚠️ **Do NOT assume the answer is "read the row".** Letting a database row decide a security posture widens the surface rather than narrowing it — an operator with the register verb would then be able to turn the browser's isolation off by writing a word. `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §5B's derived-constant rule offers the cheaper shape: GATE the pair, so an advertisement that moves away from what the code enforces fails a control.
- Owns: choosing between deriving the behaviour from one source and gating the pair, and applying it to the two lines `.7.3.5` enforced.
- Acceptance: flipping the advertised word in the producer, with the worker unchanged, makes a control go RED — observed, not asserted; the chosen mechanism is recorded with the rejected alternative and its reason; and the browser suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0268.
- ⭐ **THE PAIR WAS ALREADY GATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and saying so is most of this leaf.** The leaf was opened expecting to build a mechanism; measuring first found two, built by two earlier leaves that did not know about each other. What was missing was that nothing SAID they were a pair, and that they are guarded at wildly different strengths.
- **Direction 1 — the advertisement moves, the worker does not.** Gated by `scripts/census_advertised_policies.py` (`.7.3.6.1`), whose ledger pins each verdict to the VALUE it was earned for. Observed RED again here, in situ: flipping R3's `subresource_policy` from `deny` to `allow` in `gated_advertises` with the worker untouched prints `the verdict 'enforced' was earned for 'deny', the producer now advertises 'allow'` at `resolvers.rs:320`, rc=1. Restored byte-identical; re-check `36 advertised lines, every one carries a verdict`.
- **Direction 2 — the worker moves, the advertisement does not.** Gated by `a_subresource_the_pack_advertises_as_denied_is_not_dialed` (`.7.3.5`), which drives a real Chrome and reads an origin's own counter.
- 🔴 **AND THAT IS THE ASYMMETRY THIS LEAF REPAIRS.** Direction 1 is a doctrine gate in the pre-commit hook: it runs on **every commit**. Direction 2 needs a browser, so it runs in CI — `.github/workflows/rust.yml` wraps `cargo test --all` in `scripts/ci_browser.py` — and CI runs **at push**. The cadence is ~300 commits (`COMMIT.md`), and the tree is **237 commits ahead of `origin/main`** as this closes. ⛔ So one half of one claim was guarded hundreds of commits more loosely than the other, and nothing said so.
- **The repair: the decision becomes a pure function.** `refusing_policy(is_document, url, requested) -> Option<&'static str>` in `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs` is the whole of the R3 request policy, lifted out of the async interception closure it was inline in. It touches no network, no browser and no filesystem, so `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --bins` covers it — **8 → 12 tests, 0.08 s**, wherever cargo runs. ⛔ The end-to-end control is NOT replaced: it stays the proof that the decision is actually wired to Chrome's `Fetch` domain, which a pure function cannot show.
- ⚠️ **THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, and it is the one the leaf warned about.** Plumbing the advertised word down to the worker — deriving behaviour from one source instead of gating two — would make a value decide whether this pack isolates anything. `resolver_capabilities` has no tenant column (`.11.9.1.1.1`), so that value is writable by any tenant administrator, and `.7.3.6.2` had just refused to widen that same surface. ⛔ A one-source design that puts the source where an attacker can reach it is worse than two sources with a gate between them.
- ⚠️ **A second rejected alternative, cheaper and still wrong:** sharing the label strings (`"subresource"`, `"redirect"`) between the crates via `reasonbraid-adapter`. It would add a dependency edge and bind the wrong thing — the labels are not the claim. `subresource_policy: "deny"` could flip to `"allow"` without either label changing.
- 🔴 **FALSIFIED TWICE, both neutralizations in situ and restored byte-identical.** (1) The **pre-`.7.3.5` defect**, `refusing_policy` returning `None` for everything: `9 passed; 3 failed`. (2) The **almost-fix** `.7.3.5` itself neutralized into — *deny means deny*, refusing every request including the navigation: `8 passed; 4 failed`. ⭐ The discriminating arm is `a_policy_that_refused_everything_would_fail_this`, which fires on (2) and **not** on (1) — so the suite separates a policy from a blackout rather than merely detecting change.
- ⭐ **One arm documents an edge rather than hiding it:** `the_asked_for_comparison_is_exact_and_fails_closed` states that a trailing slash makes a URL a different URL, so a server that normalises the navigation target yields a document request the policy calls a redirect. That is the fail-closed direction, and it is now written down instead of waiting to be discovered.
- Verification: `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --bins --locked` → **`test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed`** in 0.08 s (was 8). `python3 -B scripts/ci_browser.py --timeout 900 -- cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --test browser_roundtrip --locked` → see the acceptance block. `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --check` rc=0; `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-browse --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0.
- promotion: pending — the transferable half is *two halves of one claim can be gated at cadences hundreds of commits apart, and the weaker one is invisible because both are green*. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md` and routed.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0268 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.3): the pair was gated at two cadences, and the looser half is now a pure function`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.4 — The egress ladder is compared in the direction that admits a wider pack than the caller asked for

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`, which had to decide what `egress_class` MEANS before it could grade seven lines and found the comparison answering a different question from the one ADR-018 states.
- **The finding, derived over the whole 4 × 6 matrix.** `resolvers.rs` filters both ADR-018 classes with the same test, `declared >= required`. For `sandbox_level` the ladder runs `none < process < constrained_process < vm_container` — higher is MORE isolated — so the test is a genuine safety floor. For `egress_class` the ladder runs `none < loopback < listed < any` — higher is MORE reach — so the same test is a *capability* floor, and the only combination it refuses out of 24 is a caller asking for the WIDEST class.
- 🔴 **The consequence, stated as a row rather than as a worry.** A caller requiring `egress_class: "listed"` is served `rx-agent-mediated`, which declares `any`. There is no value of `required_egress` that means *do not give me a pack that can dial anywhere* — which is the one thing ADR-018 says the class is for: *the allowed destinations … the claim is the MAXIMUM, never the minimum*.
- ⚠️ **The code is internally consistent and the ADR is what it contradicts, so the repair is a decision and not an obvious inversion.** The shipped default `required_egress: "loopback"` only makes sense under the capability reading — under the bound reading no pack would ever be eligible, since every pack declares `listed` or `any`.
- ⭐ **A second observation from the same matrix, recorded rather than acted on here:** with the shipped defaults (`sandbox_level: "process"`, `egress_class: "loopback"`), R0, R1, R5 and RX are all ineligible, because each declares `sandbox_level: "none"`. Every test in the suite passes `"required_sandbox": "none"` explicitly. Fail-closed and therefore safe, but the documented default of `POST /v1/resources/{id}/resolve` resolves nothing for the flagship pack.
- ⛔ **A third, smaller one:** `required_egress` is not validated against the vocabulary. `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/profiles.rs:9914` passes `"public"`, which is not an ADR-018 class; `position()` returns `None`, every row is ineligible and the caller gets `unresolvable_now`. Fail-closed, but a typo is indistinguishable from an absence.
- Owns: deciding whether the egress comparison is a bound or a capability, whether ADR-018 is amended or the code is, and what an out-of-vocabulary requirement should answer.
- Acceptance: a control observes a caller requiring `listed` being served a pack declaring `any` — RED before the repair; the decision names which of the two documents moved and why; ADR-018 is superseded or amended in the same commit if it is the one that moved; an out-of-vocabulary required class is answered by name rather than by an empty result; and the resolver suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0269.
- 🔴 **REPRODUCED AT RUNTIME, on two resolvers differing in ONE field.** `an_egress_bound_excludes_a_pack_that_declares_a_wider_one` registers `rsv-egress-listed` and `rsv-egress-any` on one scheme, identical but for `egress_class`, and asks for at most `listed`. Before the repair: `{"resolvers":["rsv-egress-listed","rsv-egress-any"],"unresolvable_now":false}` — `left: [rsv-egress-listed, rsv-egress-any]`, `right: [rsv-egress-listed]`. ⭐ One field differs, so nothing else can explain the outcome.
- 🔴 **THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE TEST WRITTEN FOR TWO LADDERS THAT RUN IN OPPOSITE SAFETY DIRECTIONS.** `declared >= required` is a floor. The sandbox ladder goes up towards more ISOLATION, so a floor is right. The egress ladder goes up towards more REACH, so the same test admitted a pack that reaches further than the caller permitted. ⭐ **The comment above it quoted ADR-018's *the claim is the MAXIMUM* and drew the opposite conclusion in the same sentence** — *"so a resolver claiming LESS than required is ineligible"*, when under a maximum claim a resolver claiming less is claiming to be more constrained.
- **Measured over the whole 4 × 6 matrix before anything changed:** the egress filter refused exactly **one combination of 24**, and it refused the wrong one. Asking for `any` — the widest class — was the only way to narrow the field, and it narrowed it to `rx-agent-mediated`, the single pack declaring no bound.
- ✅ **The decision: the CODE moved, ADR-018 stands unchanged.** `egress` is now `declared <= required`. ⚠️ The code was internally consistent, so this is a decision and not an obvious inversion: the shipped default `required_egress: "loopback"` only makes sense under the capability reading, because under the ceiling reading no pack would ever be eligible. It moved because **a capability floor over a maximum claim is incoherent** — it asks a promise-not-to-exceed to behave like a promise-to-reach, and it cannot express any isolation requirement at all, which is what ADR-018 says the classes are for.
- ✅ **The default becomes `any`, and the BEHAVIOUR is unchanged.** Under the old floor test `loopback` admitted every pack (all declare `listed` or `any`); under the ceiling test `any` admits every pack. Nothing a caller sees changed — the word now says what it does. ⛔ Whether the default SHOULD be permissive is a separate decision this leaf does not take.
- ✅ **An off-ladder required class is refused by name.** `position()` returned `None`, every row became ineligible, and the caller got `unresolvable_now` — fail-closed and silent about which. Now `invalid_command`, and ⛔ validated AFTER the tenant binding deliberately: checking the body first would answer 400 for a resource the caller may not know exists, re-opening the existence oracle `.11.14.3.4` closed.
- ⚠️ **ONE EXISTING TEST CHANGED, and it is recorded rather than quietly edited.** The RX resolution test passed `required_egress: "listed"` and expected `["rx-agent-mediated"]` — which is the defect seen from the suite's own side. It now passes `"any"`, because RX declares `any` and a caller permitting at most `listed` must not be handed it. The reason is written into the test beside the line. 🔎 `.7.3.6.5` may find RX's `any` to be a MISDESCRIPTION (the pack performs no egress at all), in which case that line changes again for a different reason.
- ⭐ **Three arms beyond the bound, so the repair is a filter and not a blackout:** permitting `any` still admits both packs; a bound no pack meets is the explicit `unresolvable_now` with the reference preserved; and the off-ladder class is named.
- ⚠️ **Recorded, not repaired:** `required_sandbox` defaults to `process`, which excludes the four packs declaring `none` — including R0. Every test passes `"none"` explicitly, so the documented default of the resolve verb resolves nothing for the flagship pack. Fail-closed and therefore safe; it is a default-policy question, not a comparison one, and this leaf owns the comparison.
- Verification: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **`test result: ok. 59 passed; 0 failed`** in 13.09 s. RED before: `58 passed; 1 failed`. `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `mdbook build docs/book` + `check_book_links.sh` rc=0.
- promotion: declined for a new knowledge note — the transferable sentence is the decision record's own title, and the mechanism is a second instance of `[[a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason]]`'s family seen in a filter rather than a control: one predicate serving two populations that disagree about which direction is safe.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_the-egress-claim-is-a-ceiling-the-sandbox-claim-is-a-floor.md`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0269 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.4): the egress claim is a ceiling, the sandbox claim is a floor`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.5 — The terms with no stated meaning, defined where a caller reads them or corrected

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`. The census returned **7 `undefined`** and **7 `misdescribed`** lines; this leaf owns both classes, because the same act settles them — deciding what the word is supposed to mean.
- **`undefined` (7):** `archive_policy` on all six packs, defined nowhere in the repository; and `javascript_policy: "allow-bounded"` on R3, where nothing states what *bounded* means and no control asserts any bound. ⚠️ `.7.3.5` made the R3 line MORE ambiguous, not less: inline script still runs while external script subresources are now denied.
- **`misdescribed` (7):** `egress_class: "listed"` on R0/R1/R2/R3/R5 — no list is consulted anywhere; the mechanism is a destination CLASSIFIER (public-only), and ADR-018's vocabulary has no class for *bounded by classification*. `egress_class: "any"` on RX, a pack that performs no egress at all. And **`sandbox_level: "vm_container"` on R3 — G4's open strand**: the worker is an ordinary child process in an owned process group, and `security_evidence` emits `"container_required": true`, a requirement ON THE DEPLOYMENT published as a property of the product.
- ⚠️ **Do NOT assume the answer is "enforce them".** At least `sandbox_level` may be honestly corrected rather than implemented, and `archive_policy` may be a field that should not exist. That is a decision this leaf owns rather than a repair it performs.
- Owns: defining each term in the book where a caller reads it, or correcting the advertisement and recording why the word was wrong rather than the code — per line, with the census re-run to show the verdict moved.
- Acceptance: no line is left `undefined` or `misdescribed`; each definition lands in `docs/book/` where a caller choosing a pack reads it; each correction records why the advertisement was wrong; `.doctrine/advertised_policy_verdicts.tsv` carries the new verdict with its evidence; and G4's open strand is named as discharged or still open, explicitly.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0270.
- ✅ **ALL 36 LINES NOW CARRY A DEFINED VERDICT: `enforced` 6 · `unverified` 9 · `vacuous` 21 — `undefined` 0, `misdescribed` 0.** Thirteen of the fourteen were settled by DEFINING a term; exactly one advertisement was corrected.
- 🔴 **G4'S OPEN STRAND IS DISCHARGED, by correcting the advertisement rather than building a container — and the reproduction is the sharpest of the four children.** The R3 pack advertised `sandbox_level: "vm_container"`, the TOP of the ADR-018 ladder, while `reasonbraid-browse` spawns an ordinary child process in an owned process group — rung one. A caller requiring `vm_container` was served it: **`{"resolvers":["r3-browser-worker"],"unresolvable_now":false}`**. ⛔ That is the silent downgrade ADR-018's exit clause exists to prevent, performed by the one pack that executes untrusted JavaScript.
- ⭐ **NOTHING HAD EVER REQUIRED `vm_container`, and that is why the claim survived.** `git grep vm_container` over `crates/` returns the ladder constant, one SDK vocabulary test and the advertisement itself — no caller, no control. **A rung nobody stands on holds any weight you like.** ⛔ Correcting it therefore broke no test: every strict-sandbox caller in the suite expects either a test-registered resolver that declares its own level or `unresolvable_now`, and the R3 resolution test asks for `none`.
- ⚠️ **`security_evidence`'s `container_required: true` STAYS, and is now consistent rather than contradictory.** The level says what the CODE provides; that key says what the DEPLOYMENT must add to reach the intended posture. The defect was one field claiming the other's content, not the existence of either.
- ⭐ **`archive_policy` WAS DEFINED, NOT CORRECTED, and the definition dissolves the apparent self-contradiction.** `ROADMAP.md` §16 lists the resolver policies as *"…decompression, **archive-depth**, and total-work"* — depth is the axis. So `deny` = the pack does not expand an archive NESTED inside the container it acquired. R2 therefore expands the zip or tar it was GIVEN — its own advertised media types — and refuses one inside it by name (`nested_archive`, `reasonbraid-extract/src/main.rs:342` and `:415`, asserted `:782`). 🔴 The `.7.3.6.1` census called this line *the sharpest instance* of a contradiction; it was the sharpest instance of an **undefined term**, and the two look identical until the term is pinned.
- ⭐ **`egress_class: "listed"` WAS DEFINED, and migration `0025`'s own comment had already said it**: *"the §12.4 public-only destination CLASSES ARE the list the `.2.1` classifier enforces"*. A list of destination classes, not of hosts. The word was not wrong; it was undocumented, and a definition sitting in a migration comment is not a definition a caller can read.
- ⭐ **`javascript_policy: "allow-bounded"` WAS DEFINED FROM THE PRODUCER, by enumerating what actually bounds execution:** external script subresources refused at the CDP `Fetch` domain (`.7.3.5`); a wall-clock budget and a step budget (`BrowseLimits`); a private per-render browser profile, discarded; and no credential of any kind reaching the browser (0 matches for `credential|cookie|Authorization` across the crate). Four bounds, each with a mechanism.
- ⚠️ **ONE VERDICT OF `.7.3.6.1`'s IS CORRECTED, and it was mine.** RX's `egress_class: "any"` was graded `misdescribed` because the pack performs no egress in-product. That judged the wrong granularity: the class is the MAXIMUM of the **acquisition the pack delivers**, and an enrolled agent's reach is genuinely unbounded, so `any` is the honest ceiling. Re-graded `vacuous` — nothing can violate `any`. ⭐ `.7.3.6.4` is what gives it teeth: a caller must now permit `any` to be served this pack.
- 🔎 **A live-document drift found and repaired on the way, and it is the standing corpus rule's own shape.** `docs/book/src/blockers.md` said C2 is CLOSED with all five gate records re-derived; `docs/book/src/qualification-review.md`, two pages of the same book, still said *"The first is done"* and *"Until the remaining four records are re-derived"*. REPAIR-0265 closed C2 and swept the blockers page but not this one. Both passages corrected here. ⛔ Not opened as a leaf: it is repaired in this commit, which is what `§15` asks for.
- ⛔ **NOT CLAIMED: that G4 is now Met.** What closes is the last un-discharged strand of its re-derivation (`.11.4.7.4`). The record's verdict — *G4 must be re-earned* — is unchanged by this leaf, and re-earning it is not this leaf's work.
- Verification: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **`test result: ok. 60 passed; 0 failed`** in 13.24 s. RED before: `59 passed; 1 failed`, with the body above. `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --check` rc=0, `--self-test` 26/26. `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make gate` green; `mdbook build docs/book` + `check_book_links.sh` rc=0.

- ⛔ `R-73-74-3`'s framing is preserved because it is the stronger claim: the deployment fixture USES the fabricated form, so the bypass is exercised by the suite meant to qualify it — this is proved, not merely absent.

The cost merely made the case unmissable. Re-derive with `time python3 -B scripts/project_env.py cargo check -p reasonbraid-server --tests` on an idle machine before quoting a build cost anywhere.

The note above was RIGHT and this bullet's "not the >10 minutes" is wrong: run 1 of the interval took 627 s. ⬇️ Preserved verbatim so the overstatement stays visible.
- ✅ **RE-MEASURED by REPAIR-0190, as that note asked, and the answer is 2 m 39 s.** `time python3 -B scripts/project_env.py cargo check -p reasonbraid-server --tests` -> `Finished ... in 2m 38s`, `real 2m39.014s`, rc=0, with the tree unchanged and no other build on the machine (`ps -eo pid,etime,time,command | grep -E "cargo|rustc"` listed only this one). ⛔ The two numbers answer DIFFERENT questions rather than contradicting each other, which is what the original note predicted: it measured a contended machine with a cold cache, this measured an uncontended one with a warm one. **"Ten minutes" is not a property of the crate**, and no decision should rest on it.

- 🔴 **AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT FOUND THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, which is not CPU contention at all.** The first attempt STALLED: `rustc` sat at **3.84 s of CPU across 6 minutes** in state `S`, with `dep-graph.part.bin` byte-identical across a 20 s window and all four threads asleep — blocked, not slow. `taskpolicy -B -p <pid>` changed nothing, `sample` could not even attach (rc=124 at a 60 s timeout), and a machine-wide census found no competing build. ##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1.1 — The publish verb takes its repository location from the request body

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1`'s decomposition.
- Reproduce, at the source: `api.rs::publish_publication` reads `repo_path` straight from the request body and hands it to `publisher::publish`, which calls `gix::open(repo_path)`. Any enrolled principal names any path on the server's filesystem. ⚠️ It COMPOSES with `R-52-2` clause 7: the module doc says *"into the LOCAL bare repository"* and `gix::open` accepts a non-bare one.
- Owns: a publication repository ROOT as server configuration (`rb-server` argument + `ApiState`), the request's `repo_path` resolved strictly INSIDE it, and a typed refusal for anything outside — including via `..` and via a symlink, which are different escapes and must be tested separately.
- ⚠️ **Fail-closed is part of the contract, not a detail:** with NO root configured the verb refuses. `api_router(pool)` keeps its signature — 34 call sites across 34 files — and the root arrives through a new seam beside `api_router_gated` and `api_router_with_acquisition`, which is the established shape here.
- ⚠️ `.11.12` owns `rb-server`'s boot ORDER. This leaf adds an argument and its validation; it must place that refusal BEFORE any mutation (so it does not deepen `.11.12`'s finding) and must NOT decide `.11.12`'s two questions — the secret-store ordering and the `--host` gate.
- Acceptance: three controls, each observed RED first — a request whose `repo_path` escapes the configured root via `..` is refused with a typed error; one that escapes via a SYMLINK inside the root is refused; and a server with no configured root refuses the verb outright. The existing publish test is re-pointed at the configured root rather than deleted.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0190.
- **The fix.** `publisher::validate_root` + `publisher::resolve_repository` are ONE definition of "inside the declared root", called at BOOT by `rb-server --publication-repo-root` and again per request by the verb, so the two cannot drift into disagreeing. Both sides are CANONICALIZED before they are compared, which is what lets one question answer two different escapes: `..` is a walk the caller spells and a symlink is one the filesystem spells on the caller's behalf, and every component of the symlink case IS inside the root — so a string containment test refuses the first and admits the second. `ApiState` gains the root, `api_router_with_publication_root` is the new seam beside `api_router_gated`/`api_router_with_acquisition`, and `api_router(pool)` keeps its signature and declares NO root, which closes the verb rather than leaving it open.
- **`api_router`'s caller census, corrected.** This leaf's own text said "34 call sites across 34 files". Re-derived with `git grep -n "api_router(" -- ':(glob)crates/**/*.rs'`, minus the definition and the `lib.rs` re-export, it was **33 across 33** before this repair and is **32 across 32** after, because `rb-server` now calls the seam. ⛔ The number is not carried into the source comment: it names the command instead (`docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §5B).

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1.1.1 — The build-cost finding REPAIR-0190 published does not survive its own grading

- Opened: `pending` by the director's challenge on 2026-09-15 — *"make sure the findings have legs"* — which is `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §4.1's grading event, and the answer is that one of them does not.
- **Graded on all three axes SEPARATELY, as §4.1 requires.**
  - **PROSE — FAILS.** REPAIR-0190 published *"this build is I/O-bound against the external repository volume"* and *"the mechanism is not CPU contention at all"*. Neither is established.
  - **NUMBER — one FAILS.** *"about 9 % CPU utilisation"* is true of the lib-only arm and false of the `--tests` arm by a factor of **22**.
  - **NAMED INSTANCE — FAILS, and that axis has no tolerance band.** *"The completed runs say the same thing without any drama"* is false: the two arms disagree by more than an order of magnitude, and they were published adjacent as if they agreed.
- **The arithmetic, which is all it took and which I did not do before publishing.** `--tests`: 159.0 s wall, 46.5 s user, 282.8 s sys -> **207 %** of one core. Lib-only: 181.7 s wall, 5.8 s user, 11.3 s sys -> **9 %**. The clippy arm: 158.7 s wall, 47.1 s user, 267.7 s sys -> **198 %**. ⛔ Two of the three arms are not idle at all — they are burning **kernel** CPU across several cores, which is the opposite of a process blocked on a slow volume.
- 🔴 **THE REAL FAILURE IS LEG 2, AND `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` NAMES IT EXACTLY**: *"the cheapest oracle is your own project's history — before publishing a finding, check whether a case of the same shape has already been adjudicated; if you cannot name a difference, the earlier ruling wins."* `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_checkpoint-cost-model.md` had already adjudicated *"a process blocked on this volume with near-zero CPU"*: macOS first-execution validation, **~21.9 s per newly-written executable against 0.15 s on the boot volume**, cached per file identity, `user 0.00 sys 0.00` throughout, with `syspolicyd` named. I observed `syspolicyd` at 74 % and published a COMPETING mechanism without reading the ruling that already explained the signature.
- Owns: withdrawing the unearned claim at every site that carries it; deferring to the existing ruling or naming a difference with evidence; giving the one surviving number its three legs; and closing the leg-3 gap that let a hand-divided ratio be published at all.
- ⛔ **The surviving claim is narrow and is the only thing `.9.2.1`'s note actually asked for**: `cargo check -p reasonbraid-server --tests` completes in about 2 m 39 s, not the ">10 minutes" recorded. That stands, and it is what the re-measurement was for.
- Acceptance: the five publication sites carry the correction rather than the claim; the deferral to the cost-model ruling is stated with the arithmetic that makes the stall consistent with it, or a difference is named and evidenced; the surviving number is re-derived as an INTERVAL rather than a point estimate; and `scripts/measure_check_phases.py` records user/sys/CPU per phase so the ratio comes from the instrument instead of from a reader's division.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-DOC-0018.
- 🔴 **RE-DERIVED AS AN INTERVAL, AND THE INTERVAL REFUTES MY CORRECTION AS WELL AS MY MECHANISM.** Three runs of the same command, each doing the same work (the crate root is touched between runs so none is a no-op), with the ratio computed by `measure_check_phases.cpu_percent` rather than by hand:

| run | wall | user | sys | cpu % |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (coldest) | **627.0 s** | 49.7 s | 290.3 s | **54.2 %** |
| 2 | 148.9 s | 37.1 s | 287.4 s | **217.9 %** |
| 3 | 140.7 s | 34.7 s | 274.3 s | **219.7 %** |

- ⛔ **The CPU work is CONSTANT and the wall clock is not.** Total CPU per run: 340.0 s, 324.5 s, 309.0 s — a spread of **31 s**. Wall clock: **140.7 s to 627.0 s, a factor of 4.5**. The build does the same work every time; what changes is how long it waits to do it. At run 2–3's ~2.2 cores, run 1 spent about **472 s not computing**.
- 🔴 **RUN 1 EXCEEDS TEN MINUTES, so `.9.2.1`'s original note was RIGHT and my "correction" of it was wrong.** It recorded ">10 minutes" and a kill at ~35 minutes under measured contention; I contradicted it from **one warm run** and published 2 m 39 s as the answer. Both numbers are true, of different cache states, and neither is "the" build cost. ⛔ `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md`'s stochastic rider is the rule I broke: a point estimate for a quantity whose own spread is 4.5× reads as precision and is luck.
- **What survives, stated with its conditions instead of as a fact about the crate:** on a WARM page cache `cargo check -p reasonbraid-server --tests` completes in **141–149 s at ~218 % CPU** (≈2.2 cores, overwhelmingly kernel); on a COLD one the same work takes **627 s at 54 %**. ##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1.2 — Both publish verbs are authorized by enrolment alone

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1`'s decomposition.
- Reproduce, at the source: `publish_publication` and `mark_publication_effective` each check `reader_tenant(…).is_some()` and nothing else. Enrolment in ANY tenant is the whole predicate for writing a publication into a Git repository and for declaring it effective.
- Owns: binding both verbs to an explicitly held grant, in the shape this codebase already uses — `deployments::register_target` takes an `owning_authority` from the caller and requires `authority::grant_held_by(pool, grant_id, principal)`. ⛔ That is THE predicate (`MEMORY.md`, `.9.3.1`); never a sixth spelling.
- ⚠️ **A known limit this leaf must RECORD rather than pretend to fix:** `.9.3.4` measured that no `GrantAction` and no `TargetSelector` can NAME a publication, so a held grant is effectively tenant-wide for this verb. Binding to a held grant is strictly stronger than enrolment and is the best the vocabulary expresses today; the narrowing belongs to `.9.3.4`. Say so in the leaf and in the book rather than implying the verb is narrowly scoped.
- ⚠️ This CHANGES THE WIRE CONTRACT of two shipped verbs (a new required field). The book and every fixture that drives them move with it.
- Acceptance: a control observed RED first in which an enrolled principal holding NO grant is refused by both verbs, and a holder succeeds; a grant that exists but is held by SOMEONE ELSE is also refused, because "names a grant" and "holds a grant" are the two things `.9.3.1` found conflated.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0192.
- **The fix.** `api::held_publication_authority` — ONE definition both verbs call, reading `owning_authority` from the body and deciding with `authority::grant_held_by`, which is `deployments::register_target`'s shape and `.9.3.1`'s predicate. ⛔ Not a sixth spelling: the two verbs share no core to put the check in, so the shared thing IS this function, and a later change cannot move one verb without the other. It runs BEFORE the path is resolved and before the publication is loaded, so an unauthorized caller reaches neither the filesystem nor the database.
- ⚠️ **THE LIMIT IS RECORDED, NOT PAPERED OVER** (`.9.3.4`): no `GrantAction` and no `TargetSelector` can NAME a publication, so a held grant is effectively TENANT-WIDE for these verbs. Holding is strictly stronger than enrolment and is the best today's vocabulary expresses; the narrowing belongs to `.9.3.4`. The book says so in its own words — "do not read the refusal as meaning a caller is confined to a particular publication" — rather than implying the verb is narrowly scoped.
- **The wire change's blast radius was MEASURED, not assumed.** `git grep -rn "policy-publications" -- ':(glob)crates/**' ':(glob)docs/**' ':(glob)scripts/**' ':(glob)deploy/**'` returns the route registrations, the handler docs, `rb-server`'s argument help, two book lines and the phase records — and **no client outside `tests/policy.rs`**. Neither the CLI nor the MCP surface drives these verbs, so the contract change moves the book and one test file.
- ⭐ **THE MATCHED PAIR IS WHAT MAKES LEG B MEAN ANYTHING**, and it is the method this session promoted (`docs/knowledge/a-falsification-you-can-leave-behind.md`): the same request, the same verb, everything identical except WHOSE grant is named, is admitted. Grant ids are derivable (`grt_<principal_id>`), which is why "names an active grant" would have been no check at all — the exact conflation `.9.3.1` found on three other surfaces, and the reason this leaf's acceptance asked for the someone-else's-grant leg specifically.
- ⛔ **The positive arm is a real SUCCESS on one verb and an ADMISSION on the other, and the difference is stated rather than smoothed over.** `effective` completes (200, state `effective`) for the holder. `publish` is admitted and then stopped by the projection the seeded row names, which does not exist — a LATER refusal, asserted to be `invalid_command` and NOT to carry the authority message, which is what proves the gate let it through. Driving `publish` to a real 200 needs the whole proposal → decision → approval → projection chain, which `the_publish_verb_drives_the_git_half` already owns end to end.
- **Every fixture that drives either verb now carries a held authority**, because otherwise they would all be refused before reaching what they measure — including `.9.2.1.1`'s containment control, which would have stopped measuring containment entirely.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1.3 — `mark_effective` records Git object ids it never looks for

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1`'s decomposition.
- Reproduce, at the source: `publications::mark_effective` takes `git_object_ids: Vec<String>`, refuses only the EMPTY list, and writes them into the row. Nothing opens a repository. The parent's goal line already says *"reject fabricated effective Git IDs"*, verbatim.
- ⛔ **The bypass is EXERCISED by the suite meant to qualify it**, which is the stronger claim and the reason `R-73-74-3`'s framing is preserved: `git grep -n '"git_object_ids": \["abc123"' crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/policy.rs` returns **3** sites, one of them the deployment fixture. The suite proves the transition works using ids that do not exist.
- Owns: verifying every declared object EXISTS in the configured repository before the publication is marked effective, and RE-SEEDING those fixtures with real objects. ⛔ `MEMORY.md`: never delete a fixture that depends on a defect — re-seed it, so the test still asserts the transition and now asserts it honestly.
- ⚠️ Depends on `.1`: the verification needs a repository, and the route currently takes no path. It must read the CONFIGURED root, not a caller-supplied one — otherwise the check is satisfiable by pointing at a repository the caller prepared.
- Acceptance: a control observed RED first in which `mark_publication_effective` with an id that resolves to nothing is refused with a typed error; the three fixture sites carry ids read back from a real repository; and the existing empty-list and wrong-stage refusals still hold.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0191.
- **The design question the leaf left open, decided and recorded rather than assumed.** `policy_publications` has **no repository column** (`migrations/0042_policy_publications.sql`), so `mark_effective` had no way to know which repository a declared id was claimed to live in. Three sources were available: the caller, the configured root treated as the repository itself, or a new column recording where `publish` wrote. ⭐ The caller was chosen, CONSTRAINED BY `.9.2.1.1`'s predicate, because it is the only one that works for both of the verb's uses: the standalone `effective` verb exists for a Git half performed out of band, where no column could have been filled, and `.9.2.1.1` had already shaped the root as a CONTAINER of repositories rather than as one. ⚠️ **This is a WIRE-CONTRACT CHANGE to a shipped verb** — `repo_path` is now required on `POST /v1/policy-publications/{id}/effective` — and the book moves with it.
- **The fix, and where it lives.** `publisher::missing_objects` answers which declared ids name nothing, and `publications::mark_effective` calls it. ⛔ The check is in the CORE rather than in either handler: `git grep -n "publications::mark_effective" f3d77c9 -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src` returns **2 production callers**, both in `api.rs`, so a handler-level repair would have left the sibling open and its own suite green (`.6.1.2`'s rule, applied rather than re-derived). ⭐ And the containment guarantee is made STRUCTURAL: `resolve_repository` now returns a `PublicationRepository` newtype with no other constructor, so a verb taking one cannot be reached with a path that has not passed containment — a convention a later caller could forget became a type they cannot.
- ⛔ **An unparseable id and a well-formed absent one are the SAME answer, and both are asserted.** A check that validated only the SHAPE would refuse `abc123` and accept forty zeros, recording a claim about an object that is not there. ⚠️ And a repository that fails to open is a DEPLOYMENT fault (`RepositoryUnreadable`), deliberately not collapsed into "the ids are missing" — an unreadable store must not read as a forged publication.
- ⛔ **The check is PER-ID, not per-request**, and the live control pins it: one real id beside one fabricated id is refused, and the message names only the fabricated one. "Does any declared id resolve" would have let a real id launder a forged one beside it.
- **The three fixtures are RE-SEEDED, not relaxed** (`MEMORY.md`: never delete a fixture that depends on a defect). `seeded_publication_repository` writes real blobs into a bare repository under the test's own configured root and hands back the ids; each fixture asserts the same transition it always did, and now asserts it honestly.
- 🔴 **I mapped one of the three sites to the wrong test, and the COMPILER was the oracle that caught it.** The third `abc123` site is in `the_drift_corrections_and_outcomes_ride_the_records`, not `the_scheduled_reviews_evaluate_the_triggers`; the reviews test never drives the transition at all. Seeding the wrong function produced `cannot find value \`object_ids\`` and `unused variable: \`object_ids\`` in one build — two errors that together name both halves of the mistake. ⚠️ A line number inside a 3,600-line file is not a location; the enclosing function is, and I had not asked for it.
- **RED first, measured on both sides rather than asserted.** At `f3d77c9` — the commit before this repair — `git grep -n '"git_object_ids": \["abc123"' f3d77c9 -- crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/policy.rs` returns **3 sites**, and that suite was GREEN: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh policy` at that commit returned `13 passed; 0 failed`. So the transition accepted ids that resolve to nothing, at three sites, in a suite whose job was to qualify it. The same body now returns **400** naming the missing ids — one input, two commits, opposite answers.
- ⚠️ **A limit stated rather than implied:** the check proves each declared object EXISTS in the named repository. It does NOT prove the object is the publication's own — a sibling repository inside the configured root that happens to hold a matching id would satisfy it. Binding the ids to the publication's refs needs the repository recorded with the publication, which is a migration and a different leaf; it is not smuggled in here.
- Verification: `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/policy.rs::the_publication_stages_and_marks_its_typed_state` (the fabricated-id and per-id legs) and `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/publisher.rs::a_declared_object_id_must_exist_in_the_repository` (4 arms). `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh policy` -> `13 passed; 0 failed`, rc=0; `cargo test -p reasonbraid-server --test publisher` -> `7 passed; 0 failed`, rc=0.

- Status: `active`; censused and SPLIT below into `.9.3.1`–`.9.3.3`, because `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.3.1` measured concrete live defects against three of its five mechanisms and a single leaf would have to qualify all of them at once. ⛔ `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.13`'s ownership repair.

  1. **The canary wave is a number nothing sequences on** (`R-40-42-5` clause 5). `deployments.rs` stores `wave` as a bare `i64` and no path orders execution by it, so the record's own phrase — "records-only honesty" — is the accurate description of today's contract. ⛔ No part of this goal line names waves or rollout ordering, so a census driven by it reads the column as satisfied by being stored. - ⭐ **ATTACHED CLAUSE — a routed-record finding this leaf's goal line does NOT make visible** (`R-33-35-1` clause 2, tranche 4c; same ledger). 🔴 **`deployments::assign` takes no principal, no tenant and no authority field, and the contrast is inside ONE module.** `register_target` calls `crate::authority::grant_held_by(pool, &input.owning_authority, principal)` — this tree's own predicate, put there by `.9.3.1` — while `assign(pool, input)`, the verb that points a deployment target at a publication, has no such parameter and `AssignmentInput` carries no `owning_authority` at all. `record_receipt` is the same shape. ⛔ The goal line's "validate receipts and corrective authority" reads as covering this and does not: a receipt's VALIDITY is not who may record one, and `assign` is neither a receipt nor a correction. ⚠️ `.9.3.1` named `deployments.rs` and repaired the site that HAD an authority field; the sites with no field are a wire-contract change, which is why they are attached here rather than absorbed there.

Neither side of the waiver path consults an expiry: `corrections::record_correction` requires `expires_at` to be present and RFC3339-parseable and never compares it to `now()`, and `reviews::schedule_reviews` selects `WHERE operation = 'waiver'` with no expiry predicate. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.3.1 — Citing an authority is the same as holding one

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.13`'s ownership repair.
- Reproduce, at the source: `corrections.rs::authority_holds(pool, grant_id)` takes the grant ID **and nothing else**, and asks only `SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM authority_grants WHERE grant_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()))`. It never receives the caller, the action, the selector, the boundary, the publication, or `valid_from`. `record_policy_correction` above it admits on ENROLMENT alone.
- ⛔ So any enrolled principal who can name any active grant records a suspension, a retraction or a waiver in its name. ⭐ The module's own error type for a missing grant is already called `GhostAuthority` — the concept is present and the check is not.
- `deployments.rs` repeats the shape for `owning_authority`, so the repair must cover both or it will be half a repair.
- Owns: binding the cited authority to the authenticated caller AND to the target's action, scope and boundary, on both call sites; and honouring `valid_from` alongside `expires_at`.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0184.
- 🔴 **THE CENSUS FOUND A THIRD CALL SITE AND A WIDER DEFECT THAN THE LEAF NAMED.** `git grep -n "FROM authority_grants" aee579a -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src/` (pinned to the pre-repair commit, because this repair CHANGED the population) returns **9 sites**, of which **5 ask the grant-validity question** — `corrections`, `deployments`, `lifecycle` and `policy` twice — **in four different spellings**; the other 4 ask different questions. ⛔ The population number was first taken with `src/*.rs`, a glob that does NOT recurse, and it missed `src/authority/selection.rs`. `policy::register` checked `status` alone; `policy::resolve`, `corrections::authority_holds` and `deployments::register_target` added expiry; `lifecycle::record_approval` added expiry AND a subject match. ⛔ **`git grep -n "valid_from"` over those four modules returns rc=1 — NOT ONE of the five consulted it**, though the column is `NOT NULL`, so a grant that had not begun was as good as a live one everywhere. ⭐ And the odd-one-out rule from `docs/knowledge/a-signature-is-a-promise-the-body-must-keep` paid again: the ONE site that bound a subject is the one that had had the attention — and it was still half-bound, matching the grant to `input.approver`, **a string off the wire that nothing tied to the caller**. So a caller could approve AS another principal by naming their grant, which is derivable (`grt_<principal_id>`). That is a THIRD instance of this leaf's own mechanism, named by no leaf, and repairing two of three would have been the "half a repair" this leaf warns about.
- ⛔ **`expires_at IS NULL` was dead in four of the five predicates**: `migrations/0004_authority.sql` declares the column `NOT NULL`. The shared predicate does not reproduce it — carrying it forward would keep teaching the next reader that the column is optional.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.3.4 — An administrative authority cannot name what it is authority OVER

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.3.1`, whose third acceptance leg asked for something the vocabulary cannot express.
- Measured, not asserted: `GrantAction` has ten variants — nine thread-shaped plus `TenantAdmin` — and `TargetSelector` is `TenantWide | Threads { threads }`. `git grep -n "Publication\|DeploymentTarget\|Correction" -- crates/reasonbraid-core/src/authority.rs` returns **rc=1**.
- So for the administrative surfaces — recording a correction, registering a deployment target, approving a policy — a grant can be bound to its HOLDER (which `.9.3.1` did) but not to its SCOPE: there is no action meaning "may retract a publication" and no selector that can name one. Every such grant is effectively tenant-wide for these verbs.
- ⛔ Do NOT read this as "the administrative surfaces are unauthorized". After `.9.3.1` each requires a live grant HELD BY the caller; what is missing is the narrower question of WHICH publications that authority covers.
- Owns: the decision whether `GrantAction` and `TargetSelector` gain administrative members — and if so, which, since both are closed wire vocabularies and §9.8 publishes a stable registry — and then the coverage checks at the three sites.
- ⚠️ Coordinate with `.11.7.1`, which holds the open question of how the roadmap's published code registry absorbs post-roadmap additions. A new `GrantAction` wire name is the same class of change.
- Acceptance: a decision record naming whether the vocabularies extend and why, with the current variants enumerated by command; and if they do, the new members plus a coverage check at each of the three sites, each control observed RED first.
- Status: `active`; the DECISION is taken and recorded (`docs/decisions/2026-09-15_the-action-set-extends-the-target-selector-does-not.md`, REASONBRAID-DOC-0020), and the implementation is DECOMPOSED into `.1` and `.2` below, each with its own acceptance and its own RED-first control.
- **The decision: `GrantAction` EXTENDS with administrative verbs, `TargetSelector` does NOT, and the extension is a MIGRATION rather than an addition.**
- 🔴 **THIS LEAF'S OWN PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND IT IS THE PREMISE THAT WOULD HAVE DECLINED THE EXTENSION.** The line above says both are "closed wire vocabularies and §9.8 publishes a stable registry" and reads across to `.11.7.1`'s frozen-roadmap hold. §9.8 is the **reason-code** registry — a different vocabulary. `git grep -c "GrantAction\|TargetSelector" ROADMAP.md` returns **0**. The freeze does not reach these types and `.11.7.1` is not a prerequisite; the coupling between the two leaves was the false premise and is dissolved.
- ⭐ **And the project had ALREADY RULED on how to do it**, which the leaf did not consult: `docs/decisions/2026-09-06_authority-boundary.md`, *How to apply* — *"Add an action/ceiling by extending the checker FIRST — a grant that exceeds the boundary must be unrepresentable, not merely unapproved."* So the extension is prescribed, with an ordering constraint the children inherit.
- ⛔ **THE SITE CENSUS IN THIS LEAF WAS STALE AND THIS SESSION IS WHAT STALED IT.** It says "the three sites". Re-derived 2026-09-15: `git grep -n "grant_held_by(\|grant_is_live(" -- ':(glob)crates/reasonbraid-server/src/**'` returns **6** — four `grant_held_by` (`api.rs` serving BOTH publication verbs, `corrections`, `deployments`, `lifecycle`) and two `grant_is_live` (`policy.rs` ×2, a weaker question with the same scope gap). The fourth is `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1.2`'s, added in this session, so the number is pinned to the commit rather than refreshed silently (`MEMORY.md`).
- ⛔ **Why `TargetSelector` does not extend, measured rather than preferred:** `TargetSelector::Threads { threads: Vec<ThreadId> }` ENUMERATES its objects at grant time. That works for threads, which exist before anyone is authorized over them, and cannot work for the case that matters — the ordinary flow publishes a NEW publication whose id does not exist when the grant is issued. A `Publications { … }` variant would be unusable for exactly the operation it was added for. The residual is ACCEPTED and published: after `.1` and `.2`, a publication grant is narrowed by VERB and stays tenant-wide by OBJECT, and the book keeps saying so.
- 🔴 **Why it is a MIGRATION**, and this is the part that sizes the children: `migrations/0004_authority.sql:15` stores `permitted_actions` as a JSONB array of **GrantAction wire names**, so **no stored boundary contains a name that did not exist when it was written**. The moment a verb requires a new action, every already-enrolled tenant's boundary fails to permit it and that verb stops working for them. Fail-CLOSED, which is the safe direction, and still live breakage. ⚠️ `ADMIN_ACTIONS` (`api.rs`) is a hand-maintained list of **9 of the 10** variants — `ThreadCreateAuto` is already excluded — so the default set is a decision, not a default.
- ⚠️ **Not implemented in this commit, and said plainly rather than implied.** `git grep -n "GrantAction::" -- ':(glob)crates/**/*.rs'` returns **207 references across 19 files**, and the change is three things at once (the vocabulary, the default set, the stored-boundary disposition) with a live-breakage edge. It is decomposed for the same reason `.9.2.1` was by REPAIR-0189, and the children carry acceptance so this is ownership rather than routing (`.11.13`).
- Verification / commit: per child; the decision half is `REASONBRAID-DOC-0020`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.3.2 — A publication can be reviewed once, for ever

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.13`'s ownership repair.
- Reproduce, at the source: `reviews::schedule_reviews` builds `review_id = format!("rev_{publication_id}_{trigger}")` — deterministic — and `migrations/0045_policy_reviews.sql:12` makes `review_id` the PRIMARY KEY. The dedupe skips a pair whose review is still `due`; once it is `done` the skip no longer applies, the INSERT collides with the existing key, and **`if inserted.is_ok()`** discards the error. No second review for that pair can ever be scheduled.
- ⛔ The same `is_ok()` discards EVERY insert error, so a total storage failure returns `Ok(vec![])` — a successful empty schedule, indistinguishable from "nothing was due".
- ⛔ And the `repeated_waiver` trigger fires on the FIRST waiver — one row yields one pair — and on waivers that lapsed long ago, because neither `record_correction` nor `schedule_reviews` consults an expiry. Two records reached this independently (`R-75-1` clause 1 and `R-53-5` clause 1).
- Owns: an occurrence-scoped review identity, a real repeated-count threshold with a window, an expiry predicate on the waiver read, and an insert whose failure is reported rather than dropped.
- Acceptance: a second occurrence after a completed review schedules a NEW review; a single waiver does NOT satisfy `repeated_waiver` and the threshold is stated in the book; a lapsed waiver does not trigger; a forced insert failure surfaces as an error rather than an empty success. All observed RED first.
- ⚠️ `policy.rs`'s two hardcoded `expires_at` of `2026-09-15` must become relative clocks in the same commit (`.9.3`'s goal line: "use relative test clocks with failure visibility") — measured 2026-09-14 as NOT yet breaking, and they will the moment this leaf adds the expiry predicate.
- Verification / commit: pending.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.3.3 — A deployment's declared digest is bound to nothing it deploys

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.13`'s ownership repair.
- Reproduce, at the source: `deployments::assign` validates `is_sha256_hex(&input.desired_digest)` — the SHAPE — and compares it against no publication projection; `tests/policy.rs:2724` assigns `sha256:` followed by sixty-four `a`s with `desired_ref: "abc123"` and asserts 200. The receipt then overwrites the observed state from client-supplied data bound to no node, keeping no history, so a target reports `applied` carrying a digest the publication never had.
- ⚠️ The canary `wave` is a bare `i64` that nothing sequences on — recorded as the current contract rather than as a defect, and the leaf must decide whether the wave is a SEQUENCER or a LABEL and say which in the book.
- Owns: comparing the declared digest and ref against the publication's actual projection at assignment, binding the receipt to the reporting node, retaining what a receipt replaced, and settling the wave's meaning.
- Acceptance: an assignment whose digest is not the publication's projection is REFUSED; a receipt from a node the target does not name is refused; the prior observed state is recoverable after a receipt; and the existing fixture is re-seeded with the real projection digest rather than relaxed. Observed RED first.
- Verification / commit: pending.

- 🔴 **And the gate that exists for exactly this cannot see them.** `scripts/check_storage_locality.sh` enumerates its population with `git ls-files -z -- "*.rs"`. Its two patterns are `env::temp_dir()` and `subsec_nanos()`/`as_nanos()` — both Rust — so the shell family is outside the scan by construction, not by exception. `.doctrine/storage_locality_exceptions.txt` therefore does not list them either: they are invisible, not waived.
- ⭐ The project already knows the right shape, which is why this is a gap rather than a disagreement: `scripts/dev.sh:45` writes `mktemp -d "$ROOT/target/dev-ephemeral.XXXXXX"` and `scripts/check_book_frontier.sh:44` uses `target/doctrine_scratch`. The repair is to make the other four match, not to invent a convention.
- census, run before proposing anything (`TOOLBOX.md`): `git grep -nE 'mktemp|\{TMPDIR|tempfile\.(mkdtemp|TemporaryDirectory|NamedTemporary)|gettempdir' -- ':!*.rs' ':!*.md'` returns **19** sites across **19** files. **Classified, not published as a count** (`docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md`): the twelve Python sites all pass `dir=<a repository-derived parent>` to `tempfile`, which writes under that parent rather than under `TMPDIR`, so they CONFORM and were written deliberately. Two shell sites conform as above. The breaching set is the five named above. A raw count of 19 would have been a false positive of nearly four to one.
- Owns: moving the five onto repository-derived scratch with the same cleanup guarantees they have now, and deciding whether `STORAGE-LOCALITY`'s population should include tracked shell and Python.
- ⚠️ The second half is a rule proposal, so it carries the same obligation the first gate did: measure what an extended population would FIRE ON before registering it. The census above is that measurement's starting point and says the answer today would be five — a gate that fires on five and is fixed in the same commit, which is the shape `REASON-CODE-DOC` had and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9`'s rejected gate did not.
- ⛔ Do NOT widen the checker's file glob without also deciding what `dir=`-passing Python looks like to it. A pattern that flags `tempfile.mkdtemp(` unconditionally would flag twelve conforming sites and teach bypass, which is the failure mode `FILE-TERMINATION` avoided by refusing to wrap `git diff --check`.
- Acceptance: each of the five writes under a repository-derived path proved on this volume; the enforcer still passes and its own scratch is on-volume; the extension decision is recorded with its population measurement whichever way it goes.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0170.
- 🔴 **CORRECTION, and it is this leaf's own published number that was wrong: SEVEN sites, not five.** The opening census above ran `git grep … | grep -v '^docs/'`. That convenience filter excluded the directory holding the files the record names — and the record names them by ROLE, not by path, which is why reading it as "the guards" was possible at all. `R-84-1` says "tracked **task-acceptance and waiver-routing probe scripts** both `WORK=$(mktemp -d)`", and the files spelling `WORK=` verbatim are `docs/tasks/artifacts/task_acceptance/run_task_acceptance_probes.sh` line 22 and `docs/tasks/artifacts/waiver_routing/run_waiver_routing_probes.sh` line 33 — **both excluded by my own filter**. I had read "probe scripts" as the guards and repaired those, which the record also predicted ("guards themselves may mktemp similarly"); the guards were a correct find and not the ones it named first.
- ⚠️ **`MEMORY.md` carries this exact warning and I breached it anyway**: *"Scope a census to `crates/` WHOLE"*, recorded after `git grep -- 'crates/*/src'` silently matched nothing. A path filter that excludes a directory is the same defect as a glob that matches none — both make a census report a smaller world with no error. The number is corrected here rather than quietly used, and the superseded 5 is left in the line above, per `TOOLBOX.md`.
- **The corrected census, scoped to every tracked `*.sh` and `*.py` with no path filter:** 8 shell `mktemp` call sites and 14 Python `tempfile` call sites. **Classified**: 7 breaching (all shell), 14 conforming Python that pass a repository-derived `dir=`, 1 conforming shell (`dev.sh`, the idiom the repair copies), and 1 Python that is a deliberate CONTROL. All 7 are repaired; the Python control is a reviewed exception.
- ⭐ **The one Python hit is why a blanket pattern needs an allowlist.** `scripts/tests/test_ci_env.py` line 95 calls `tempfile.mkstemp()` with no `dir=` inside a string that is the SOURCE of a child probe program, in a test named `test_exec_uses_relocated_root_and_local_temporary_file`. Its entire purpose is to observe where the launcher makes a child's temporary file land; pinning `dir=` would assert the answer instead of measuring it. Recorded verbatim in `.doctrine/storage_locality_exceptions.txt`.
- **Locality PROVED, not assumed:** the checkout and `target/doctrine_scratch` both measure device `16777244`; the ambient directory measures `16777232`. A different volume, which is the same pair `STORAGE-LOCALITY` already records for `env::temp_dir()`.
- **DECISION: the gate IS extended to tracked `*.sh` and `*.py`**, on the measurement the leaf demanded. It fires on **0** today and would have fired on all **7** — the shape `REASON-CODE-DOC` had (0 today, 9 historically, registered) and the shape `.11.9`'s rejected gate did not (114 of 131). ⛔ The rule is about the ARGUMENT, not the call: `mktemp` and `tempfile` both name by exclusive creation, which is the half of this doctrine a clock gets wrong. A shell site breaches only when its template is not repository-derived; a Python site only when it passes no `dir=`. A pattern flagging the call itself would have condemned 15 conforming sites and taught bypass.
- ⚠️ **Shell and Python skip comments; Rust deliberately does not**, and the asymmetry is measured rather than stylistic: every repaired site carries a comment EXPLAINING the rule and naming the command, so a comment-sensitive shell rule flags its own documentation for ever. The Rust arm asserting that a commented `env::temp_dir()` still counts has been in this self-test since the gate shipped and is unchanged. Both directions are now asserted.
- 🔴 **And the gate flagged ITSELF on the first run — the `SELF-TEST` doctrine's founding incident, repeating in a file that carries a `--self-test` of its own and still could not see it.** Its diagnostic message spelled the command it matches, so the message was a breach. ⛔ Fixed by RE-WORDING rather than by excluding the file's path: `TOOLBOX.md` says to make the failure cheap when correctness depends on enumerating what to exclude, and a reworded message self-polices — spell the literal again and the whole-tree scan goes red on this file immediately. The self-test's own fixtures assemble the command from two halves for the same reason.
- Verification: `bash scripts/check_storage_locality.sh` -> `265 tracked Rust/shell/Python files keep their scratch on the repository volume and name it by creation (2 reviewed exception(s))`, rc=0. `--self-test` -> **22 classifications** across all three languages, rc=0 (8 before). ⭐ **FALSIFIED against the EXACT pre-repair sources** — `git checkout` the six files, re-run, and the gate names all **7** sites by file and line, rc=1; restored, rc=0. Both repaired probe scripts run: **10 pass / 0 fail** and **5 pass / 0 fail**, rc=0. The three repaired guards each run rc=0 and `check_self_tests.sh --self-test` passes with 21 scripts discovered. `make gate` 18 checks, `mdbook build` and both book checks rc=0.
- ⛔ NOT claimed: that every ambient-storage path in the repository is now closed. This gate sees `*.rs`, `*.sh` and `*.py`; a Makefile recipe, a CI workflow step or a Rust `tempfile` call reach none of its three patterns, and no census of those was run here.
- promotion: declined. The method rules exercised — scope a census with no convenience filter, classify hits before publishing a count, and measure what a proposed gate would fire on — are all already durable; this leaf is a further instance of each, and the one durable statement specific to it is the gate's own re-worded message and the comment above it.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0170 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.2.2): the gates' own scratch comes back onto the repository volume, and the gate can see it`.
