#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.2.4 — The visibility gate cannot see the abbreviation

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7`'s gate-record census, which found a live instance while counting something else.
- 🔴 **The gate built to stop ONE specific false claim has two live instances it cannot see.** `scripts/check_visibility_policy.sh` exists because, in its own header's words, "the superseded private-repository instruction had already leaked past two" reviews. Its `PATTERN` enumerates four sentence shapes, every one of them anchored on the full word `repositor(y|ies)`: a keep/make form, a copular form, a modal form and a "until the clearance gate" form. ⛔ **No abbreviation appears in any of the four**, which is the whole finding — read the script for the literal alternatives rather than reproducing them here, because writing one out trips the gate.
- REPRODUCED with a positive control on the exact sentence rather than by reading the regex:

  ```bash
  printf '%s\n' "model has no external owners yet (the repo is private) —" \
    | grep -qiE 'repositor(y|ies) +(is|are|was|were|stays?|remains?) +(\*\*)?privat' \
    && echo MATCHED || echo "NOT MATCHED"
  ```

  returns **NOT MATCHED**, while `bash scripts/check_visibility_policy.sh` returns **rc=0** over the corpus containing it.
- The two instances, located by file and enclosing construct: `docs/decisions/2026-09-07_phase6-gate-record.md` (deferral 2, "the real-owner acceptance") and `docs/tasks/PHASE-7.md:666`. Neither is in `.doctrine/visibility_exceptions.txt`, which carries three entries.
- ⚠️ **BOTH ARE CORRECT HISTORY, and that is why the blind spot survived.** They are dated 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08; the director's correction is 2026-09-09. Nothing is currently false because of them — so nothing ever failed, and the gap stayed invisible. ⛔ The gate's value is against a NEW or REWORDED sentence, and an abbreviation is exactly how a new one would arrive.
- ⭐ **The gate PROVED precise for the forms it does cover, by refusing this leaf.** Writing the four shapes out longhand above tripped `VISIBILITY-POLICY` on this very section, which is the correct answer: the sentence I had written matched the modal form. ⛔ So the defect is a narrow coverage gap in a gate that otherwise works, not a gate that does not fire — and the acceptance below must preserve that precision rather than trading it for a looser match.
- ⭐ **The same trap caught the instrument measuring it, which is worth keeping.** The census's first search used `\brepo\b`; `git grep -E` does not support `\b`, so it returned rc=1, no match — blind in precisely the way the gate is. It was caught only because a known line existed to test the tool against. **A search returning nothing is a claim about the SEARCH until a positive control says otherwise.**
- Owns: deciding whether the pattern gains the abbreviation (and which other forms a census finds), and what happens to the two historical sentences — an exceptions entry naming each with its reason, or a past-tense rewording that keeps the provenance.
- ⛔ Do not widen the pattern by guesswork. `.11.2.2`'s lesson applies: census the corpus for the forms that actually occur before writing the rule, and the gate's own header warns that a bare `privat` match is wrong because the corpus legitimately discusses private files, channels, overlays and repositories.
- ⚠️ `docs/decisions/` supersedes rather than mutates, so the phase-6 record is NOT edited here; `.11.4.7.3` owns whether that record needs a superseding note.
- Acceptance: the pattern's blind spot is reproduced with a control that fails against the current script; the widened pattern is derived from a census of the forms present, not invented; both historical instances are dispositioned explicitly; the gate's own `--self-test` gains an abbreviation case; and the existing three exceptions still pass.
- ✅ **REPRODUCED against the shipped script, not by reading the regex.** `bash scripts/check_visibility_policy.sh` returned **rc=0** over a corpus containing both instances, and the widened matcher's self-test goes RED on the abbreviated probe the moment the pattern is reverted to the full word.
- ✅ **THE CENSUS, and the widening is DERIVED from it.** `git grep -n -I -iE "(repo|repos|repository|repositories)[^a-zA-Z]" -- '*.md' | grep -iE privat` returns **~60 co-occurring lines**. Reading them, the abbreviation is the ONLY uncovered spelling that STATES a visibility; the many `private-repository instruction` lines put `private` BEFORE the noun and are *corrections of the superseded policy*, so no clause matches them and none should. ⛔ The repair is therefore one substitution — `repositor(y|ies)` → `repo(s|sitory|sitories)?` in the three noun-anchored clauses — not a new clause. **Measured delta: 3 matches → 11, and `comm` confirms none lost.**
- 🔴 **SIX OF THE EIGHT NEW MATCHES WERE THE PROJECT DOCUMENTING ITS OWN BLIND SPOT**, and that is the finding rather than an inconvenience. Writing down what the instances read puts the trigger into the corpus, so widening the gate flags `MEMORY.md`, `docs/TASK_TREE.md` and three places in this tree. ⭐ It is `check_self_tests.sh`'s founding incident exactly — *a control searched for a string it contained* — reached from the documentation side.
- ✅ **DISPOSITIONED BY A RULE, not case by case: except what must stay VERBATIM, reword what is PROSE.**
  - **Reworded (5)** — `MEMORY.md`, `docs/TASK_TREE.md` and three sentences here now NAME the abbreviated copular form instead of instantiating it. ⭐ This follows `check_self_tests.sh`'s own precedent of RE-WORDING rather than path-excluding, so those surfaces stay policed as they change.
  - **Excepted (3)** — `2026-09-07_phase6-gate-record.md:44` (a dated record; `docs/decisions/` supersedes rather than mutates), `PHASE-7.md:666` (inside a dated `Done (2026-09-08)` entry whose 2026-09-09 correction is the line ABOVE it, so the record corrects itself in place), and this leaf's own reproduction command (the literal sentence IS the evidence; rewording it destroys the reproduction).
- ✅ **The self-test gains the abbreviation in both directions**: four new positive probes (the copular form, its uppercase variant, the keep-form and the plural `repos`) and three new negative probes drawn from real corrected lines. 8 leak shapes, 7 unrelated senses.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED FOUR WAYS.** (1) the pattern reverted to the full word → three positive probes red by name; (2) a bare `privat[a-z]*.repo` clause added, the over-broad direction the header warns against → **all four** negative probes red, including two real corrections; (3) a genuinely NEW sentence injected into `docs/book/src/deployment.md` → refused by file and line, which is what the gate is FOR; (4) a bogus exception added → `stale exception` by name. All restored.
- ✅ **All six exceptions resolve**, three pre-existing and three added; the stale-exception arm is live, so the file cannot rot silently.
- ⛔ **NOT claimed:** that the pattern is complete. It covers the spellings this corpus actually contains, measured today; a form nobody has written yet is not covered, and the census command is recorded so the next reader re-derives rather than trusts.
- Routed OUT: none. ⚠️ `.11.4.7.3` still owns whether the phase-6 record needs a superseding note; this leaf only stops the gate being blind to it.
- NO REGRESSION: no Rust, schema, migration or route changed. The three pre-existing exceptions still resolve and the four original positive probes still fire.
- lockstep: `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`'s `VISIBILITY-POLICY` row gains the abbreviation; `README.md` and the book are unchanged.
- promotion: declined for a new record — this is `check_self_tests.sh`'s documented self-reference trap reached from the documentation side, and `a-census-is-as-wide-as-its-key.md` already carries the widening half. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0258`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.2.5 — The census gate is discharged by any command in the section, including one about something else

- Opened: `pending`, found by FALSIFYING a claim I had published to the director — that the enforcement layer "is doing real work, not ceremony". Two of the three sub-claims survived; this one did not.
- 🔴 **The finding, by controlled experiment rather than by reading the script.** Two probe sections were staged, carrying the IDENTICAL claim line `- ⚠️ The two copies must agree about things nothing checks.` and differing in one variable:

| probe | section also contains | gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — \`cargo clippy …\` rc=0.` | **not flagged** |
| B | nothing else | flagged |

- **The mechanism, then confirmed in the source.** `scripts/check_gap_claims.sh:71` fires only when `added[i] && low[i] ~ CLAIM_RE && !has[sec[i]]` — where `has[sec]` is true if ANY line of the section matches `CENSUS_RE`. That expression (`:60`) includes `cargo `, `make `, `git grep`, `scripts/check_` and `--self-test`.
- ⛔ **So a leaf discharges its own gap claims by having been VERIFIED.** Every closed leaf's `[x] ADDRESSED` / `[x] NO REGRESSION` box names `cargo` or `make` by construction — `TASK-ACCEPTANCE` requires tool output in each box — so the census gate is inert for exactly the leaves that are complete. It fires only on a claim added to a section that has not yet recorded a command.
- 🔎 **This is why the gate caught me at all**: `.7.4.5` was being OPENED when the claim was written, so its section had no verification box yet. Had the claim been added one commit later, in the same section, it would have passed. The catch was real and the mechanism was luck.
- ⚠️ **NOT an argument for widening `CENSUS_RE`**, and the script says why at `:17`: a predicate firing on 81 pre-existing claims "is unusable and teaches bypass". The scoping to added lines is sound. The defect is the DISCHARGE test, which asks "does this section contain a command?" instead of "does this section contain a command *for this claim*".
- ⭐ **`.11.2.3` is the same family** — a gate that disagreed with the renderer it was meant to police — and `docs/knowledge/a-control-is-calibrated-against-the-renderer.md` is the transferable form. This one is calibrated against a proxy for a census rather than against a census.
- Owns: measuring how many of the tree's existing discharges are genuine versus incidental (the population before the rule, per `.11.6`); deciding the discharge test — proximity to the claim line, an explicit marker such as the `census:` form the script already accepts, or something else the measurement supports; and extending the script's `--self-test` with the two-probe arm above, which it does not currently have.
- Acceptance: the two-probe control is an arm of `scripts/check_gap_claims.sh --self-test`, observed distinguishing A from B, with probe A's current pass recorded as the RED; a census classifies every existing discharge in `docs/tasks/` as genuine or incidental before any rule is proposed; the chosen discharge test is justified against that census rather than against this one example; and `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` stays green on the tree as it stands, or every newly-flagged section is repaired in the same commit.
- ✅ **THE POPULATION, CLASSIFIED BEFORE ANY RULE WAS PROPOSED** (`.11.6`, acceptance clause 2). Over the governed corpus: **103 claim lines, 103 discharged, 0 undischarged** — the shipped rule finds nothing anywhere, which is the finding restated as a number. Distance from each claim to its nearest in-section census: **36 same line, 52 within 3, 14 within 10, 1 at 34 lines**.
- ⛔ **AND DISTANCE IS THE WRONG AXIS, which reading the tail showed.** The 34-line case pairs a claim about one instrument with a census about another; two 5-line cases pair a frontier TABLE ROW with an adjacent table row. Proximity would have accepted some incidental discharges and rejected genuine ones, so it was measured and rejected rather than adopted because it was the obvious rule.
- ✅ **SIX CANDIDATE DISCHARGE TESTS, PRICED AGAINST THE SAME 103** — the newly-flagged column is the backlog each would create, and this gate's own header rejects a predicate that fires on a standing population:

| candidate discharge test | standing claims it would newly flag | verdict |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| same SECTION (shipped) | 0 of 103 | the defect — inert by construction |
| same LINE | 67 (65.0%) | rejected |
| same BULLET | 61 (59.2%) | rejected |
| within 1 line / bullet-or-next | 39 (37.9%) | rejected |
| within 3 lines | 15 (14.6%) | rejected — and it accepts the 34-line incidental class it was aimed at |
| section, checklist BOXES excluded | 10 (9.7%) | close, but 6 of the 10 are a false-positive class |
| **section, boxes excluded UNLESS the claim is itself in a box** | **1 (1.0%)** | ✅ **SHIPPED** |

- ⭐ **THE SHIPPED RULE TARGETS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE SYMPTOM, and that is why it is cheap.** The leaf's own diagnosis is that `TASK-ACCEPTANCE` forces tool output into every `- [x]` box, so every closed leaf names `cargo` or `make` by construction. Excluding boxes from the discharge set addresses exactly that; proximity only correlates with it.
- 🔴 **THE 10%-RULE'S EXTRA NINE WERE CLASSIFIED, NOT COUNTED, and 6 of them were FALSE POSITIVES** — claims made INSIDE a `- [x]` box whose census sits in a SIBLING box of the same acceptance record. That is the normal and correct structure: an acceptance record is one unit, and the ADDRESSED box legitimately evidences what the ROOT CAUSE box asserts. The final clause exists for them, and its price is the difference between 10 and 1.
- ⭐ **THE PREDICATE SHIPPED WITH A REDUNDANT CLAUSE AND THE FALSIFICATION SWEEP DELETED IT.** It was written as `own[j]==own[i] || (sec[j]==sec[i] && (!isbox[j] || isbox[i]))`. Dropping the first clause changed **no arm and no corpus number**, because same-bullet implies same-section AND `isbox[j]==isbox[i]`, so the second reduces to `!isbox[i] || isbox[i]` — always true. ⛔ Removed rather than kept: a redundant clause is one a later edit can turn into a difference nobody measured. 🔎 It was found by a degenerate arm that should have failed and did not — the sweep earning its keep on the code it was checking.
- ✅ **CALIBRATED IN COMMITS TOO, and the replay is honest by `.11.18.2`'s discriminator.** The LOOSER rule has been enforced since the initial commit, but the tightening it adds was policed by nothing — deterrence removed claims with no section census at all, never claims discharged only by a box. Over 200 commits the tightened rule would have blocked **1 (0.5%)**, and that one commit is the one that added the single standing instance. **1 block, 1 true positive, 0 false positives** — `REASON-CODE-DOC`'s shape.
- ✅ **THE TWO-PROBE CONTROL IS AN ARM, AND PROBE A's PASS IS THE RED** (acceptance clause 1). Arms 17–18 rebuild the leaf's experiment verbatim; against the pre-fix section-wide discharge, restored in situ, arm 17 fails BY NAME — *"probe A must be flagged: a verification box is not a census for a prose claim"*.
- ✅ **FOUR MORE IN-SITU WRONG RULES, EACH REDDING ITS OWN ARM**, and the negative arms get their red from a DEGENERATE rule rather than from the old one, per `docs/knowledge/a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason.md`:

| in-situ wrong rule | arm that goes RED by name |
| --- | --- |
| the pre-fix section-wide discharge | 17 — PROBE A |
| a box NEVER discharges, even a boxed claim | 21 — an acceptance record is one unit |
| only the same bullet discharges | 20 — only boxes are excluded, not distance (+ 1, 8, 16) |
| any census anywhere discharges | 18 and 9, 11, 14 — the discharge stays section-scoped |

  ⚠️ Arm 19 is LABELLED in the source as passing under every wrong rule tried: it guards a property the simplified predicate DERIVES rather than states, and it is what would notice a future edit making ownership load-bearing again.
- 🔴 **THE REPAIRED GATE THEN FLAGGED A CLOSED RECORD, AND THE CENSUS REFUTED THAT RECORD'S PREMISE.** The one standing instance is `.3.4.3.1.1`'s closing *"nothing enforces the stored value"*. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.2.6 — The acceptance gate reads one checklist and this tree has 194

- Opened: `pending` by `.3.5.4`, which met it while getting its own commit past the gate.
- **The finding.** `scripts/check_task_acceptance.sh` requires a staged code change to be owned by a leaf carrying ticked `ROOT CAUSE` / `ADDRESSED` / `NO REGRESSION` boxes with tool output inside each bullet. Its extractor walks the staged `docs/tasks/*.md` line by line, stops at the **first** box whose text matches the keyword, prints that bullet, and exits at the next box. One file, one box, per label.
- **Measured, not inferred.** `grep -cE '^\s*-\s*\[[xX ]\].*[Rr][Oo][Oo][Tt].?[Cc][Aa][Uu][Ss][Ee]' docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md` returns **194**; running the gate's own awk over the same file returns exactly one — **line 388**, a leaf closed long ago. Every commit that touches `scripts/` or `crates/` is validated against that same historical bullet, whatever leaf the change actually belongs to.
- 🔴 **This is a THIRD leakage hole in a check whose own header documents two.** It names cross-FILE leakage (a co-staged unrelated tree supplying the signature) and incidental-PROSE leakage (a token matched anywhere in the leaf rather than inside the ticked box), and concludes "the signature must sit in the SAME BULLET as the box it backs". It does — just not the bullet belonging to the change being committed. Cross-LEAF leakage is the same soundness failure one level up, and it is total here rather than occasional, because this project keeps one tree file per work unit rather than one file per leaf.
- ⚠️ **What is NOT claimed.** No false acceptance has been shown to have shipped: every recent leaf was written with a real checklist, so the gate's verdict has been right by the author's discipline rather than by the gate. That is exactly the state `check_self_tests.sh` was built for — a control that silently stopped working — and the argument for repairing it is the same.
- ⚠️ **And the honest limit the gate already states still applies above this one:** it proves a box was ticked and cites something re-runnable, never that the output is true. Repairing the scoping does not change that.
- Owns: deciding how the gate identifies the leaf a staged change belongs to — the candidates measured rather than assumed, since a tree file has no machine-readable leaf boundary today beyond heading depth and the `Status:` line `TASK-STATUS` already parses — then the scoping repair, a two-sided `--self-test` arm that a degenerate whole-file extractor must fail, and the `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` row.
- ⛔ A repair must not make the gate refuse honest commits: a leaf legitimately has no `ROOT CAUSE` box until it closes, and a docs-only commit is already out of scope. Measure the refusal rate over recent history before shipping a predicate, as `.11.2.5` priced six candidates against 103 claim lines.
- Acceptance: the gate validates the checklist of the leaf that owns the staged change, not the file's first; the 194-versus-1 measurement is reproduced and then shown closed; a degenerate first-box implementation fails the self-test; the refusal rate is priced over recent commits and reported.

- 🔴 **THE CALIBRATION IS DONE, AND IT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT LARGER THAN THE FIRST: the gate hard-gates a vocabulary this project does not use.** A census of every evidence-bullet lead-in in this tree returns `NO REGRESSION` **203**, `LOCKSTEP` **147**, `REPRODUCE / ISSUE` **142**, `FIX / LOCKSTEP` **45** — against `ADDRESSED` **14** and `ROOT CAUSE` **13**. Two of the three labels the gate BLOCKS on are the project's rarest spellings; the two it does not know at all, `REPRODUCE / ISSUE` and `FIX / LOCKSTEP`, are how the checklist is actually written. ⭐ Same root cause as the scoping hole: the gate has been inert for ~200 commits, so nothing kept either its scope or its vocabulary honest. This is `.11.2.4`'s defect — a check blind to the other spellings of its own noun — in the gate that polices the other gates.
- ✅ **FOUR CANDIDATES PRICED over the last 300 commits** (231 touched code AND staged a tree file), each measured rather than argued:

| Candidate | Refused | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the three boxes must appear in the staged diff's ADDED lines | **23.8%** | rejected — a gate people route around (`.11.5`) |
| same, accepting prose bullets as well as ticked boxes | **25.5%** | rejected — no better, so the box/prose form was never the problem |
| scope to every leaf the commit CLOSES (an added `Status: done`) | **57.7%** | rejected — a commit closes **2.75 leaves on average, up to 5**, because parent lanes close with their child and legitimately carry no checklist |
| scope to the DEEPEST closed leaf + the CORPUS-DERIVED vocabulary | **20.9%** | ⭐ the candidate, and its refusals are TRUE POSITIVES |

- ⭐ **THE REFRAMING THAT MAKES 20.9 % SHIPPABLE, and it is the whole decision.** That figure measures leaves ALREADY CLOSED in a window when the gate was inert — it is past drift, not a forecast of future refusals. The gate is staged-scope-aware and only ever examines the leaf being closed NOW, so a leaf written to the enforced standard passes. ⚠️ Classified rather than assumed: of a sample of five refusals, **four carry no regression evidence anywhere in the tree** — `.11.14.1.2`, `.11.14.3.5`, `.11.14.3.7`, `.13.5` return zero `no.?regress` bullets in their own section and have no `## Commit acceptance` section either. They are real omissions the inert gate never asked about, not false alarms.
- 🔴 **MY OWN THIRD MEASUREMENT WAS UNSOUND AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REPLACED.** The first run of the closed-leaf candidate matched added `Status: done` lines by their TEXT. That line is byte-identical for every leaf, so one commit appeared to close dozens and the candidate scored 64.7%. Re-derived from the diff's hunk headers — POST-image line numbers, the only sound way to say WHERE a line was added — it scores 57.7%. ⭐ Third instance of `a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance` in one session, after `.3.5.4`'s `list_runs` collision and its `tenant_id` spelling.
- Owns next, with the design now settled by measurement: register the corpus-derived vocabulary through the existing `.doctrine/` seam rather than hardcoding this project's words in a portable check; scope to the deepest closed leaf; a two-sided `--self-test` whose degenerate arm is the CURRENT first-box extractor and must fail; and the `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` row.
- ⚠️ The 20.9 % is historical debt that the repair does NOT clear. Decide explicitly whether those leaves are backfilled or accepted as closed-under-the-old-gate, and say which — a gate whose own corpus fails it is the state this leaf exists to end.
- ✅ **THE REPAIR, both halves.** (1) **Scope**: the owner is the leaf whose `Status:` line this commit turns to `done`, read from the staged diff's hunk headers — a pre-commit hook runs before the message exists, so the message cannot be the source. The DEEPEST closed leaf is asked, because a parent lane closes with its child and carries no checklist. (2) **Vocabulary**: the label families move to `.doctrine/acceptance_labels.txt`, a project seam, so the portable check keeps no project's words; the families are DERIVED from the census above. ⚠️ The gate now reads the STAGED BLOB, not the working tree — line numbers that index one and content read from the other silently misalign, which is exactly what a pre-commit hook invites.
- ✅ **A commit that closes no leaf is `NOT CHECKED`, reported rather than silently passed.** An acceptance checklist is the artifact of a leaf CLOSING; a code change mid-leaf is legitimately incomplete, and its ownership is `TASK-TREE-OWNERSHIP`'s question, not this one. 12 of 231 historical commits fall here.
- ✅ **THE GATE GAINED A `--self-test` — it had none**, so it was in the population `check_self_tests.sh --census` reports as uncovered. Six arms, and the NEGATIVE one is the extractor this repair replaced: a first-box scan over the whole file, which must pick `PROJ.1` (a sibling that closed earlier with a complete checklist) while the real extractor picks `PROJ.2.1` (the leaf actually closing, with none). If the degenerate scan ever stops picking the wrong leaf, the fixture no longer reproduces the defect and the positive arm proves nothing.
- ✅ **THE DEBT IS COUNTED, NOT BACKFILLED** — `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_acceptance-debt-is-counted-not-backfilled.md`. `--debt` reports **73 of 281** closed leaves answering fewer than every question. ⛔ Backfilling is rejected on principle rather than effort: writing `NO REGRESSION: …` into a leaf closed weeks ago asserts a suite was run when nobody ran one — manufacturing evidence after the fact, the exact offence this gate guards against. The softer "re-run today and record it there" is rejected too: a true statement about today attached to a past change is a false record.
- ⚠️ **NOT claimed: that the 67 leaves regressed anything.** Most were verified; what is missing is the record of it in the leaf. A documentation gap measured precisely is not a quality claim about the code.
- ⚠️ **Honest limit, unchanged by this repair:** the gate proves the author cited something re-runnable, never that the output is true. Scoping it correctly makes it ask the right leaf; it does not make it a verifier.
- 🔴 **THE IN-SITU FALSIFICATION EARNED ITS KEEP: the first repair PASSED with its own checklist deleted.** Removing this leaf's `NO REGRESSION` bullet changed nothing, because the leaf *discusses* the label — five prose bullets naming `NO REGRESSION` satisfied the question. That is leakage hole (2), incidental prose, walking back in through the widened vocabulary, and **a self-referential leaf is exactly where it bites** (`check_self_tests.sh`'s founding trap, reached from a third side). ✅ Fixed by anchoring the family as the bullet's **LEAD-IN** — `[^[:alpha:]]*` steps over the checkbox, the emoji and the bold markers and stops at the first letter. Re-priced: **17.5 % → 20.6 %**, three points paid for correctness.
- 🔴 **AND MY FALSIFICATION HARNESS ITSELF RETURNED THE WRONG INSTANCE — the FOURTH `a-key-too-loose` of the session.** The regex that was to delete `.11.2.6`'s `NO REGRESSION` bullet matched `.3.5.4`'s, because both open `— \`make gate\` prints \`=== all doctrines green ===\` over 21 checks`. The falsification reported PASS while editing a different leaf entirely. Re-done by POSITION — anchored inside `.11.2.6`'s own section — and then exhaustively: removing **every** bullet answering a family refuses (CAUSE 2 bullets, FIX 3, NO REGRESSION 1), restoring passes. ⭐ Removing ONE bullet correctly still passes, because this leaf answers each question more than once in the project's real forms; a falsification that removes one instance of a redundant answer proves nothing.
- ✅ **One definition of the lead-in rule, shared by the gate and `--debt`.** They were written separately and disagreed — the census undercounted at **67** where the gate's rule gives **73**. Two copies of one rule drift; this repository has now repaired that shape five times.
- 🔎 **AND THE REPAIR TRIPPED A NEIGHBOURING GATE'S DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL, which is now closed.** `check_self_tests.sh` discovers instruments by grepping for the flag's literal text; the new test case RUNS the checker with `--self-test`, so its source contains the literal and discovery found it. Its header predicted this ("a script that merely MENTIONS the flag … is run with an argument it ignores") and was wrong about the consequence: a unittest module does not ignore an unknown argument, it exits `error: unrecognized arguments: --self-test`, so a passing test suite was reported as a failing instrument. ✅ `scripts/tests/` is now excluded BY PATH — tests OF instruments are not instruments, and they are run by `unittest discover` in the pre-push list where their arguments mean what they say. ⛔ A directory, not a filename: naming files is how an exclusion list rots. Census after: **37 discovered, 8 of 45 instruments still carry none**.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0262.

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.13`'s ownership repair. ⛔ **I left a known-broken published row standing for a session with a rationale and no owner. The rationale survives; the absence of an owner does not.**

  - `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md:39` — the `INDEX-FRONTIER` row contains `` `\| — \|` `` inside a code span; the renderer emits THREE cells and the third is a bare `—`. **The doctrine registry's published page does not name the enforcer for `INDEX-FRONTIER`**, and its rationale is cut mid-sentence at "fixed this exact". ⛔ **Deliberately still standing** — it is the last real-world instance in 322 files, and `TOOLBOX.md`'s measured rule is that a self-test written alongside the code shares its blind spots, which this parser's demonstrably did. Reproduce at `ad63351`.
  - `RECONCILIATION.md:111` — repaired in REPAIR-0175 with its superseded text named, because it is that leaf's own deliverable and a truncated Evidence cell publishes half a record.

  1. The corrected parser is run against the LIVE `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md:39` and FIRES — a control observed red on a row this leaf did not write, which is the whole reason the row was kept.
  2. The self-test's `a pipe inside a code span is not a separator` arm is replaced by one asserting it IS a separator, plus an arm proving the escaped form is not.

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0187. ⭐ **The warning above did NOT materialise, and the reason is worth keeping:** the ratchet runs the WORKING-TREE parser against *both* sides of its comparison — its `now=` and `before=` assignments pipe `git show ":$f"` and `git show "HEAD:$f"` through the SAME `count_defects` (locate by `grep -n '^  \(now\|before\)=' scripts/check_table_arity.sh`, not by a line number that drifts), so correcting the rule moves `now` and `before` together. Staged unrepaired it would have been 1 vs 1 (no rise); staged repaired it is **0 vs 1**, a FALL, promoted silently. A rule correction cannot block its own fix through this ratchet. The same-commit repair was still the right call — for the published page, not for the gate.

  - `` | `` x | y `` | 2 | `` → 2 cells — a double-backtick run does not protect a pipe either.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.2.8 — The census gate cannot see this project's own census family

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1` (REPAIR-0266), which was REFUSED by `GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS` for a claim it had discharged with `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --readers` — a tracked, self-tested instrument built for exactly that claim.
- **The finding, read from the gate's own pattern rather than retyped.** `CENSUS_RE` (`scripts/check_gap_claims.sh`) lists `scripts/check_` and does NOT list `scripts/census_`. Re-derive:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, pathlib
pat = re.search(r"^CENSUS_RE='([^']*)'", pathlib.Path("scripts/check_gap_claims.sh").read_text(), re.M).group(1)
print(bool(re.search(pat, "python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --readers")))  # -> False
print(bool(re.search(pat, "bash scripts/check_gap_claims.sh")))                            # -> True
EOF
```

- ⚠️ **The population, classified before any rule is proposed** (`.11.6`), and the first number was wrong in the direction that would have inflated the finding. Sections of `docs/tasks/*.md` citing a `scripts/census_*` invocation: **78**, of which 8 carry no other recognised census — but intersecting with the gate's OWN `CLAIM_RE`, which is what makes a section subject to the rule at all, gives **28 sections, 28 masked, 0 that would be refused today**. ⛔ So this is a LATENT false-refusal, not a live one, and the 8 was a population rather than a defect count.
- ⭐ **What makes it worth owning anyway is what it cost in the act of being found.** Refused, the author's cheapest route to green was to paste a raw `git grep … | wc -l` beside the instrument — a LESS durable census than the tracked, self-tested script already cited. A gate that prefers an ad-hoc grep to a registered instrument is teaching the bypass `.11.9` rejects gates for, with the sign reversed: it did not let a bad claim through, it degraded a good one.
- ⛔ **`.11.2.5` ruled against widening `CENSUS_RE` and this must name the difference** (`docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 2 — if it was ruled the other way, the earlier ruling wins unless a difference is named). That ruling is about the DISCHARGE test being too loose, and its objection is that a change "firing on 81 pre-existing claims is unusable and teaches bypass". This change fires on nothing: it makes the gate recognise one more spelling of a census, so it can only turn a refusal into a pass, and the measurement says there are **0** of either today. The direction is opposite and the backlog is empty.
- ⚠️ **It is still a LOOSENING and must be priced as one.** `scripts/census_*` is 15 tracked instruments whose entire purpose is enumeration, so recognising them is not a widening of what counts as evidence — but the calibration must show it, not assert it.
- Owns: deciding whether `CENSUS_RE` gains the `scripts/census_` spelling, and whether the raw `git grep` that `.7.3.6.1` was pushed into keeping should stay as a reader's cross-check or be removed as the artefact of a gate defect.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.2.7 — The pre-push script suite disagreed with itself, 3 problems then 19, over byte-identical code

- Opened: `pending` by `.4.2.3.1`, which ran the pre-push script gate during its own verification and got two different answers from it (§15: found while using the instrument, so it is owned rather than reported).
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT, and it is a disagreement rather than a failure.** `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` — one of the four commands `COMMIT.md` names as the pre-push gate — was run twice on 2026-09-19, minutes apart, with **no edit between them**. First run: `Ran 73 tests ... FAILED (failures=1, errors=2)`. Second run: **17 ERROR + 2 FAIL**. A gate that answers differently about the same bytes is not measuring the bytes.
- ⛔ **NOT this leaf's change, and that is proved rather than argued:** `git status --porcelain -- scripts/` returns **nothing**, and `git diff --stat HEAD -- scripts/ci_browser.py scripts/ci_env.py scripts/ci_scanners.py scripts/tests/` is **empty**. The Python under test is byte-identical to `HEAD`.
- **The affected population, all of it in three modules** — `test_ci_browser` (8), `test_ci_scanners` (6 + 1 FAIL), `test_ci_env` (3 + 1 FAIL). Both FAILs name the same thing: `test_terminal_signal_reaps_installer_before_launcher_returns` and `test_terminal_cancellation_retains_receipt_and_reaps_version_child`. Every one of the three modules drives a SUBPROCESS with a deadline; none of the other nine modules is affected.
- ⚠️ **A hypothesis is recorded as a hypothesis, per `TOOLBOX.md`.** The machine was under measured load at the time — `syspolicyd` 34.9%, `XprotectService` 20.3%, swap **6151 MB of 7168 MB** used, with rustc children sitting at 0.0% CPU blocked on paging. A deadline-driven control on a paging machine is the obvious suspect. ⛔ It is NOT the finding: the finding is the disagreement, and the cause must be established by re-running on a quiet machine and by reading the errors, not by assuming the convenient explanation.
- ⭐ **The class already has a name here, and this is its mirror.** `docs/knowledge/a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason.md` was promoted by `.11.20.2`. A control that FAILS for an unrelated reason destroys the same thing — the link between the verdict and the code — and is worse in one respect: it trains a reader to discount a red gate.
- Owns: capturing the actual error text (the first pass captured only the `ERROR:`/`FAIL:` headers, which is why the cause is still open); re-running on an unloaded machine to separate load from a real defect; then deciding per module whether the deadline is too tight, is measured against the wrong clock, or is a genuine reaping defect the load merely exposes. ⚠️ If the deadlines are widened, the widening must be calibrated rather than picked (`.11.6`), and a control that can no longer fail is not the goal.
- Acceptance: the full error text recorded for at least one test per module; a quiet-machine re-run reported with its own numbers beside the loaded one, so the disagreement is bounded rather than asserted; a per-module disposition with its reason; and, if a deadline moves, the population it was calibrated over.
- ⛔ Explicitly NOT claimed by the leaf that opened this: that the suite is green. `.4.2.3.1` records this gate as RED with a cause not yet established, which is the honest state.
- Status: `pending`.
- Verification / commit: pending.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.2 — The dependency gate is red: RUSTSEC-2026-0285

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2`, which ran `cargo deny check` as the re-derivation of a G1 line and got rc=**1**.
- The finding: `advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. **RUSTSEC-2026-0285** — rustls accepted TLS 1.3 handshake messages sent at the wrong encryption level when they followed a key-changing message in the same record. `rustls 0.23.43`; the advisory names ≥0.23.45.
- ⭐ **The exposure is narrower than "a TLS vulnerability", and the leaf must say which.** The handshake transcript stays authenticated, so a network-position attacker cannot alter or complete a handshake. The practical effect is that a peer may send in PLAINTEXT what should have been encrypted without rustls rejecting the connection. ⛔ Do not restate it as handshake forgery.
- ⚠️ **This is DEPENDENCY drift, not advisory-database drift against a fixed graph.** `git show ecceb8d:Cargo.lock | grep -c '^name = "rustls"$'` returns **0** — rustls entered the graph after Phase 1 (positive control: the same command for `tokio` returns **1**).
- Owns: taking the upgrade, re-running the gate, and deciding whether `cargo update -p rustls` alone is right or the lockfile wants a wider refresh. ⚠️ A lockfile change is a supply-chain change: state what moved and what did not.
- Acceptance: `cargo deny check` rc=0 with all four sections ok; the diff to `Cargo.lock` is enumerated rather than summarised; the workspace builds and its suites pass afterwards; and the leaf records whether any OTHER advisory was masked by the run stopping at the first.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0199. `cargo update -p rustls` — `rustls 0.23.43 → 0.23.45`. `cargo deny check` now returns **`advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`**, rc=0.
- ⭐ **The lock diff is FOUR LINES, enumerated rather than summarised**, which is the whole reason the acceptance asked for it: a lockfile bump is a supply-chain change, and "just a patch update" is a claim about a file nobody read.
  ```
  3824c3824  < version = "0.23.43"      > version = "0.23.45"
  3826c3826  < checksum = "0283386c…"  > checksum = "0d41d731…"
  ```
  ⛔ Nothing transitive moved. `cargo update` reported `Locking 1 package to latest compatible version` and named 37 unchanged dependencies behind latest, which are deliberately left alone: this leaf owns ONE advisory, not a lockfile refresh.
- **No other advisory was masked.** `cargo deny` does not stop at the first finding — it reports all four sections every run, and the failing run's advisories block contained exactly one `error[vulnerability]` (`grep -c '^error\[vulnerability\]'` = 1, `grep -c '^warning\['` = 0).
- ⭐ **The exposure, stated at its real width rather than as "a TLS vulnerability".** RUSTSEC-2026-0285: rustls accepted TLS 1.3 handshake messages sent at the wrong encryption level when they followed a key-changing message in the same record (RFC 8446 §5.1 requires terminating with `unexpected_message`). ⛔ The handshake transcript stays AUTHENTICATED, so a network-position attacker cannot alter or complete a handshake; the practical effect is that a peer may send in plaintext what should have been encrypted without rustls rejecting the connection. Functionally the same bug as Go's CVE-2025-61730.
- **NO REGRESSION, and it is the strongest evidence this tree has had all session:** `cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` reaches **94 test binaries**, **102 suites ok / 1 failed**, **815 tests passed / 1 failed**. The single failure in the entire workspace is `.11.4.7.2.4`'s known browser control, which predates this change and reproduces without it.
- ⭐ **That run also ANSWERS `.11.4.7.2.4`'s `--no-fail-fast` question with a measurement rather than a preference.** Default fail-fast reached **11** binaries and left four crates unknown; `--no-fail-fast` reached **94** and turned "unknown" into "one known failure". Cost: **319.3 s** of test execution, dominated by one 135.23 s suite. ⚠️ The verdict belongs to `.11.4.7.2.4`, which owns it — recorded here because this leaf is what produced the number.
- ⛔ No product code, schema, migration, test or script changed. `Cargo.lock` is the entire diff.
- promotion: declined. The method exercised — enumerate a dependency diff instead of summarising it — is an instance of `docs/knowledge/a-census-is-an-instrument-not-a-table`, not a new statement.
- Verification: `cargo deny check` rc=0; `cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` 815 passed / 1 pre-existing failure; `make gate` 18 checks rc=0.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.3 — The secret scan is red on a test fixture

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2`, which ran `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` as the re-derivation of a G1 line and got rc=**1**.
- The finding: one hit, rule `generic-api-key`, at `crates/reasonbraid-core/tests/delegation_representation.rs:74` — the literal `idempotency_key: "…"`, entropy 3.875 — introduced 2026-09-13 by REPAIR-0134 (`.3.4.5`).
- ⭐ **It is a FALSE POSITIVE and the gate is red anyway, and both halves matter.** A sixteen-hex-character test fixture is not a credential; a red gate is still a red gate, and a project that lets one sit goes blind to the next true positive.
- ⛔ Two repairs are available and they are NOT equivalent. `.gitleaksignore` takes **exact historical fingerprints only** and says so in its own header (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.2.2`, provenance in `docs/decisions/2026-09-09_history-fixture-fingerprints.md`) — suppressing the PATH or the RULE is explicitly forbidden there. The alternative is to change the fixture so it does not read as a secret. ⚠️ Prefer the fixture change where it costs nothing: an allowlist entry is a permanent claim about a line, and the line is a test constant nobody depends on.
- ⚠️ **CI would fail identically** — `scripts/ci_scanners.py` pins gitleaks 8.30.1 and runs `detect --source . --redact=100`, the same detection with the same rules. This is not a local-tooling artifact.
- Owns: the repair, plus the question `.11.4.7.2` raised and did not own — whether `make deny` and `make secret-scan` should join the commit-time gate rather than living only in a CI workflow that has never run.
- ⚠️ That question needs a MEASUREMENT, not a preference: both are slower than the 18 doctrines, and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.5`'s constraint is that a gate people route around is a gate that lies. Time them before proposing either.
- Acceptance: `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` rc=0; the leaf states which of the two repairs was taken and why the other was not; if an allowlist entry was used, it is an exact fingerprint with a reason; and the commit-time-gate question carries the timing census that settles it.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0200. `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` now returns **`no leaks found`**, rc=0.
- 🔴 **BOTH repairs were taken, because measuring proved my planned one INSUFFICIENT.** The leaf said to prefer the fixture rename and avoid an allowlist entry. ⛔ **A rename cannot reach a historical finding.** `gitleaks detect` scans all 488 commits, and the finding is attributed to the commit that INTRODUCED the line: after renaming, the scan still returned rc=1 with `fingerprint=b3802b16601fb4a2da67a8721d7659ae1e36aed9:crates/reasonbraid-core/tests/delegation_representation.rs:generic-api-key:74`. ⭐ The exact-fingerprint entry is the ONLY instrument that clears it — which is precisely what `.gitleaksignore`'s header says it is for, and what its two existing entries are.
- **The fingerprint** carries its reason inline: a verified test constant, an envelope field in a byte-size instrument, referenced nowhere else (`git grep -c` returns 1). ⛔ The path and the rule are NOT suppressed — `.gitleaksignore` forbids that in its own header.
- **The rename is kept anyway, as forward hygiene**: `b3f1c2d4e5a60718` → `key-delegation-1`. Every sibling fixture already spells these readably (`k-forged`, `client-key-0001`, `key_ac5_second`); the hex blob was the single outlier, and the next author copies what they see.
- ⚠️ **The rename is EXACTLY 16 characters, and that is load-bearing.** `delegation_representation.rs:172` asserts `baseline == 308` — a byte count over the serialized envelope, which contains this field. A shorter or longer name would have silently moved a measurement instrument's number. The file now says so in a comment, so nobody "tidies" it back.
- ⭐ **THE COMMIT-TIME-GATE QUESTION, SETTLED ON WHAT EACH CHECK IS TRIGGERED BY rather than on cost.** A commit CAN introduce a secret → the secret scan is **change-triggered** and belongs in the commit gate. An advisory appears against code nobody touched → `cargo deny` is **TIME-triggered**, so gating it on commits is both too often and too rarely, and a push is the moment the claim leaves the machine.
  - `SECRET-SCAN` added to `scripts/check_doctrines.project.sh` — the 10th project check. Priced first (`.11.5`): **1.07 / 1.14 / 1.15 s** over three runs, scanning 488 commits and 15.11 MB, against a **6.65 s** enforcer — about +17%.
  - `.githooks/pre-push` created, running `cargo deny check` — **1.15 s** with the advisory database cached under the repository-local `CARGO_HOME` (`.project-data/cargo/advisory-dbs`, so §13 holds).
  - ⚠️ **The enforcer's own published cost was STALE**: `check_self_tests.sh`'s header records "about 3.15 s". Measured today: **6.65 s**. Not corrected here — it is another file's number and correcting it in passing is how a leaf stops being bounded — but recorded so the next reader does not inherit it.
- ⛔ **Both new gates SKIP LOUDLY rather than failing closed when their tool is absent**, and that is a deliberate weakening with a stated reason: failing closed would block every contributor who has not installed `gitleaks` or `cargo-deny`. ⚠️ A skip is a weaker guarantee than a pass and must never READ like one, so each prints a notice naming what was not checked.
- **FALSIFIED, three arms, each self-reversing and each proved restored by `cmp -s`:** removing the fingerprint → `SECRET-SCAN` rc=1 naming the re-run command; `PATH` stripped of `gitleaks` → rc=0 with `SECRET-SCAN: SKIPPED` on stderr, never a silent pass; restoring `rustls 0.23.43` in `Cargo.lock` → `pre-push` rc=1, printing the advisory and `pre-push: REFUSED`. Positive control afterwards: rc=0.
- promotion: declined. The transferable half — that a control's reach is a property of what it SCANS, not of what you changed — is an instance of `docs/knowledge/a-claim-of-sameness-is-worth-its-call-graph`; the rest is this repository's tooling.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.4 — A control asserts the exact fact its own repair made honest

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2`, whose G1 unit-baseline re-derivation ran the workspace suite and got rc=101.
- The failure: `crates/reasonbraid-browse/tests/browser_roundtrip.rs:582`, `a_real_navigation_deadline_stops_the_browser_and_origin`, asserting `response["error"]["cleanup_confirmed"] == true`. Observed `false`, with `cleanup_error: "browser stderr completion unconfirmed"`.
- ⭐ **The assertion ABOVE it passes.** `response["error"]["kind"] == "time_budget_exceeded"` holds — which means **REPAIR-0089's fix is working exactly as designed**. That repair found `Lifetime::finish` replacing the response's `kind` with the conjunction of four cleanup facts, and split them: `kind` keeps the render's own outcome, and `cleanup_confirmed` / `cleanup_error` carry the cleanup fact separately. The product is now telling the truth, and the control fails ON the truth.
- 🔴 **So this is not a flaky test and not a regression. It is a control asserting a property the product deliberately stopped claiming.** `docs/decisions/2026-09-10_browser-checkpoint-timing.md` records the cause: detached `chrome_crashpad_handler` and `GoogleUpdater` processes retain the browser's inherited stderr write endpoint after the group exits, so the stderr task cannot observe completion. REPAIR-0089's own note says the rule is "never to CLAIM an unobserved termination".
- ⛔ **NOT a load artifact, measured in both directions.** First observed inside `cargo test --all` while another project was compiling on the same machine (`elapsed_ms` 41170). Re-run ISOLATED on a quiet machine, single-threaded: identical failure, same line, `elapsed_ms` 40022, 81.30 s. Two runs, two load states, one result.
- ⚠️ **The blast radius is larger than one test, and that is why this is a leaf rather than a note.** `cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary, so this failure ABORTS the workspace run at the 11th of many: `reasonbraid-cli`, `-core`, `-node` and `-server` never execute. Every claim of the form "the suites are green" is therefore unverifiable on this machine until it is resolved — including the one `.11.4.7.2` was re-deriving.
- Owns: deciding which of the two is wrong. Either (a) the control over-asserts for a desktop runtime whose documented behaviour it cannot control, and should assert `kind` plus an explicit disposition of `cleanup_confirmed` rather than demanding `true`; or (b) the product genuinely should be able to confirm stderr completion despite the detached handlers, and does not.
- ⛔ **Do NOT resolve this by loosening the assertion to accept either value.** REPAIR-0089 explicitly refused that, for a stated reason: the control would stop proving that the deadline cancels a real in-flight navigation. Whatever is chosen must keep that proof.
- ⚠️ And do not resolve it by widening the 30-second budget: `NAVIGATION_WINDOW` is the thing under test, the render reaches ~40 s against it, and the budget was already refused as a fix once.
- ⭐ Worth asking while here: whether the workspace run should use `--no-fail-fast`, so one environment-sensitive control cannot hide the state of four crates. ⚠️ That is a measurement about run time, not a preference — price it.
- ⭐ **PRICED, at `.11.4.7.2.2` (REPAIR-0199), and the number settles it.** Default fail-fast reaches **11** test binaries and leaves `cli`, `core`, `node` and `server` UNKNOWN. `--no-fail-fast` reaches **94**: **102 suites ok / 1 failed, 815 tests passed / 1 failed**, in **319.3 s** of test execution (one suite is 135.23 s of that). ⛔ So the cost of knowing is not extra failures — there is exactly ONE failure in the whole workspace, this one — it is run time on a run that already takes minutes. ⚠️ This leaf still owns the DECISION and where it belongs (`make test`? a pre-push path?); what it no longer owns is the measurement.
- Acceptance: the failure is reproduced and attributed to (a) or (b) with runtime evidence, never to "flaky"; the repair keeps REPAIR-0089's proof that the deadline cancels a real navigation; `cargo test --all --locked` reaches every crate afterwards and its result is recorded whatever it is; and if `--no-fail-fast` is adopted, the timing census that justified it is in the leaf.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0202.
- 🔴 **THE LEAF'S OWN (a)/(b) CHOICE IS REFUTED, AND THE ANSWER IS A THIRD THING IT DID NOT OFFER: THE RUN HAD PICKED ITS OWN BROWSER.** `crates/reasonbraid-browse/tests/support/mod.rs::browser_binary()` carried a discovery list, so any run that did not go through `scripts/ci_browser.py` — a bare `cargo test --all`, which is exactly what `.11.4.7.2` and `.11.4.7.2.2` used — silently selected `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/…`. The control is qualified against the runtime `.11.4.3.1.2.5` pinned; it was being evaluated against the desktop browser that pin exists to avoid. ⭐ **A pin a second path can bypass is not a pin.**
- **The two-site contrast, one variable.** Same test binary, same machine, same competing load — another repository's release build held a core at 98.8% across both arms, so load is a CONSTANT here rather than a confound — and `R3_BROWSER_BIN` is the only thing that changes:

  | runtime | verdict | worker elapsed | escaped handler last seen | survival past the worker's own exit |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | desktop Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83 | cleanup unconfirmed, FAILED 4 of 4 | 41.07 s | +47.18 s | +6.24 s |
  | pinned Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.36 | cleanup confirmed, PASSED 2 of 2 | 31.13 s | +30.97 s | 0, inside one 150 ms sample |

  ⭐ The ten-second gap between the elapsed times is not noise: it is `CLEANUP_BUDGET` being spent in full on an end-of-file that cannot arrive.
- **PINPOINTED at the file descriptor, never inferred.** `lsof -p` on both processes during a failing run, sampled every 500 ms: the worker's fd 11 is `PIPE 0xbb56abe118065101 ->0x2e37041051b342b4` and `chrome_crashpad_handler`'s fd 2 is `PIPE 0x2e37041051b342b4 ->0xbb56abe118065101` — the two ends of ONE pipe, printed by the kernel rather than deduced. That handler reports `PPID 1` and process group `45254` while the owned browser group was `45239`: it left the group the worker owns and kept the inherited stderr write end. `Lifetime::finish` reaps the owned group — and `verify_browser_groups()` independently confirms its absence — then waits for `read_stderr` to reach EOF, which needs the ESCAPED holder to close too.
- 🔴 **AND THE PINNED RUNTIME ESCAPES IDENTICALLY — the tidy story is wrong.** Under Chrome for Testing the same instrument shows TWO handlers at `PPID 1`, process groups `50752` and `50754` against an owned group of `50742`, both holding `0xe8181443c00b5a90`, whose peer is the worker's fd 11. The structure is the same; only the EXIT LATENCY differs. ⛔ So this control's green is a property of how fast a third-party process exits, **not** a containment guarantee, and saying so is the difference between closing a question and hiding one. Annotated at `.7.3.2`, which owns detached-descendant containment, rather than left as a passing test's implied claim.
- **The repair, in the test harness and nowhere else.** `browser_binary()` is now `std::env::var_os("R3_BROWSER_BIN").map(PathBuf::from)` and nothing more. `ci_browser.py` sets that variable to the build it has just downloaded, SHA-256-verified and version-checked; `make test` and `.github/workflows/rust.yml` both run the workspace suite through it, so the qualified path loses nothing.
- ⛔ **NO PRODUCT CODE CHANGED, and that is a finding rather than an omission.** The worker was right on every run: an escaped descendant holding the pipe IS an unaccounted-for browser process, and `a_render_refusal_survives_an_unconfirmed_cleanup` pins that reading deliberately with an injected `setsid` writer. "Repairing" this in `lifetime.rs` would have meant claiming a termination nobody observed — the exact thing REPAIR-0089 refused by name.
- ⚠️ **A SKIP MUST NEVER READ LIKE A PASS, and this one nearly did.** Removing the fallback turns six failures into six skips, and `libtest` captures `println!`/`eprintln!` and replays them only for a FAILING test — invisible in precisely the run that needs them. MEASURED rather than assumed, with a one-test `rustc --test` probe: a write through the `std::io::stderr()` HANDLE escapes the capture and the macros do not (`PROBE-direct-stderr-handle` printed, `test result: ok. 1 passed`, the two macro lines absent). `support::skip_without_browser` uses the handle, so an ordinary `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse` prints six lines naming what went unqualified and the command that qualifies it.
- ⭐ **THE `--no-fail-fast` DECISION, TAKEN — on `.11.4.7.2.2`'s priced census rather than on preference.** Default fail-fast reaches **11** of 94 test binaries and leaves `cli`, `core`, `node` and `server` UNKNOWN; `--no-fail-fast` reaches **94** — 102 suites ok / 1 failed, 815 passed / 1 failed — for **319.3 s** of test execution, one suite being 135.23 s of it. ⛔ The cost of knowing is not extra failures; it is that a RED run now pays full price instead of stopping early. A command whose job is to answer *is the workspace green* cannot answer it from 11 binaries, so `--no-fail-fast` is adopted in `make test` and in the `rust.yml` workspace command — the two places that run the whole workspace — and nowhere else. ⚠️ The number is one leaf old and its producing command is recorded, so it is REUSED rather than re-derived; this line says so instead of implying a fresh measurement.
- ⛔ **The book had already said it, and a sentence is not a mechanism.** `docs/book/src/deployment.md` carried *"Direct Cargo commands bypass this setup and do not establish pinned-runtime coverage by themselves"* — correct, written down, and toothless while the fallback made a direct run look identical to a qualified one. The chapter now states the enforced behaviour instead of advising against the bypass.
- ⛔ **NOT claimed:** that desktop Chrome is unsupported, or that the escaped-helper behaviour is repaired. The production worker's own discovery in `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs` is deliberately UNCHANGED — a deployment runs the browser its host provides, and narrowing that is `.7.3.2`'s decision, not a test harness's.
- Verification: the QUALIFIED path, `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py python3 -B scripts/ci_browser.py -- cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --locked --no-fail-fast`, returns rc=0 with `test result: ok. 8 passed` and `test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed`, zero skips, and `ci-browser: completed; evidence target/ci-browser/mac-arm64-_sj06d0w`. The UNQUALIFIED path, `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --locked` with the variable unset, returns rc=0 with 8 + 17 passed and six `SKIP (R3_BROWSER_BIN unset): …` lines on the terminal of a CAPTURED run. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-browse --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0 (10m16s, under the competing build above). ⚠️ **The FULL-workspace qualified run did NOT complete, and that is recorded rather than smoothed over**: `make test` reached **78 of ~94 test binaries with zero failures** and was then cut off by `ci_browser.py`'s own `COMMAND_SECONDS = 3600` cap — `ci-browser: refused: Command [...] timed out after 3600 seconds`, `make: *** [test] Error 2`. ⛔ So the acceptance clause *`cargo test --all --locked` reaches every crate afterwards* is **NOT met by a single run**, and stitching it to `.11.4.7.2.2`'s 94-binary result would be exactly what `knowledge/an-aborted-run-is-not-a-partial-pass` forbids. A completed run is owned by `.11.4.8`, which this leaf opened.
- **FALSIFIED, and the arm is the one that proves this is not suppression:** with the repair in place, naming the desktop browser explicitly still fails — `R3_BROWSER_BIN=/Applications/Google Chrome.app/…` gives rc=101, the same assertion at `browser_roundtrip.rs:582`, `cleanup_confirmed: false`, `browser stderr completion unconfirmed`, 41.07 s. The control still measures the property and still refuses the runtime it was never qualified against; what changed is that nobody selects that runtime by accident. Positive control: the qualified run above, rc=0.
- promotion: PROMOTED — `docs/knowledge/a-pin-a-second-path-can-bypass-is-not-a-pin.md` (the transferable half: a harness that DISCOVERS its dependency is not running the pinned one, and a skip announced through a captured channel reads as a pass) plus `docs/decisions/2026-09-15_test-browser-runtime-is-named-not-discovered.md` (this repository's rule and the numbers behind it).

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.8 — The only qualified browser path does not fit its own deadline on this machine

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2.4`, which made `make test` the ONLY way to qualify a browser control and then watched what that costs.
- 🔴 **AND THE FIRST RUN AFTER THAT CHANGE WAS CUT OFF, which is how this leaf stopped being about bandwidth alone.** `make test` reached **78 of ~94 test binaries with ZERO failures** and then died at `ci_browser.py`'s own `COMMAND_SECONDS = 3600` cap: `ci-browser: refused: Command [...] timed out after 3600 seconds`, `make: *** [test] Error 2`. ⛔ **A gate that cannot finish reports nothing**, and this is the ONLY path that can now qualify a browser control.
- **Censused rather than asserted: this is the FIRST timeout in the harness's history here.** Of 16 `target/ci-browser/*/browser.json` receipts, 12 read `completed exit=0`, 3 read `completed exit=101` (real test failures) and exactly 1 reads `failed … TimeoutExpired` — this run.
- ⛔ **NOT attributable to `--no-fail-fast`, and the argument is stated rather than assumed.** Fail-fast stops at a FAILURE; with zero failures in the 78 binaries that ran, both settings do identical work. ⚠️ That is reasoning, not a measurement, and this leaf owns measuring it — the honest reading is that the flag is not exonerated until a completed run exists with and without it.
- **What IS measured about the cost, from this project's own records:** macOS validates each freshly written executable on its FIRST run at about **21.9 s** apiece on this volume against 0.15 s on the boot volume (`.11.4.3.1.2.15`), and this run compiled every test binary from cold — roughly 34 minutes of validation before a single assertion. On top of that, a competing release build from another repository held a core at 98.8% for the entire run.
- **The finding, read from the source rather than timed once.** `scripts/ci_browser.py::execute` downloads `archive.zip` on EVERY invocation — `PINNED_ARCHIVES["mac-arm64"]` is **191,016,009 bytes** — extracts it member by member with size and link validation, verifies the executable's version, and on success `shutil.rmtree(runtime)` plus `archive.unlink()` retire the payload. So a second run repeats the whole acquisition. ⭐ The retirement is DELIBERATE and correct as a containment property (`.11.4.3.1.2.5`: each call owns its download; a failure retains it for inspection); what has never been priced is its recurring cost now that it sits on the only qualified path.
- ⚠️ **Measured incidentally, not as a census**: one invocation this session had reached 154 MB of 191 MB after roughly two minutes. `du -sh target/ci-browser/` returns **2.2 G** across **16** workspaces — twelve retired theirs and occupy 8.0 K each, while **three retained failures keep 542 M apiece** (the archive AND the extracted runtime, not the archive alone, which is why a first estimate of ~573 M was low by a factor of three).
- ⛔ **The tension is real and must not be resolved by removing the verification.** The pin's value is that the bytes are hash-checked on the path that uses them; a cached runtime that nothing re-verifies is a different guarantee wearing the same name. ⚠️ `.11.5`'s constraint applies directly: a gate people route around is a gate that lies, and a two-minute download in front of every browser control is exactly the shape people route around — which is how the fallback this leaf's parent deleted came to matter in the first place.
- Owns: a COMPLETED qualified workspace run and the deadline that admits it — whether `COMMAND_SECONDS` rises, whether `make test` passes its own `--timeout`, or whether the workspace run is tiered so the browser harness wraps only the suites that need a browser; pricing the acquisition (download, extraction, version check) as three separate numbers rather than one; deciding whether a repository-local verified cache keyed by the recorded SHA-256 preserves the property the per-call download provides, including what re-verification a cache hit must still perform; and the disposition of the three retained failure payloads, against `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py`'s precedent of measuring before retiring.
- Acceptance: one COMPLETED `cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` under the pinned runtime, with its binary count, pass/fail totals and wall-clock recorded, and the deadline change that admitted it named; the three phase timings recorded from at least two runs; an explicit statement of which property the per-call download provides and whether a verified cache provides the same one or a weaker one, named either way; a decision taken with its reason; and, if a cache is adopted, a falsification showing a corrupted or substituted cached payload is refused.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0203.
- ✅ **THE COMPLETED RUN EXISTS, AND IT IS GREEN.** `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py python3 -B scripts/ci_browser.py --timeout 7200 -- cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` returns rc=**0** with `ci-browser: completed; evidence target/ci-browser/mac-arm64-_kx2kgdt`: **94 test binaries plus 9 doc-test targets — 103 suites, 816 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored**, in `real 30m15.757s`.
- ⭐ **The arithmetic against `.11.4.7.2.2` is exact, which is what makes it checkable.** That run measured **815 passed / 1 failed** over the same 94 binaries; this one measures **816 passed / 0 failed**. One test moved from failed to passed and nothing else moved — precisely `.11.4.7.2.4`'s control. ⛔ And **zero** `SKIP (R3_BROWSER_BIN unset)` lines appear, so the qualified path skips nothing: the 816 is full coverage, not coverage minus six.
- **THE THREE ACQUISITION PHASES, measured separately as the acceptance asked**, by watching `ci_browser.py`'s own fsynced receipt rather than by instrumenting the script under measurement:

  | phase | elapsed | what it moved |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | download | 51.54 s | 191,016,009 bytes at about 3.7 MB/s |
  | extract + binary SHA-256 | 0.63 s | 675 entries, 5 links, 375,683,518 expanded bytes |
  | version check | 1.86 s | one execution of the binary, output compared to the pinned version string |
  | **acquisition total** | **55.27 s** | from process start to the first test |

  ⚠️ The extraction figure is fast enough to deserve its limit stated: the writes land in the page cache rather than on the platter, so 0.63 s is the cost the RUN pays, not a durable-write measurement.
- ⛔ **SO THE CACHE IS REFUSED, and the number is the whole argument.** Acquisition is **55.27 s of a 1,872 s run — 3.0%** — and 93% of that is the download. **The property the per-call download provides**: these exact bytes, fetched from the pinned origin and hash-checked by THIS process on THIS invocation. **What a cache would provide**: bytes verified on some earlier invocation, re-hashed on the hit — nearly the same guarantee, but trusting the local filesystem between runs instead of re-fetching. ⚠️ Nearly is not the same, and the price of the difference is **52 seconds**. A containment property is not worth trading for 3%.
- ⭐ **THE DEADLINE IS THE REAL DEFECT, and it is fixed in two places rather than by raising a number.** (1) `make test` and `.github/workflows/rust.yml` now run `cargo test --all --locked --no-run` BEFORE entering the browser harness, so its deadline bounds test EXECUTION rather than a compile. (2) Both pass `--timeout 5400` for the workspace run, leaving `COMMAND_SECONDS = 3600` as the script's default for the crate-scoped invocations the book documents, which finish in 31 s.
- ⚠️ **The cold path is NOT re-measured, and the leaf says so rather than implying otherwise.** 5400 rests on TWO observations — a warm run executing in 1,816.78 s, and a cold run cut off at 78 of 94 binaries by the 3600 s cap — not on a third run from a wiped `target/`. ⛔ The remaining cost inside the harness on a cold tree is macOS validating each freshly written executable on its FIRST run, about 21.9 s apiece here (`.11.4.3.1.2.15`), which `--no-run` does NOT move because validation happens at execution. ⭐ **The instrument that will actually settle it is the remote runner** — a cold Linux checkout with no such validation cost — which is blocker **C1**.
- **The retained payloads, censused before retiring, on `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py`'s precedent.** `du -sh target/ci-browser/` measured **2.2 G** across 16 workspaces: 12 had retired their own payload (8.0 K each) and **4 retained 542 M apiece**. ⛔ `mac-arm64-0281kcb0` is KEPT because `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/extraction-fixture-ownership.md:18` says in tracked text that it "remains preserved" — deleting it would make a committed sentence false. The other three were retired to **8.0 K** each, keeping `browser.json` and `version.log`: each receipt carries `archive_sha256` and `binary_sha256`, so the payload is byte-reproducible from the pin, and the receipt was the evidence all along. `target/ci-browser/` now measures **542 M**.
- promotion: declined. The transferable half — that a deadline should bound the phase it is about, and that a cost is priced as a RATIO against the run it sits in — is already carried by `docs/knowledge/a-census-is-an-instrument-not-a-table` and by `TOOLBOX.md`'s slow-gate section, which this leaf applied rather than extended.
- Verification: the completed run above, rc=0, 816 passed / 0 failed. `make gate` 18 checks rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make -n test` expands to the three steps in order. ⛔ No Rust source changed in this leaf — the diff is two build-command files and a task tree.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0203 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.8): the qualified run finishes, and the deadline now bounds what it is about`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.1 — The doctrine registry is data, so it must not be executable

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0094.
- Reproduce: each registry entry is a bash DOUBLE-quoted string, so backticks in a description are command substitution. The description added in REPAIR-0092 contained them, and the enforcer printed `line 36: - : command not found` and `line 36: pending: command not found` while rendering that description with the backticked words silently MISSING — bash had executed them and substituted the empty result.
- Why the instance fix was not enough: REPAIR-0092 removed the backticks and censused the other rows, but left the trap armed. Every other doctrine description in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` uses backticks, so copying one into the registry is the natural next move, and the only symptom is stderr noise plus words vanishing from a description nobody re-reads.
- The half that matters more than the output damage: the driver **executes** whatever a description contains, in the pre-commit hook and in CI. Today it ran `- Status:` and `pending` and got "command not found". A description carrying `$(...)` would be run the same way.
- Fix: a self-guard at the top of `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` that reads its own SOURCE TEXT and refuses a backtick, `$(`, `${` or a bare `$` inside the registry block, placed BEFORE the array assignment — the only placement that prevents the execution rather than reporting it afterwards.
- Verification: 15 checks green. FALSIFIED by reintroducing the exact original text — the guard exits 1, names line 12 and the offending entry, and no check runs; restoring the repair returns `=== all doctrines green ===`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0094 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.1): refuse shell expansion in the doctrine registry`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.2 — A LOCKSTEP box may not claim a document the commit does not touch

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0099. The census was decisive, and the check it specified now enforces it.
- Reproduce: commit `6bf0c40` (REPAIR-0092) carries a ticked LOCKSTEP box naming `MEMORY.md` and `LIVE_STATUS.md`, and staged neither. Cause chain: a scripted multi-edit hit a failed `assert`, the script exited non-zero, the compound command ran `git add -A && git commit` regardless, and `-A` staged whatever partial state existed. The commit succeeded with a checklist box that was false.
- Why `TASK-ACCEPTANCE` cannot catch it: that gate proves the box is TICKED and CITES something re-runnable. It does not and cannot prove the cited edit landed. This is the complementary half.
- census, run before proposing any rule, because the obvious rule is wrong: over the last 25 commits, 10 close a leaf, and of those `CHANGELOG.md` is staged 10/10 but `MEMORY.md` only 6/10, `LIVE_STATUS.md` 7/10 and `DEV_NOTES.md` 7/10. A blanket "closing a leaf must stage MEMORY" would assert a rule the project does not follow, would flag four pre-existing commits, and would not even catch `6bf0c40`, which did stage `CHANGELOG.md`.
- census of the rule that DOES hold: of the 6 commits in that window adding a `**LOCKSTEP**` bullet naming a core live document, exactly **one — `6bf0c40`, this session's own — named a document it did not stage**. Zero false positives across the rest. Keying the gate on the author's own CLAIM rather than on a blanket requirement is what makes it sound: a leaf that does not claim `MEMORY.md` is not required to stage it.
- Owns: `scripts/check_lockstep_claim.sh`, staged-diff-scoped like `TASK-ACCEPTANCE` and `TABLE-ARITY-RATCHET` — for each staged `docs/tasks/*.md`, take the ADDED lines containing `**LOCKSTEP**`, and require every core live document named there to be in the staged set. Register it and mirror it in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`.
- Known false-positive shape, to handle honestly rather than guess at: a box naming a document in order to say it is UNCHANGED. Prose negation detection is fragile, so follow the `GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS` precedent and provide an explicit escape in the same section — `lockstep: <doc> unchanged (<why>)` — rather than parsing intent.
- Acceptance: the check must FAIL against `6bf0c40`'s staged shape and PASS against `c6a843f`'s, and its `--self-test` must prove both directions.
- Fix: `scripts/check_lockstep_claim.sh`, registered as `LOCKSTEP-CLAIM` and mirrored in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`. Staged-diff-scoped over `docs/tasks/*.md`: for each ADDED line carrying a bold `**LOCKSTEP**` bullet, every core live document named on it must be in the changed set. The claim shape is the BOLD bullet, so narrative that merely reports on a past box — `c6a843f`'s two "its LOCKSTEP box overstated" lines — is not a claim about this commit and is deliberately not matched.
- The document list is COMMIT.md's root live documents (`README.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`). `docs/decisions/` and `docs/book/` are directories a box names by area rather than by file, and `KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md` is derived with its own gate. The `--self-test` re-checks that every listed name still appears in COMMIT.md, so the list cannot drift silently away from the document it was taken from.
- The escape is the `GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS` precedent rather than prose parsing: `lockstep: <doc> unchanged (<why>)` in the claim's own heading section. The refusal text says explicitly that deleting the document's NAME is not a discharge — the name is the claim, and removing it hides the decision instead of recording it.
- A third mode beyond the gate and the self-test: `--against <sha>` re-runs the predicate over any past commit, which is what makes this leaf's acceptance literally executable rather than argued.
- Verification: `--self-test` passes (2 claim shapes matched, 2 narrative lines ignored, 3 naming cases including a nested path and a longer filename, the escape both ways, 5 documents confirmed in COMMIT.md). The acceptance runs as stated: `--against 6bf0c40` FAILS, naming `docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md:2284` and both `MEMORY.md` and `LIVE_STATUS.md`; `--against c6a843f` passes. `make gate` prints `=== all doctrines green ===` with 16 checks.
- census re-run with the FINISHED gate, widened from the 25-commit window the rule was designed on: over the last 30 commits, 11 add a bold LOCKSTEP claim and were therefore genuinely exercised — 10 pass and exactly one, `6bf0c40`, breaches. Zero false positives. The remaining 19 pass vacuously because they add no claim, and that distinction is recorded so "30 green" is not mistaken for 30 tests.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0099 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.2): gate a LOCKSTEP box against the commit it claims`.
