#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.8.1 — The route census's key collapses two routes into one, and misses a third

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.4.4` (REPAIR-0254), which added a route and asked this instrument whether the book documented it (§15: found while working, not left unowned).
- **The mechanism, one function.** `stem()` deletes every `{param}` and squeezes the resulting `//`:
  `re.sub(r"\{[^}]*\}", "", route).replace("//", "/").rstrip("/")`. `classify()` then asks whether `"<METHOD> <stem>"` appears in the book.
- 🔴 **DEFECT 1 — a FALSE `described`, and it is the dangerous direction.** `/v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` and `/v1/snapshots` BOTH stem to `/v1/snapshots`. The book's `POST /v1/snapshots` (the SUBMIT route, `deployment.md:576`) therefore satisfies the ITEM route's check, so `/v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` is counted **described by a line documenting a different route**. Every collection/item pair in the surface has this shape.
- 🔴 **DEFECT 2 — a FALSE `absent`.** A parameter in the MIDDLE of a path leaves a stem no book ever writes: `/v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/derivations` → `/v1/snapshots/derivations`. The book names it as `GET /v1/snapshots/{id}/derivations` at `deployment.md:584` and the census reports it ABSENT. Same for `…/assessments` and the new `…/tombstone`.
- ⛔ **So the headline is wrong in BOTH columns** — `described` is inflated by defect 1 and `absent` by defect 2 — and `.11.8` published its counts as a measured backlog. Neither number is a floor for attention in the direction it claims. ⚠️ **Which figures belong to whom, because REPAIR-0254's opening note conflated them and that is corrected here:** `.11.8` published **103 routes — 22 described, 1 mentioned, 80 absent**; `35 / 1 / 68` is what the DEFECTIVE instrument reports over TODAY's larger corpus. A number needs its producer AND its moment (`a-restated-number-needs-a-producer`).
- ⭐ This is `docs/knowledge/a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance.md` and `a-census-is-as-wide-as-its-key.md` in one function, in an instrument whose own leaf's transferable lesson was *check an instrument's first number against one obtained a DIFFERENT way*. The cross-check that leaf ran compared TOTALS, which both defects survive.
- ⚠️ The self-test passed throughout and claims "parameters stripped" as one of its four sides. It asserts the stripping HAPPENS; it never asserts the stripped form matches how a book writes a route, nor that two routes keep distinct keys. `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason`.
- Owns: a key that distinguishes a collection from its item and matches the book's own `{id}` spelling; the corrected three-class census re-derived rather than patched; self-test arms that fire on BOTH defects; and `.11.8`'s published numbers restated from the corrected instrument, or explicitly withdrawn.
- Acceptance: both defects reproduced by name against the real book before the repair; a key whose two directions are each asserted (a collection and its item classify separately; a mid-path parameter matches the book's spelling); the corrected counts published with the old ones named as superseded; and the self-test seen RED under a mutant restoring each defect.
- ✅ **BOTH DEFECTS RE-DERIVED BY HAND against the real book, not merely by the instrument.** Defect 1: `/v1/calls` was counted `described` by `GET /v1/calls/{call_id}` at `docs/book/src/authority.md:833` — a contract line for the ITEM route crediting the COLLECTION — and `grep -rnoE "(GET|POST|…) /v1/calls($|[^/{_a-zA-Z0-9-])" docs/book/src/*.md` returns **nothing**, so the collection really is undocumented. `/v1/policy-publications` was credited the same way by `POST /v1/policy-publications/{id}/publish` (`cli.md:20`). Defect 2: the book writes `GET /v1/snapshots/{id}/derivations` at `deployment.md:584`, and the old key asked for `/v1/snapshots/derivations`.
- ✅ **THE REPAIR: normalise, do not delete.** `route_key` rewrites every `{whatever}` to `{}` on BOTH sides, so a key matches the book's own spelling and two different routes keep different keys. A right match edge (`(?![\w/{-])`) stops `/v1/snapshots` matching inside `GET /v1/snapshots/{}`.
- ⛔ **NO LEFT EDGE, and that is measured rather than assumed.** It would guard a short route matching inside a longer one — a population this surface has **0** of — and it costs a real answer: `authority.md:375` shows `curl -i "$RB_URL/v1/admin/grants"`, whose preceding `L` would make a route the book plainly shows read `absent`. That is the same under-reporting this leaf removes. ⭐ The assumption is not left in a comment: `tail_collisions()` PRINTS the count every run, so the day a route's key becomes another's tail the reader is told a left edge is needed instead of quietly getting a wrong number.
- ✅ **THE CORRECTED COUNTS, and the old ones superseded APPLES-TO-APPLES.** Today's corpus: **104 product routes — 49 described, 3 mentioned, 52 absent** (was 35 / 1 / 68 from the defective key; **21 of 104 misclassified** — 18 wrongly `absent`, 3 wrongly credited as documented). ⭐ And at `.11.8`'s OWN commit `0fbb85f`, measured in a throwaway on-volume worktree with only the key replaced: **103 routes — 30 described, 3 mentioned, 70 absent**, against its published **22 / 1 / 80**. So that leaf under-reported the documentation by 8 and over-stated the gap by 10, at the moment it published.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED FIVE WAYS, each red by name.** (1) the old deleting key restored → four arms red including both collection/item directions and the mid-path arm; (2) the right edge removed → `THE COLLECTION WAS CREDITED TO THE ITEM'S LINE`; (3) the left edge reinstated → `a route behind a variable prefix was not seen`; (4) `tail_collisions` returning `[]` → `missed a key that is the tail of another`; (5) its predicate always true → `reported a collision between unrelated routes`. ⚠️ A sixth attempt was a BAD MUTANT of mine — `return [] or sorted(...)` evaluates to the sorted list — and it is recorded rather than counted, because a mutant that changes nothing proves nothing.
- ⛔ **The self-test's old third arm ASSERTED THE DEFECT**: `stem("/v1/calls/{call_id}/respond") == "/v1/calls/respond"`, codifying a key no book ever writes as the correct answer. That is why the defect survived its own control, and it is the sharpest instance of `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason` this tree has: not a control that could not see the defect, but one that demanded it.
- Routed OUT: none. ⛔ Still NOT claimed, and `.11.8`'s limit stands unchanged: 52 is not 52 defects, `described` remains a proxy (a contract line is not proof the description is correct), and no gate is proposed — `.11.6`'s reasoning is untouched by a better key.
- NO REGRESSION: no Rust, schema or migration changed. The instrument is read-only and the other 83 routes classify as before.
- lockstep: `README.md` unchanged; `LIVE_STATUS.md`'s `.11.8` paragraph carries the supersession with both producers named; the book documents no census numbers, so it needs no edit.
- promotion: declined for a new record — `docs/knowledge/a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance.md` and `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason.md` both already state this, and `.11.20.2`'s criterion makes a third file absorb-or-decline. ⭐ Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md` with the one addition those notes lack: a key can be too loose and too TIGHT in the same expression.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0255`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.23 — The scaffold ships an enforcer that registers checks it does not carry

- Opened: `pending` 2026-09-18, measuring the spine this project shares with its template `rdje/bedrock` after the director named improving that template as the agent network's first workload (§15: found while answering, not left unowned).
- 🔴 **THE DEFECT** — ⚠️ *the headline below overstated it and is corrected at the foot of this leaf: a project is instantiated from a GitHub TEMPLATE, which copies everything, so creation is not affected. The real hazard is at UPDATE time for a project built from an older snapshot.* As first written: a project that pulls this spine cannot commit. `scripts/update_scaffold.sh` carries `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` in its `NEUTRAL` list — the registry of 18 doctrines — but **not the 7 check scripts that registry names**. Copying only the 29 `NEUTRAL` paths into a fresh `git init` repository and running the enforcer there prints seven `?? (missing/not executable: …)` rows and `=== 10 doctrine breach(es) — commit blocked ===`.
- **The seven, by command** (`NEUTRAL` parsed from the script, registrations parsed from the enforcer array): `HEADING-DEPTH`, `TASK-STATUS`, `LOCKSTEP-CLAIM`, `INDEX-FRONTIER`, `FRONTIER-STATUS`, `RUST-FORMATTING`, `SELF-TEST`. `NEUTRAL` carries 29 paths of which 15 are check scripts; the enforcer registers 18.
- ⭐ **ROOT CAUSE, and it is a shape this tree has now met four times: `NEUTRAL` is a SECOND COPY of a fact the registry owns, and nothing derives it.** `INDEX-FRONTIER` is the index's copy of the frontier; `FRONTIER-STATUS` is a row's copy of a leaf's status; this is the scaffold's copy of the doctrine registry. Each drifted the moment the first copy grew.
- ⚠️ **It drifted in exactly the direction that hurts.** Every one of the seven was EARNED here, each by a measured defect — and the list they are missing from is the only mechanism that moves them anywhere. So the spine's improvements accumulate in the instance and cannot leave it.
- ⛔ **The backflow half is NOT this leaf's and must not be pretended into it.** `update_scaffold.sh` pulls downstream only; `rdje/bedrock` is the root template and has no upstream to pull from, so carrying a doctrine UP is manual work owned by a `BEDROCK-MAINTENANCE` leaf in that repository. This leaf makes the seven TRANSPORTABLE; it does not transport them.
- Owns: adding the seven to `NEUTRAL`, and a check that `NEUTRAL` covers every script the registry names — so the class cannot recur, here or in any project that adopts the spine.
- Acceptance: the fresh-repo reproduction re-run and green; a gate that fails when a registered check is absent from `NEUTRAL`, seen RED against a deliberately unlisted script and measured against the enforcer's cost; the conditional registrations (`KNOWLEDGE-MAP`, `PROJECT-SPECIFIC`) handled explicitly rather than by accident; and the count stated as a producer command rather than a number.
- ✅ **THE FIX, and the reproduction re-run.** The seven scripts join `NEUTRAL`, and `scripts/check_scaffold_coverage.sh` now fails when the registry names a check the list does not carry. Re-running the fresh-repo reproduction — 37 `NEUTRAL` paths into a bare `git init` — prints **zero `??` rows**, against seven before. ⚠️ Four breaches remain there and none is a scaffold defect: `MEMORY-ARCH`, `README-STABILITY` and `KNOWLEDGE-MAP` have no content to check in an empty project, which is correct behaviour, and the fourth is named below.
- 🔴 **THE GATE FAILED ITS OWN REPRODUCTION, and that is the useful part.** `SCAFFOLD-COVERAGE` was the fourth breach, because `scripts/update_scaffold.sh` is deliberately ABSENT from its own `NEUTRAL` list — a sync script that overwrites itself mid-run is its own hazard — so a project created by `bootstrap.sh` has one and a project that only pulled `NEUTRAL` may not. With no scaffold there is nothing to cover, which is **NOT CHECKED**, never a pass and never a breach. ⭐ Found by running the gate in the very reproduction it was written to validate, not by reading it.
- 🔴 **AND FALSIFICATION FOUND THE GATE'S OWN GUARD DEAD.** Mutating the `$EXEMPT` filter away changed nothing: the parser anchored on `^[[:space:]]*"` and so never saw the CONDITIONAL `DOCTRINES+=("…")` form, which is how `KNOWLEDGE-MAP` and `PROJECT-SPECIFIC` are registered. The exemption was unreachable code protecting nothing. The parser now matches both forms explicitly and the mutant is red by name.
- ⚠️ **Widening that parser then over-matched, which is the third instance of one lesson today.** Dropping the anchor entirely matched the registry's own explanatory comment — `Each entry: "ID|what it proves|relative/path/to/check.sh"` — and reported that placeholder as an uncarried check. A comment is not a registration; the two real shapes are matched by name. `a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance`, after `.11.8.1` and `.11.22` in the same session.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED FOUR WAYS, each red by name:** a registered script dropped from `NEUTRAL` (names it); the `$EXEMPT` filter removed (now names `check_doctrines.project.sh`, which a template must not carry); a missing scaffold turned back into a breach (the NOT-CHECKED arm fires); and both parsers asserted against known inputs so a silently empty set cannot pass anything.
- ✅ **Cost: 0.02 s** against a ~12.6 s enforcer, measured three runs. Registered as doctrine 16 of 21.
- ⛔ **The backflow is still manual and this leaf does not pretend otherwise.** `update_scaffold.sh` pulls downstream only, and `rdje/bedrock` is the root template with nothing to pull from. What changed is that the seven are now TRANSPORTABLE and the class cannot silently recur; carrying them UP is a `BEDROCK-MAINTENANCE` leaf in that repository.
- 🔎 **Recorded rather than fixed:** `scripts/update_scaffold.sh` is not in its own `NEUTRAL`, so a downstream project's copy of the sync script never ages forward. That may be deliberate self-modification safety or may be a gap; it is the TEMPLATE's call, not an instance's, and it is stated here for whoever owns that decision.
- Routed OUT: none.
- NO REGRESSION: no Rust, schema, migration or route changed. `NEUTRAL` grew by 8 paths and lost none; the enforcer gains one check.
- lockstep: `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` gains the `SCAFFOLD-COVERAGE` row; `README.md` and the book are unchanged, as neither documents the scaffold's file list.
- promotion: declined for a new record — this is the fourth instance of *a second copy nothing derives*, which `.7.2.9`'s promoted shape and `a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance` already carry between them. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- 🔴 **CORRECTED 2026-09-18 by the director, one commit after closing: THE SEVERITY CLAIM WAS WRONG AND THE REPRODUCTION MODELLED A PATH THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** This leaf said *"a project that pulled this spine could not make its first commit"* and reproduced it by copying only the `NEUTRAL` paths into a bare `git init`. **Projects are not created that way.** `rdje/bedrock` is a **GitHub template repository**, not a syncable remote: a new project is instantiated from it through GitHub's *Use this template*, which copies the WHOLE repository, and is then cloned and bootstrapped locally. Confirmed in this repository's own history — `b932c05 "Initial commit"` (the template instantiation) then `823c2bc "bootstrapped from bedrock"` — and by its remotes: **reasonbraid's remote set contains no bedrock entry** — `origin` is `rdje/reasonbraid` and nothing else. ⚠️ bedrock of course has its OWN `origin` (`rdje/bedrock.git`), which is how the template itself is maintained; what is absent is a link FROM an instantiated project BACK to the template.
- ⛔ **So a fresh project receives every script and commits fine.** The bare-repo reproduction was a model of a creation path nobody uses, and its `10 doctrine breach(es) — commit blocked` measured my own fixture rather than the product.
- ✅ **WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and why the repair still stands.** `update_scaffold.sh` is an UPDATE mechanism for an EXISTING project, and it only copies the listed files — it deletes nothing (`grep -nE "rm -|delete|prune"` over it returns nothing outside the scratch trap). `NEUTRAL` carried `check_doctrines.sh` and not the 7 scripts that registry names, so running it against a project instantiated from an OLDER template snapshot would install a registry naming checks that never arrive and break THAT project's gate. A real hazard, at update time, for an older project — not at creation, and not for a fresh one.
- ⚠️ **The corrected severity, stated plainly:** the defect is *the update mechanism cannot deliver the doctrines the registry names*, not *the spine ships broken*. `SCAFFOLD-COVERAGE` is still worth its 0.02 s on that basis — registry-versus-list drift is silent and only bites the project being updated — but it is a consistency guard, not a shipped-broken guard.
- ⭐ **The root-cause finding is untouched:** `NEUTRAL` is a second copy of the registry that nothing derives, the fourth instance of that shape, and it had drifted by seven. That is what the gate fixes and it needed fixing.
- 🔎 **The method failure worth keeping, because it is the leaf's real lesson:** I built a fixture, reproduced a failure in it, and reported the fixture's behaviour as the product's. **A reproduction is only evidence if the path it models is one that occurs** — and I never checked how a project is actually created before asserting that creation was broken. `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md`'s falsify leg asks what would have to be true for the claim to be FALSE; here it was *"projects are created some other way"*, and one question to the director settled it.
- Status: `done`; severity corrected by `REASONBRAID-DOC-0055`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0259`; correction `REASONBRAID-DOC-0055`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.22 — A frontier row's status is a second copy of a leaf's Status line, and nothing relates them

- Opened: `pending` by the frontier correction that followed REPAIR-0256 (§15: the symptom was fixed by hand, so the gap is owned rather than left to recur).
- 🔴 **THE GAP, and it has already fired TWICE in two days.** A frontier row carries a leaf id and a status column. The leaf carries its own `- Status:` line. **0 of the 10 tracked scripts that mention a frontier relate the two**, censused below rather than asserted.
- **THE CENSUS, by command.** `git grep -lni "frontier" -- scripts .githooks knowledge-map` returns **10** scripts. Classifying each by whether it is row-aware AND reads a leaf `Status:` line leaves **2 candidates**, and hand-checking both — because a loose key is what `.11.8.1` had just been about — shows **neither relates them**:

  ```bash
  git grep -lni "frontier" -- scripts .githooks knowledge-map     # -> 10 scripts
  grep -n "Order | Leaf" scripts/check_task_status.sh             # -> 0: it never reads the table
  grep -n "cat >" scripts/bootstrap.sh                            # -> 4: a template writer, not a check
  ```

  `check_task_status.sh` matched only because its own SELF-TEST FIXTURES contain the strings `- Status: \`pending\`` and `- Status: \`done\`` (lines 58–59); it counts `- Status:` lines per leaf and reads no table. `bootstrap.sh` matched because it WRITES `Status:` inside a heredoc when seeding a first tree. ⭐ Two false positives out of two candidates, from a key I wrote one commit after repairing a key defect of exactly this shape — recorded because it is the finding, not an aside.
  - REPAIR-0253 found **five** rows saying `pending` whose leaves said `done` (`.11.18`, `.11.17`, `.11.14.3.7`, `.11.14.3.5`, `.11.4.7.2`) and reconciled them by hand;
  - two commits later, row 1 — the frontier ITSELF, the single row a reader acts on — named `.7.4.5`, which has been `done` since REPAIR-0216. Discovered only by opening the leaf to work on it.
- ⛔ **Why the three gates that look adjacent all miss it, stated per gate so no one re-checks them:**
  - `INDEX-FRONTIER` compares `docs/TASK_TREE.md`'s Frontier column to the TREE's row 1. Both named `.7.4.5`; two files agreeing is exactly what it asks for, and it is silent when they agree about a closed leaf.
  - `TASK-STATUS` requires exactly ONE `- Status:` line per leaf. It reads leaves, never tables.
  - `TABLE-ARITY-RATCHET` reads cell COUNTS, never cell meaning.
  ⭐ So the defect lives precisely in the seam between three checks that each do their own job correctly — the `.7.2.9` shape, one layer up.
- ⚠️ **The dangerous direction is row 1 specifically.** A stale `pending` on a historical row costs a reader a moment; a stale row 1 sends the next session to a leaf that closed, which is how REPAIR-0256's successor began. ⛔ **And the inverse must not be gated away:** a row deliberately naming a `done` leaf as HISTORY is correct and common — rows `1a11`–`1a18` are all `done`. The rule wanted is about row 1 and about the status COLUMN's agreement, not about the presence of closed leaves in the table.
- ⚠️ **A LEAF'S STATUS IS NOT ALWAYS IN A `Status:` LINE, and a rule written without this would be wrong on its first run.** Measured over the tree: **350 leaves, 28 carry no `- Status:` line, and 27 of those state it in their `Opened:` bullet** (`- Opened: \`pending\` by …`). The frontier's own row 1 is one of them — `.11.2.4` has no `Status:` line at all. ⛔ So `TASK-STATUS`'s "exactly ONE" permits zero, and any comparison must read BOTH forms or it will report 28 false disagreements and be switched off. Producing command:

  ```bash
  python3 -B -c 'import re,pathlib; s=pathlib.Path("docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md").read_text(); \
    h=list(re.finditer(r"^#{3,6} (SIGNOFF-REPAIR[\d.]*\d) — ", s, re.M)); \
    print(sum(1 for i,x in enumerate(h) if not re.search(r"^- Status: `", s[x.end():h[i+1].start() if i+1<len(h) else len(s)], re.M)))'
  ```
- Owns: deciding the exact rule (most likely: every row's status column equals its leaf's own status, read from a `Status:` line OR an `Opened:` bullet, and row 1's leaf is not `done`), measuring the corpus before proposing it (`.11.6`), and either registering a check or stating why prose is enough.
- ✅ **THE CENSUS, RUN BEFORE THE RULE, and it changed what the rule had to be.** Over the frontier table bounded to its contiguous pipe lines: **66 rows naming 49 distinct leaves — 13 leaves carry 2 to 4 rows each, and 10 rows' status columns disagree with their leaf.** ⭐ **That reveals a sharper root cause than "nothing compares them": the table gains a NEW row when a leaf closes and the OPENING row is never removed**, so a single leaf ends up with rows that contradict each other. `.11.14.3.10` had four rows, three of them stale. ⛔ And the defect caught its author in the act — `.11.21` had a `done` row at `1a18` and a `pending` row at `1a16`, both written by me two commits earlier in this same session.
- 🔴 **A THIRD HISTORICAL INSTANCE, found by the census rather than remembered:** `.11.15` records that `.7.4.1` "sat at Current Frontier row 2 for seven commits after it closed". With REPAIR-0253's five rows and row 1's own pointer, the founding population is **three separate firings**, not the two this leaf opened with.
- ⚠️ **Two false starts in the census itself, recorded because they are the same lesson twice.** `s.index("## Current Frontier")` matched an EARLIER prose mention of the phrase and censused a table 400 KB away, returning `0 rows`; anchoring to `^## Current Frontier$` fixed it. Then the slice ran to the next `## ` heading, sweeping in unrelated tables; bounding it to the CONTIGUOUS run of pipe lines fixed that. ⭐ Both are `a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance`, in the leaf immediately after the one that repaired a key defect of the same shape — which is the honest measure of how easy this mistake is.
- ✅ **THE RULE, with the `done`-as-history case explicitly permitted.** (1) every row's status column equals its leaf's own status; (2) row 1's leaf is not finished. ⛔ **It is NOT "no finished leaves in the table"** — most of the table is closed rows kept as recent history, and a rule banning them would condemn the corpus. What is refused is a row that LIES about its leaf, and a top-of-list pointer at work already done. A self-test arm asserts the legal `done` row directly, so the rule cannot drift into the stricter one.
- ✅ **Both status forms read.** 350 leaves, **28 carry no `Status:` line** and 27 of those state it in an `Opened:` bullet. A check reading only the first form would report 28 false disagreements — the shape that gets a gate switched off rather than fixed. `active` is a real third value (`.9.3.4`) and is not "finished".
- ✅ **THE RECONCILIATION.** 9 stale opening rows removed (each superseded by its own leaf's closing row, which is self-contained and richer) and 1 corrected in place (`.9.3.4` `pending` → `active`). The frontier table now agrees with every leaf it names.
- ✅ **Instrument: `scripts/check_frontier_status.py`, registered as `FRONTIER-STATUS`** — doctrine 16 of 20, **0.06 s** against a ~12.6 s enforcer. It reads every tracked tree, not only this one.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED FIVE WAYS plus the real defect.** Mutants: the `Opened:` fallback removed; `active` treated as finished; the row-1 rule removed; deferred (`—`) cells no longer skipped; rows read across a blank line — each red BY NAME on its own arm. ⭐ And against the REAL tree: reinstating `.11.21`'s stale row reproduces `row 1a16 says \`pending\`, but SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.21 says \`done\``, and pointing row 1 at a closed leaf reproduces `ROW 1 names SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.21, which is \`done\``. Both restored.
- ⛔ **NOT claimed:** that the frontier's ORDER is meaningful or checked, or that row 1 is the right next leaf. This checks agreement and the top-of-list, which is what drifted; whether row 1 is well chosen stays a judgement.
- Routed OUT: none.
- NO REGRESSION: no Rust, schema, migration or route changed. The 9 removed rows are duplicates whose leaves each retain a closing row; `INDEX-FRONTIER` still passes, and row 1 is unchanged.
- lockstep: `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` gains the `FRONTIER-STATUS` row; `README.md` and the book are unchanged, as neither documents the doctrine list.
- promotion: declined for a new record — `a-key-too-loose-returns-the-wrong-instance.md` already carries the census's two false starts, and the gate-seam observation is `.7.2.9`'s promoted shape one layer up. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0257`.
- Acceptance: a census of the whole frontier table naming every row whose status column disagrees with its leaf, run before any rule is written; the rule stated with the `done`-as-history case explicitly permitted; if registered, the gate seen RED against both a stale `pending` row and a row-1 pointer at a closed leaf, and its cost measured against the enforcer's ~12.6 s; and the two hand reconciliations above named as the founding population rather than a remembered anecdote.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.22.1 — The frontier may name one UNFINISHED leaf twice, and the note saying it was removed is what hides it

- Opened: `pending` by `.4.2.3.1`'s closure, which met the instance while reading the table it was about to rewrite (§15: the symptom is discharged by that closure, so the gap is owned rather than left to recur).
- 🔴 **The instance, measured across every tracked tree rather than noticed in one.** A census over the `## Current Frontier` table of all **15** tracked trees returns exactly **one** leaf carrying more than one UNFINISHED row: `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.2.3.1`, at rows **1** and **5**, both `pending`. Every other tree is clean, and this tree's other **6** repeated leaves are the legitimate opening-then-closing pattern.
- ⛔ **A duplicate row is NOT a defect in general, and `.11.22` is why** — its own census recorded *"66 rows naming 49 distinct leaves — 13 leaves carry 2 to 4 rows each"*, because a leaf legitimately gets an OPENING row and, later, a closing `done` row. The defect is narrower: **two rows for one leaf that has not finished**, which is the shape that invites a reader to work it twice or to read the second row as a different leaf.
- 🔴 **The recurrence is what makes this worth a leaf, and the caption is complicit.** The table already carries a note reading *"Row 5 is the ONLY entry left from the previous frontier's duplicated pair"* — true when written, after the pair had been collapsed to one row. A later commit promoted the same leaf to row 1, the pair came back, and the note went on saying it was gone. ⭐ A prose statement that a class of defect has been removed reads as a live guarantee; nothing re-derives it.
- ⛔ **Why `FRONTIER-STATUS` is silent, stated so nobody re-checks it:** `scripts/check_frontier_status.py` relates each row's status column to its leaf's own `Status:`/`Opened:` line. Both rows here said `pending` and the leaf said `pending`, so every row AGREED — the check does exactly its job and the defect is in a property it never asks about. Its own record says so: *"NOT claimed: that the frontier's ORDER is meaningful or checked"*. ⭐ The `.7.2.9` gate-seam shape, one layer up.
- Owns: deciding whether the rule ships as a further arm of `FRONTIER-STATUS` or is declined, **calibrated over history before it is proposed** (`.11.6`: no threshold before its population); and, either way, replacing the frontier caption's prose guarantee with something that re-derives, since a note nothing produces is `a-restated-number-needs-a-producer` in the document a reader resumes from.
- Acceptance: the calibration is run over this tree's whole history rather than a window, reporting how many commits the candidate would have blocked and how many of those carried a real unfinished duplicate; if registered, a falsification that restores a real historical duplicate and makes the gate name it; if declined, the reason recorded and the caption repaired anyway.
- Status: `pending`.
- Verification / commit: pending.


#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.21 — Unformatted Rust reached `main`, because nothing checks formatting per commit

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.4.4` (REPAIR-0254), whose own `cargo fmt --all -- --check` failed in a file it had not touched.
- **The instance.** `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/git.rs` fails `cargo fmt --all -- --check` at two sites (an over-split `||` chain near line 926 and an un-wrapped `assert!` near line 2060), in committed state, with the working tree clean of them. `git log -2 -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src/git.rs` names `22c81d7` (`.7.2.8`, REPAIR-0252) and `dc52286` (`.7.2.9`, REPAIR-0251); which of the two introduced each site is for this leaf to measure rather than assume.
- ⭐ **The mechanism is a POLICY GAP, not a lapse, which is why the leaf is about the gate and not only the file.** `CLAUDE.md` §16 routes the full CI to pre-push and the per-commit gate to `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` — and the enforcer's 18 checks contain no formatting check. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` appears only in `COMMIT.md`'s pre-push list. So unformatted Rust can sit on `main` for as many commits as pass between pushes, and here it did.
- ⚠️ **The cost is measured, not assumed, before any gate is proposed** (`.11.6`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check` links and executes nothing. If it is cheap against the 3.15 s enforcer it belongs in it; if not, the pre-push list is the right home and the honest repair is to say so.
- Owns: the two formatting sites; the measurement of the check's cost; and the decision about where it belongs, with its reason.
- Acceptance: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0 across the workspace; the check's cost measured and stated against the enforcer's; the placement decided with its rejected alternative; and if it is registered, the gate seen RED against a deliberately unformatted file.
- ✅ **THE TWO SITES REPAIRED.** `cargo fmt --all` rewrites `git.rs` alone — 5 insertions, 4 deletions — and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` then returns rc=0 across the workspace. ⚠️ Attribution left where it was found rather than guessed: the two sites arrived with REPAIR-0251/0252, and this leaf did not spend a bisect separating them, because the repair and the gate are the same for either.
- ✅ **THE COST, MEASURED BEFORE THE RULE WAS PROPOSED (`.11.6`).** Three runs each, warm, this machine: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` at **0.81 / 0.66 / 0.66 s**; `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` at **12.57 / 12.52 / 13.00 s**. So it adds about **5 %**, and `.11.5`'s constraint holds — nobody routes around two-thirds of a second. ⚠️ **A number corrected in passing:** the enforcer costs ~12.6 s, not the 3.15 s `.11.4.3.1.7.2` measured. That figure is not wrong, it is ANCHORED — the registry has grown since — and `check_self_tests.sh` already defends keeping it anchored rather than restating it. This leaf names the current one beside it rather than editing history.
- ✅ **REGISTERED, with its rejected alternative stated.** `RUST-FORMATTING` is doctrine 16 of 19 in the enforcer. ⛔ **Leaving it in the pre-push list was rejected, and on the evidence rather than on taste: that is precisely where it already was, and it is the arrangement that let the defect ship.** A check that runs once per ~300 commits cannot say WHICH commit broke formatting, so the thing being economised on is the cost of finding out.
- ⚠️ **WHOLE-WORKSPACE, not staged-scope, and the reason is this leaf's own instance.** The defect was in a file no staged change touched; a staged-scope check would not have found it and would not find the next one. That is affordable only because the workspace is formatted as of this commit — a strict check over pre-existing debt would have had to be a ratchet like `TABLE-ARITY`, and the leaf says so rather than leaving a future reader to rediscover it.
- ✅ **THE GATE SEEN RED, against real unformatted code.** `let  _deliberately = 1 ;` injected into `git.rs::expired` → `❌ RUST-FORMATTING … === 1 doctrine breach(es) — commit blocked ===`, naming `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/git.rs`. Restored byte-identical (`cmp`), and the gate returns to `=== all doctrines green ===` over 19 checks.
- ✅ **Its own `--self-test` is two-sided and reaches the TOOL, not just the verdict.** Both sides of the pure `formatting_verdict`, then a deliberately unformatted file that rustfmt must REFUSE and rustfmt's own output of that same file which it must ACCEPT — plus a `cmp` proving the two differ, so the refusal arm cannot be passing because the tool refuses everything. ⛔ An absent `rustfmt` FAILS the self-test rather than skipping it: a silent skip looks exactly like a pass (`a-guard-your-own-process-cannot-reach`'s closing rule, applied to a missing tool).
- 🔴 **AND THE REGISTRY'S OWN GUARD CAUGHT ME WHILE REGISTERING IT.** The description I first wrote spelled the command in backticks; each registry entry is a bash double-quoted string, so that is command substitution the driver would EXECUTE on every commit and in CI. `DOCTRINE-REGISTRY` refused the change by name before any commit was attempted. ⭐ `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` §*Adding a doctrine* documents exactly this trap, from a previous occurrence — the gate worked, and reading the section first would have worked too.
- ⛔ **NOT claimed:** that formatting is a correctness property, or that this would have caught anything else. It catches one class, cheaply, at the commit that causes it.
- Routed OUT: none.
- NO REGRESSION: the only Rust change is `cargo fmt`'s own rewrite of `git.rs`, which is behaviour-preserving by construction; `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` rc=0 and the workspace gate is green over 19 checks.
- lockstep: `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` gains the `RUST-FORMATTING` row (this file is the registry's human-readable mirror, and step 3 of *Adding a doctrine* requires it); `COMMIT.md`'s pre-push list keeps `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, now redundant but harmless, with a line saying the gate also runs it; `README.md` and the book are unchanged, because neither documents the doctrine list.
- promotion: declined for a new record — the transferable half (*measure a proposed gate's cost against the gate it joins, before proposing it*) is `.11.6`'s own rule and `TOOLBOX.md` carries it. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0256`.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.6 — A rule, threshold or severity proposed before its population is measured

- Opened: `pending`; raised from this session's own measured experience, not from a general principle someone liked.
- The observation: five times in one session, a rule/threshold/severity that was reasoned carefully from source was **changed by the first measurement of the population it quantified over**. This is distinct from `.11.5`'s accepted item (1), which requires a CONTROL to have failed on its defect; this is about the SHAPE of a rule before any control exists.
- The five instances, each with its own leaf and commit so the pattern is auditable rather than remembered:
  - `.11.4.5.2` (REPAIR-0099): the obvious "closing a leaf must stage `MEMORY.md`" would have asserted a rule the project does not follow (6/10), flagged four innocent commits, and still missed the defect. The census moved the rule's KEY to the author's own claim.
  - `.7.3.3.5.1` (REPAIR-0097): "narrow the advertised media types" was not merely worse, it was **unexpressible** — no subset of the advertisement is accepted, because the leg's rule is not format-shaped at all.
  - `.11.4.5.3` (REPAIR-0100): the preferred GENERATOR would have destroyed accurate curated prose in 13 of 14 rows, and blanket equality would have flagged `PHASE-8`'s legitimately different cell.
  - `.3.3.4.3.3.3.3.2.3.2` (REPAIR-0101): a deadline assertion of `< 75 s` for a 60 s bound failed at 75.03 s under load — the margin was measuring the host's scheduling, not the client's ceiling.
  - `.3.3.4.3.3.3.3.2.3.3` (REPAIR-0102): a severity routed out as "an inconsistency" turned out to put `authorization: Basic …` on the wire. The grade did not change; what was KNOWN about it did.
  - `.3.3.4.7.3` (REPAIR-0111): the stored refusal code was typed against the §9.8 registry so the record and the response could not disagree — the registry has no `not_found`, which is what the response actually returns. The obvious one-value patch was rejected by the same census that found the shape: **10** of the 19 emitted codes are absent from the registry, not one. A SIXTH instance, recorded while it was still warm, and the first one produced by this tree's own author one leaf after applying the discipline to an adjacent field.
- What is already covered, so this does not duplicate an existing gate: `GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS` enforces the census for one sentence shape — a "nothing checks X" claim. Four of the five instances above are outside that shape.
- census of that overlap, run with the GATE'S OWN predicate rather than by eye — extract `CLAIM_RE` from `scripts/check_gap_claims.sh` and count added task-tree lines matching it in each of the five commits: `1dbdb77` 0, `a21f7a5` 0, `bb52b4d` **1**, `179110b` 0, `2bec2ff` 0. So four of five add no sentence of that shape at all, and the one that does (`bb52b4d`) carried its census and passed. The existing gate is therefore not a duplicate of what this leaf is about, and that is measured rather than asserted — which the gate itself insisted on, by refusing this leaf's first draft for making exactly this claim without one.
- census owed before any rule, and the irony is deliberate: this leaf must not propose its own gate before measuring whether the pattern generalises beyond five instances in one session. Count, across the tree's history, how many leaves record a rule/threshold/severity that a later leaf revised, and how many were revised by measurement rather than by preference.
- Owns: that census; then a decision between three honest outcomes — a mechanizable gate, a `TOOLBOX.md` method statement with no gate, or an explicit "measured and not worth mechanizing". The third is a legitimate result and must stay available, or the census is theatre.
- Acceptance: the census is recorded with the command that produced it, and the decision names which of the three was taken and why. No gate ships without the census, which is the rule this leaf is about.
- Explicit limit: five instances in one session by one author is a population with an obvious bias, and the census must be capable of refuting the pattern rather than confirming it.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0145. The census PARTLY refuted the pattern, and the decision follows the measurement rather than the enthusiasm.
- **The population problem, faced rather than dodged.** "How many leaves proposed a rule a later leaf revised" is not mechanically countable: the tree's reversal vocabulary is prose and inconsistent — `grep -c superseded` over the tree returns **49**, and nearly all of those are about superseded DESIGNS rather than a leaf reversing its own rule. Counting by vocabulary would have produced a confident number measuring nothing, which is the failure this leaf is about.
- **So the census runs over the one sub-population where "a rule was proposed" IS mechanically countable: the gates this project has shipped.** The producing command dates each registered check to the commit that introduced it: `for f in <every check named in check_doctrines.sh and check_doctrines.project.sh>; do git log --format='%s' --diff-filter=A -- "$f" | head -1; done`. Eighteen doctrines are registered; **11 checks were introduced by this repository** (the rest arrive with the spine's initial commit), across **9 leaves** — `.11.4.3.1.2.13` (two), `.11.4.3.1.2.16`, `.11.4.3.1.2.18`, `.11.4.3.1.2.21`, `.11.4.4` (two), `.11.4.5.2`, `.11.4.5.3`, `.11.4.3.1.7.2`, and `PHASE-8.4.2` in another tree.
- **The result, and it is a coin flip rather than a law: 4 of the 8 leaves assessed had their RULE revised by the census that preceded it.**
  - ✓ `.11.4.3.1.2.16` (FILE-TERMINATION): "the obvious gate — wrapping `git diff --check` — would be wrong here", rejected by a census of 642 tracked text files finding 9 legitimately non-conforming.
  - ✓ `.11.4.3.1.2.21` (STORAGE-LOCALITY): the census itself was revised three times — "censusing for a token drawn from the last instance finds the last instance; census the CONCEPT" — and the rule's scope moved with it.
  - ✓ `.11.4.5.2` (LOCKSTEP-CLAIM): the rule's KEY moved from "a closing leaf must stage `MEMORY.md`" to the author's own claim, because the project does not follow the obvious version (6 of 10) and it would still have missed the defect.
  - ✓ `.11.4.5.3` (INDEX-FRONTIER): the census rejected BOTH provisional options, including the generator the leaf had preferred in writing.
  - ✗ `.11.4.3.1.7.2` (SELF-TEST): measured and shipped **unchanged** — 1.01 s against a 3.15 s enforcer, so the rule proceeded as proposed. ⭐ This is the case the pattern's advocates must also count: a measurement that confirms is not a wasted one.
  - ✗ `.11.4.4` (TASK-STATUS, HEADING-DEPTH): the CENSUS was corrected (a first pass reported one section holding 18 status lines; it held one and had swallowed five children) and that correction found a SECOND defect — but the proposed rule was not revised. A different phenomenon, and counted as such rather than folded in to help the total.
  - ✗ `.11.4.3.1.2.13`, `.11.4.3.1.2.18`: no rule revision recorded.
  - — `PHASE-8.4.2` (COMPATIBILITY-MATRIX): not assessed; it belongs to another tree and this leaf does not read another tree's records to pad its own denominator.
- ⛔ **The running "instances" list at the top of this leaf counts something DIFFERENT and the two must not be conflated.** Those ten include severity and threshold reversals inside repair leaves, which ship no gate and are not in this census's denominator. Ten instances is not "ten of ten"; this census's honest statement is **4 of 8 gates**.
- **The decision: a `TOOLBOX.md` method statement, no gate.** ⛔ A gate is not available, and that is a measured judgement rather than reluctance: you cannot mechanically detect "this leaf proposed a rule without measuring its population" — it is a judgement over prose. One narrow shape IS already gated (`GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS`, for a "nothing checks X" sentence), and the census at the top of this leaf confirmed with the gate's own predicate that four of five instances lie outside that shape.
- The statement is "Measure the population before proposing the rule over it" in `TOOLBOX.md`, and it carries the refutation rather than only the pattern: 4 of 8, the two cases where the obvious rule was rejected outright, and the one that was measured and shipped unchanged.
- Verification: the dating command re-runs and reproduces the 11/9 split; `make gate` prints `=== all doctrines green ===` across 18 checks; `mdbook build` and `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0, `git diff --check` rc=0.
- ⛔ NOT falsified against a superseded source, and the reason is that there is nothing executable to falsify: this leaf ships a method statement and a measurement. Its discriminating evidence is the census itself, which is capable of refuting the pattern and partly did — had every gate shipped unrevised, the statement would not have been written.
- ⚠️ The bias the leaf warned about is real and is NOT dissolved by this census: one author, one repository, and a denominator of 8. The statement says "measured across the gates this project has shipped", not "generally true".
- promotion: promoted → `TOOLBOX.md`, "Measure the population before proposing the rule over it". That is the durable home for a method with no gate, per the leaf's own three-way choice.
- ⚠️ Two further methods are promoted alongside it, and the reason is a correction: closing this leaf I removed them from `MEMORY.md` to fit the cap, on the stated grounds that they were already durable — and they were not, they were only in their own leaves. `.11.8`'s "check an instrument's first number against one obtained a DIFFERENT way" (its self-test shared the bug's blind spot, so the disagreeing second number was the only thing that caught a 42 % undercount) and `.11.4.3.1.7.2`'s "when correctness depends on enumerating what to exclude, make the failure cheap, not the list perfect" now sit in `TOOLBOX.md`. Their leaves had DECLINED promotion; that judgement is superseded here rather than left to contradict a demotion that assumed it.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0145 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.6): the census partly refuted its own pattern, and the statement says so`.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9 — A source-census record routed to a leaf is not reconciled against that leaf's split

- Opened: `pending`; found by `.4.1.2.1`, which independently rediscovered a defect the original source census had already written down.
- The finding, with its instance and the exact numbers: `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/census-1.md`'s record `R-31-32-5` routes to `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.1` and names **three** things about `issue_node_enroll_token`. `.4.1` then censused and split into three children — and carried **one** of the three clauses across. The second (`ttl_seconds` "could panic/overflow") was rediscovered nine leaves later by measuring a neighbouring leaf's premise; the third ("says authorized human but no human restriction") is still unopened today.
- ⭐ **The mechanism, and it is not carelessness.** `.4.1`'s census is a good one: it asks five questions, answers each from the code, confirms one, refutes one and names three as unmeasured. But the five come from the leaf's own **goal line** — the author's framing — and the routed record is the **reviewer's** framing. Nothing made the split re-read the record that pointed at the leaf, so a rigorous census of the wrong list looks exactly like a rigorous census.
- ROUTING EVIDENCE: the finding is about the census artifacts and the trees' use of them, not about node enrollment, which is why it is here and not under `.4.1`. What was measured is one record's clause-by-clause fate through one split; whether it generalizes is this leaf's first question, and it must be measured before any rule is proposed (`.11.4.5.2`'s lesson, and `.11.6`'s measured finding that the obvious rule is revised by its census about half the time).
- census owed, before anything is proposed: the five `census-*.md` parts hold **932 lines** across **53** review records; how many records name a repair candidate leaf, how many of those leaves have since been censused and split, and for how many of those is every clause of the record accounted for in a child. "Accounted for" must include *deliberately declined* — a clause a leaf considered and rejected is covered, and a rule that cannot tell the difference would flag every sound decision.
- ⛔ Do NOT open the two known-unrouted clauses as work under this leaf; this leaf owns the RECONCILIATION, and what it finds gets its own owners. The `ttl_seconds` clause is closed by `.4.1.2.1`; the "no human restriction" clause is unopened and is this leaf's first routing output.
- ⚠️ A gate is a candidate, not a foregone conclusion: `check_census_reconciliation.sh` could assert that a record naming a split leaf is cited by that leaf or a child. Whether that is sound depends entirely on the census above — the population may be small enough that a measured backlog is the better instrument, which is how `.11.8` ended.
- Acceptance: the census is run and recorded with the command that reproduces it; every unaccounted clause gains an owner or a recorded decline; and the decision names whether a gate holds the two in step.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0160.
- ⛔ **CORRECTION to this leaf's own census-owed line, which had a wrong number in it: the artifacts hold 131 review records, not 53.** 53 is `ls docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/ | wc -l` — the FILE count of the whole artifact directory, of which the five `census-*.md` parts are five. The 932-line figure is right. `MEMORY.md` has carried "131 records" correctly since `.1`, so the two disagreed and nothing compared them. Corrected here rather than quietly used, because this leaf exists to catch exactly that.
- **The instrument: `scripts/census_record_reconciliation.py`** (tracked, `--self-test` with 21 controls, registered in `TOOLBOX.md`). It parses every record's id, line range and candidate leaves, extracts each leaf's OWN section across every tree, and asks whether the leaf or a descendant CITES the record.
- 🔴 **The instrument was wrong FOUR times, each caught by a different control, and the sequence is recorded because it is the evidence the number is earned:**
  - **70 of 131** — the record regex required `R-N-N-N`, and this artifact set also uses `R-N-N`. Two id shapes, a 47 % blind spot, caught by a self-test control that asserted a POPULATION SIZE rather than re-deriving one from the same regex.
  - **parent swallowed child** — a leaf's section ran to the next heading of its OWN level, folding every child's text into the parent, so a child's citation counted for the parent and no split leaf could ever read as uncited. Caught by a control asserting the parent does NOT contain a child's commit id.
  - **3 citations of 19** — citation matching used the record's heading line only, while the tree's convention points at whatever line the author was reading (in practice `- Repair candidates:`). Fixed to a LINE RANGE, which needs no guess about which line an author picked.
  - **`.4.2`'s fifteen citations still read as UNCITED** — the tree elides the filename in a run: `` `census-2.md:28`, `:49`, `:56` ``. A bare `:N` inherits the nearest filename to its left. Caught by a control run against the REAL tree rather than a fixture, which is the only one of the four that a hand-written fixture would not have found.
- ⚠️ And one control was itself wrong before the code was: `elided-inherits-nearest-file` asserted `False` where `True` was correct. Restated against a record in the EARLIER file so a wrong inheritance shows up as a false positive instead of being masked by the right answer.
- **THE CENSUS, reproduced by `python3 -B scripts/census_record_reconciliation.py`:** **131** records; **614** record→candidate-leaf routings; **301** of those to a leaf that has since been SPLIT; **16** cited; **285** uncited. At RECORD granularity — the level the claim is actually about (`docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 1) — **17 of 131** records are cited by any candidate leaf and **114 by none**.
- 🔴 **THE GATE IS REJECTED, on the measurement, and decisively: it would fire on 114 of 131 records the day it was registered.** That is not a gate, it is a backlog wearing a gate's clothes, and `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`'s whole premise is that a gate people route around is a gate that lies. `.11.8` reached the same conclusion from the opposite direction — there the population was small enough to track as a backlog; here it is far too large for a gate.
- ⭐ **And the census changed the QUESTION, not just the answer — which is `.11.6`'s pattern for the fifth time.** The fan-out per record is **median 4–5 candidate leaves** (distribution 1→5 records, 2→7, 3→28, 4→26, 5→26, 6→20, 7→8, 8→6, 9→2, 10→1, 12→1, 13→1). A reviewer naming five leaves was writing a SUGGESTION LIST, not making five assignments. So "a leaf must account for every record routed to it" is unsound at the population level: most routings were speculative, and the three biggest uncited counts are the broad family containers (`.11.4` 99, `.3.3` 41, `.4.1` 36) that were never going to cite a record each.
- 🔴 **Which reframes `.4.1`'s original defect, and this is the leaf's real finding.** The failure was NOT that `.4.1` did not cite `R-31-32-5`. It is that the record named THREE distinct findings and only ONE found an owner anywhere in the tree. The reconcilable unit is **a clause with an owner**, not **a record cited by a leaf** — and no search can see the difference, because "accounted for" includes deliberately declined.
- **This leaf's one concrete obligation is DISCHARGED**: the "no human restriction" clause it named as its first routing output now has an owner, `.4.1.4`, opened with the finding measured at the source rather than restated — `resolve_principal` returns `Human` **or** `Role`, and nothing on the issuance path asks which, while two doc sites say "an authorized human".
- ⛔ **The remaining 114 uncited records are NOT closed here and are NOT left unowned**: they are routed to `.11.9.1` with their measured size, because a clause-level reconciliation of 114 records is an activity, not a leaf, and pretending otherwise would either bloat this commit or lose the backlog.
- NO REGRESSION: no product code touched. `--self-test` -> `21 controls pass` rc=0; `check_doctrines.sh` -> `=== all doctrines green ===` with the new instrument inside the SELF-TEST gate's population (22).
- LOCKSTEP: `TOOLBOX.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- promotion: declined. The three method rules exercised — measure the population before proposing the rule, match the granularity of the evidence to the claim, and check an instrument's first number a different way — are already in `TOOLBOX.md` and `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md`, and this is a further instance of each rather than a new statement (`.11.6`).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0160 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9): census the routed records, and reject the gate the leaf proposed`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1 — Reconcile the 114 uncited review records, clause by clause

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.9`, which measured the backlog rather than absorbing it.
- The measured size: **114 of 131** records are cited by none of their candidate leaves. At roughly two to four findings per record that is several hundred clauses, which is an activity rather than a leaf.
- ⛔ **"Uncited" is a POPULATION, not a defect count** (`.11.4.5.2`), and the instrument says so in its own output. Most of these records were handled by leaves that simply never named them; "accounted for" also includes DELIBERATELY DECLINED, which no search can see. The first job is classification, and the classification is what sizes the real work.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0168. This leaf did the census, corrected its own ranking, built the ledger and split; the classification activity lives in its children.
- ⛔ **This leaf's own acceptance is REVISED by its census, and the superseded version is kept rather than edited into agreement** (`TOOLBOX.md`). It read: "every one of the 114 records is classified … and each unowned clause gains a leaf". The census below measures **491 clauses across 40,127 characters** in those 114 records. That is an activity, exactly as the leaf's own opening line said, so the original acceptance descends to `.11.9.1.1`–`.11.9.1.6` collectively and this leaf's acceptance becomes: census it, choose the tranche ranking on a measurement, build a form the instrument can re-read, and prove both on the first tranche.

**The census.**

- Reproduced by `python3 -B scripts/census_record_reconciliation.py`: **131** records, **614** record→candidate-leaf routings, **301** to a leaf since SPLIT, and at record granularity **17 of 131** cited by any candidate leaf, **114 by none**. Every figure `.11.9` published reproduces exactly.
- Clause sizing, which `.11.9` could only estimate at "two to four per record": the 114 uncited records hold **40,127 characters** of body text, mean 351 and max 1,383, splitting at sentence terminators into roughly **491 clauses**.
- ⭐ **The reviewer drew from a vocabulary of 33 leaves, and one of them is a default.** Across all 614 routings there are only **33 distinct candidate leaves**, and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4` is named by **99 of the 131 records** — 76 %. `.3.3` is named by 41, `.4.1` by 37, `.4.4` by 36, `.5.1` by 34, `.4.5` by 32. A leaf named by three quarters of the corpus is not an assignment; it is the bucket a reviewer reaches for when a record also has a documentation dimension.

**The ranking this leaf proposed, and the measurement that rejected it.**

- 🔴 **`.11.9.1`'s own instruction was: "start from records with a SMALL fan-out (5 records name one leaf, 7 name two) — there the routing was a genuine assignment". The measurement says the opposite, and decisively.** Ranking instead by the record's NARROWEST candidate — the candidate leaf that the fewest other records also name — the two orders are anti-correlated:

  | Record's own fan-out | Narrowest candidate named by ≤ 10 records | by > 10 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1 | 0 | 5 |
  | 2 | 1 | 6 |
  | 3 | 6 | 18 |
  | 7 or more | 16 | 2 |

- **Why, and the instance that settles it.** All five fan-out-1 records name a CONTAINER: `R-36-39-4`→`.3.3` (41 records), `R-40-42-1`→`.4.5` (32), `R-55-2`→`.7.4` (22), `R-66-3`→`.4.1` (37), and `R-6-27-1`→`.11.4` (99). ⭐ `R-6-27-1` is the proof: its entire body is the artifact's boilerplate — "Source-review candidates only; runtime reproduction and task-tree ownership MUST follow full-read prerequisite. No edits or tests run." It carries **no finding at all**, and it still received a candidate leaf. A fan-out of one is the reviewer reaching for the default bucket, not precision. Meanwhile `R-84-1` has a fan-out of eight and names `.6.3`, a leaf **exactly one** record in the whole corpus names — and when `.6.3` is eventually censused, that record is the only one it has.
- ⚠️ **Auditor's asymmetry, honoured rather than skipped** (`docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §4): the re-derivation is the newer instrument and carries the heavier burden, so the difference is NAMED rather than the earlier line called wrong. `.11.9`'s statement is about the RECORD's side — how confident the reviewer was about where a finding goes — and it is defensible on that. It says nothing about the TARGET's side, which is what "an uncited routing is most likely a real miss" actually depends on: a leaf named by one record lost information when it did not cite it; a leaf named by 99 was never going to cite each. Both measures are real; they rank for different questions, and this activity needs the second.
- **Adopted:** rank by the narrowest candidate's frequency, reproducible with `python3 -B scripts/census_record_reconciliation.py --rank`. ⛔ Derived, not carried: the tranches below are the natural gaps in that distribution, and the command re-derives the membership if the corpus moves.

**The mechanism.**

- **The ledger: `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/RECONCILIATION.md`** — one row per CLAUSE, because `.11.9`'s finding was that the reconcilable unit is a clause with an owner and not a record cited by a leaf.
- **The closed set of six states, and it is wider than the acceptance's three — measured, not invented.** `handled` (a leaf did the work, named or not), `owned` (a leaf owns it AND its own text makes the clause visible, so its future census will read it), `attach` (a leaf owns the surface but its text does NOT make the clause visible), `unowned`, `declined`, `none`. Five of the six occurred in the first seven records.
- ⭐ **`attach` is the state the whole activity exists to find, and it did not exist in the acceptance's vocabulary.** `.11.9`'s defect is that a split censuses the leaf's own GOAL LINE rather than the routed record. For a leaf already split that is expensive retrospective work; for a leaf not yet split it costs one sentence — and `attach` is exactly the set of clauses where that sentence is still cheap. Three rows carry it today.
- ⚠️ `declined` has **zero** rows. That is deliberate and stated in the ledger: the state is invisible to every search, so the vocabulary must carry it before an instance does, or the first one will be recorded as something else.
- **The instrument re-reads it**: `--classified` reports the population, the ledger's coverage and a per-state count, and refuses a row naming a record that does not exist, a state outside the closed set, an owner that is not a leaf of any tracked tree, a `none` row with an owner, a non-`none` row without one, or the same clause twice. It found two breaches the moment it was first run, which were the two owner leaves this leaf had written into the ledger but not yet created.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.1.1 — Tranche 2a: the six records whose narrowest candidate is `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.3.2`

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.9.1.1`'s split.

- Acceptance: as `.11.9.1.1`.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0171.

🔴 **The narrowest candidate CLOSED over the clause — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9`'s exact mechanism, at the very leaf whose rarity ranked these six.** `.3.2` is `done`: it moved seven HTTP registry operations onto explicit site authority and pinned a closed set of **six** site actions (`registry_inspect`, `adapter_allow`, `adapter_revoke`, `region_declare`, `region_pair`, `region_unpair`). **Two of its own routed records asked it to census the shared-registry write SCOPE before designing that set, and it cited neither.** Measured at the source today, two site-global registries remain outside it:

- `POST /v1/resolvers` — `register_resolver` in `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs` resolves the caller's OWN tenant and admits on `authorize_tenant_admin`, then writes `resolver_capabilities`. Migration 0024 gives that table **no tenant column** and a single-column `resolver_id` primary key, and `resolvers::register` is an `ON CONFLICT (resolver_id) DO UPDATE`. So any tenant's administrator registers — or REPLACES — a site-global resolver row, the built-in `r0-https-fetcher` included, rewriting its `schemes`, `egress_class`, `sandbox_level`, `max_bytes`, `version` and `security_evidence`.
- `POST /v1/workflow-profiles` — `register_workflow_profile` is weaker still: it requires **enrolment only**, not even tenant administration. `workflow_profiles` (migration 0032) has no tenant column; `workflows::register` inserts `COALESCE(MAX(version),0) + 1` with `built_in = false` for ANY `profile_id`; and resolution reads `ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1`. An enrolled principal can therefore register `quick_advice` version 2 and shadow a §13.1 built-in for the whole site.

⛔ **Neither is opened as work here, and that restraint is deliberate** (`.11.9`: what the reconciliation finds gets its own owners, and an owner that already exists is not duplicated). `.7.1`'s goal line already carries the resolver registry's authority — "bind writes/reads to explicit tenant or site authority" over the owned surfaces `resolvers, API registration` — and `.8.1`'s already carries "version and authorize shared workflow registration, prevent built-in override and MAX+1 races". What this leaf adds is the clause BOTH leaves' text is missing, recorded as `attach`: the obligation to census the whole shared-registry write scope before designing the bind. That is the clause whose absence let a rigorous closed set be the wrong closed set, and attaching it now costs one sentence where a second partial repair would cost another `.3.2`.

⭐ **The ledger's second two-records-one-finding pair, and it is the one that matters most.** `R-31-32-2` clause 2 ("Must include scope census before design") and `R-78-2` clause 2 ("Core decision shared registry write scope at least region/adapter/resolver") are the SAME finding reached by two reviewers' records. A record-level ledger would have counted it twice and still let it fall — which is the case `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9` made for classifying clauses instead of records, now observed a second time.

🔴 **The one `unowned` clause: `regions::route` reports a storage failure as a policy refusal.** `R-53-2` named `pair` and `route` together; `.3.2.1` repaired `pair` and carries the fix as a comment in its own source — "Domain refusals are separate from SQL errors. In particular, an unavailable database must never masquerade as an undeclared region" — while `route` was never touched. Live in `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/regions.rs`: three `.map_err(|_| RegionRefusal::…)` turn ANY `sqlx::Error` into `UndeclaredRegion` or `CrossRegionRefused`. New owner `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.10`, opened with the reachability measured rather than assumed.

⭐ **Three `owned` rows are live defects whose owning leaf's own text already names them, so the classification is `owned` and not a new leaf — but each was confirmed AGAINST THE SOURCE, not matched to the goal line:**

- `.9.2` "verify both immutable and effective refs" — `reconciler::reconcile` reads `git.effective` in **no branch at all**. Under `DbState::Effective` it compares only `git.immutable` against the expected id, so §15.8's "effective | ref missing or moved → freeze deployment" cannot fire for a moved EFFECTIVE channel. `tests/reconciler.rs::the_consistent_pairs_are_quiet` asserts exactly that: immutable 7, effective 8, expected 7, `Action::Consistent`.
- `.9.2` "make CAS retries recoverable" — `publisher::publish` writes the immutable publication ref (`MustNotExist`) BEFORE the effective compare-and-swap, and the CAS failure path unwinds nothing. A publication that failed at the CAS has its immutable ref on disk, so the natural retry of the SAME publication id returns `ImmutableExists`. `tests/publisher.rs` proves the stale-CAS refusal and separately proves `ImmutableExists` for a different id; it never retries the id that failed.
- `.8.1` "reconcile durable unresolved challenges with close contracts" — the decision-family gate in `threads.rs` is `body.outcome.is_decision_family() && !body.unresolved.is_empty()`, over the CALLER's supplied list alone. `projection.open_challenges` is maintained on both edges and consulted nowhere at close, so a caller who simply omits a durable open challenge closes with a decision terminal. `R-90-1`'s demo clause is the same mechanism seen from the fixture side, and it adds the qualifier this leaf preserves rather than resolves: that behaviour may be an explicit historical acceptance, so the repair must reconcile it rather than silently change it.

⚠️ **And one `attach` is a contradiction between two tracked documents that no test can see.** `resolvers::resolve` applies `declared >= required` to BOTH ADR-018 ladders. For `SANDBOX_LEVELS` (`none` < `process` < `constrained_process` < `vm_container`) greater means MORE isolation, so the comparison refuses a downgrade, which is what the ADR says the classes are for. For `EGRESS_CLASSES` (`none` < `loopback` < `listed` < `any`) greater means more network REACH — and ADR-018 decides in its own words that "a resolver's egress claim is the MAXIMUM, never the minimum". Comparing ceilings with `>=` admits a resolver whose maximum reach is BROADER than the reference required; the default request (`required_egress = "loopback"`) admits `listed` and `any`. The module's comment reads the field the other way ("a resolver claiming LESS than required is ineligible"), which is coherent only if the class is reach rather than a ceiling. ⛔ This leaf does NOT decide which reading is right — the decision is `.7.1`'s and needs ADR-018's own revisit — but it records that the two readings exist in tracked text, disagree, and are distinguished by no control today.

🔴 **The heaviest finding is about the ledger itself, and it is this leaf's own predecessor: tranche 1 recorded three `attach` rows and performed NONE of the three attachments.** `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.1` carried no word about `R-53-4`'s caller-declared `scheme` column, and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4` none about `R-63-1`'s now-false `escalation.rs` header — measured by reading both leaves' whole sections, not by searching for a phrase.

- ⛔ **A row that says "this leaf will drop the clause" does not stop the leaf dropping it.** `attach` is the only one of the six states whose Next action is not "none", and the ledger recorded the state while leaving the action undone. `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9`'s mechanism was therefore still live *inside the instrument built to stop it* — which is the sharpest available demonstration that classification is not the same as repair.
- Fixed here rather than noted: all **seven** `attach` clauses are now attached — tranche 1's three and tranche 2a's four — as explicit `⭐ ATTACHED CLAUSE` blocks in `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.1` (three), `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.8.1` (one) and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4` (one), each naming the record, the clause ordinal and the source line that makes it true.
- And the vocabulary is tightened so the gap cannot reopen: `RECONCILIATION.md`'s `attach` row now says **in the commit that classifies it**, and carries the measured instance rather than only the rule (`TOOLBOX.md`: a rule with its instance survives; a rule alone is advice).
- ⚠️ No gate is proposed. The population is seven rows in one tracked file and the obligation is now written where its reader is; a checker that tried to assert "the owning leaf's text mentions this clause" would have to guess at paraphrase, which is the failure mode `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.6` measures.

- **REPRODUCE / ROOT CAUSE, NO REGRESSION and LOCKSTEP** for this child and its parent are in the commit acceptance below.

| shape | CLI succeeds, no match | CLI FAILS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `! cli \| grep -q X` | rc=0 (correct pass) | rc=0 (**false pass**) |
| `! cli \| grep -q X` with `pipefail` | rc=0 (correct pass) | rc=0 (**false pass**) |

⛔ `!` negates the pipeline's status, and with `pipefail` that status is 1 whether the CLI failed or merely printed nothing — so the two cases stay indistinguishable. The record's diagnosis of the DEFECT is right and its proposed REMEDY is refuted: the fix is to check the producer's exit status separately, never to set an option. ⚠️ `bash -c` starts a fresh shell that inherits neither `-e` nor `pipefail`, measured, so the outer `set -euo pipefail` at `:53` reaches none of these probes either.

| `--commands` | `--concurrency` | issued | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | 8 | 200 | PASS (correct) |
| 100 | 8 | **104** | PASS — 4 more than requested |
| 1 | 8 | **8** | PASS — 8x the request |
| 0 | 8 | **0** | **PASS: every command committed** |
| -5 | 8 | **0** | **PASS: every command committed** |

⛔ `[ 0 -ge 0 ]` and `[ 0 -ge -5 ]` are both true and `FAILED` is 0, so a capacity run that measured nothing reports success — reachable by a plain typo. The overshoot is the same arithmetic seen from the other side, and the summary's throughput is computed from the ISSUED total, so a published capacity number can exceed what was asked. (`--concurrency 0` does fail, with an opaque `division by 0`.)

⭐ **One mechanism appears at THREE separate sites, in two different records, and no leaf had connected them: a lookup keyed on `operation_id`/`command_id` ALONE, with the node it belongs to never in the predicate.**

- `node_channel.rs::event_id_for_operation` — `SELECT event_id FROM node_events WHERE operation_id = $1 ORDER BY received_at LIMIT 1`. No `node_id`, no tenant. It is the reconciliation lookup the HANDSHAKE performs, so any enrolled node that names a victim's operation id is handed the victim's event id.
- `node_channel.rs`'s receipt insert — `ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING`, and `event_id` is `node_events`' whole primary key (migration 0003), with `node_id` a plain column. A node that writes first under a known event id makes the rightful node's receipt a silent no-op, returning `false`.
- `migrations/0021_node_inbox_delivery_state.sql:19`–`:21` — the `delivery_state` view calls a row `consumed` when `EXISTS (… node_events e WHERE e.operation_id = i.command_id AND e.payload->>'kind' = 'work_result')`. The join carries no `e.node_id = i.node_id`, so ANOTHER node's result marks this node's inbox row consumed.

🔴 **The third site is `R-85-1` clause 4 and the first two are `R-48-49-3`'s — two records, one mechanism, three sites, and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.3`'s goal line already demands exactly the proof that would have caught all three**: *"prove command-id collisions across nodes cannot consume or hide foreign work"*. ⭐ This is the clause-level ledger's fourth two-records-one-finding pair, and the first where the shared finding is a SCHEMA shape rather than a code path.

🔴 **The cursor high-water mark is derived from a DELETABLE table, so pruning rewinds it.** `enqueue` writes `(SELECT COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) + 1 FROM node_inbox WHERE node_id = $1)` and `current_cursor` reads `COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0)` over the same rows. Prune DELETES acknowledged rows. Prune everything and the high-water mark is 0 again: the next enqueue re-issues cursor 1, which a node that already acknowledged cursor 1 discards as seen, and a node holding a high journal cursor against a server reporting a lower one is the `journal_lost` anomaly this module's own header names at `:43`. ⚠️ The remedy the record states — a separate durable counter rather than the deletable inbox — is the only shape that survives, and it is recorded as the clause's own text rather than invented here.

⚠️ **And the test that would catch it stops one step short, which is `R-70-3`'s whole point.** `prune_deletes_only_delivered_rows_older_than_the_window` leaves survivors `cmd_prune_3`, `4`, `5` — a partial prefix that KEEPS the highest cursor, so `MAX` never returns NULL. There is no prune-everything-then-reconnect control anywhere in the suite.

- 🔴 **But the measurement that answered it found a defect the record did not state.** The same absence of an expiry predicate means `repeated_waiver` fires on a waiver that lapsed a year ago, for ever. And the trigger named "repeated" fires on the FIRST one: one row in `policy_corrections` produces one `(publication, repeated_waiver)` pair, which is what `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/policy.rs:3161` records and asserts. ⛔ Not opened as new work — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.3`'s goal line already says "enforce waiver constraints" — but written into that leaf, because a repair that only makes the test use a relative clock would leave both halves standing.
