Line (9) is a penetration test whose critical/high findings are resolved or the release is CANCELLED (§19.6), not waived. Line (5) is the prompt-injection action-boundary suite, which lands with the exposure profile's first action-bearing surface and has nothing to attach to yet.
- What this leaf CAN own, which is not nothing: the input each engagement needs (a threat model fit to be reviewed, a scope and an environment for a pen test), the trigger that starts it, and the durable record of its outcome. ⚠️ Preparing the input is not the gate and the leaf must never let one read as the other.
- Acceptance: each of the three names the party who clears it, the input this project owes them, and the trigger; none is described as "in progress" while it is unstarted; the register and the book say the same thing.
- ⭐ **B3's deferral is now MEASURED rather than inherited, which is the only part of these three that local work could improve.** The gate record said the prompt-injection suite "lands with the exposure profile's first action-bearing surface", and this tree had been repeating that sentence. Measured 2026-09-15 under the director's instruction to unblock:
  - **The dispatched work payload carries no untrusted content.** `threads::work_payload` builds exactly `kind`, `agent_role`, `subject`, `objective`, `reservation`, `reservation_reason`, `allow_possible_duplicate`, plus an optional `target_event_id`. ⛔ No contribution text, no evidence snapshot, no derivation, no acquired bytes.
  - **The adapters hold no tools.** The Claude adapter runs `--restricted --tools ''` and the Codex adapter `--sandbox read-only`; `prompt_for` passes the payload as USER content and never as instructions.
  - **The acquisition packs terminate in evidence, not in action.** R0/R1/R2 produce snapshots and derivations that are stored and served through read surfaces; no path carries them into a dispatched run.
- ⛔ **So §16.6's action boundary genuinely has nothing to guard yet, and the deferral is CORRECT** — which is a stronger statement than the gate record's, because it rests on three measurements rather than on a plan.
- 🔴 **The trigger is therefore mechanical, and naming it is what stops the deferral being silently outlived.** The suite becomes owed the first time ANY of these is true: `work_payload` gains a field carrying acquired or contributed content; an adapter's `AdapterCapabilities.tool_support` becomes `true`; or a model output reaches a publication, a deployment, a grant or a tool call rather than becoming a contribution. ⚠️ Each is a one-line grep, which is the point — a deferral whose end condition cannot be checked is a deferral that outlives its reason.
- ⚠️ **B1 and B2 are NOT improvable this way and the leaf must not pretend otherwise.** An externally reviewed threat model and a penetration test are engagements; no measurement makes either less required. What this project can still own for them is the INPUT — a threat model fit to be reviewed, a scope and an environment for a test — and that remains this leaf's work.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.1.1 — The adapter-load ladder has no caller, and its only ceiling permits tools

- Opened: `pending` on 2026-09-15. ⚠️ **Provenance, stated because it matters:** this was NOT found by a leaf. The director asked whether a locally spawned open-weight model (Kimi, Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek) or a remote instance could join the network, and whether the network cares which agent type connects. Answering that required reading the admission path, and the reading contradicted the answer I had already given him. ⭐ The question was better than my census.
- 🔴 **`verify_ladder` HAS NO PRODUCTION CALLER.** `git grep -n "verify_ladder" -- crates` returns 8 hits: the definition (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/allowlist.rs:150`), a `pub use` re-export (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/lib.rs:43`), and **six call sites all inside `allowlist.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)]` module** (lines 266, 286, 301, 315, 331, 351). The five-rung fail-closed adapter-load ladder is a tested library that nothing runs. Same for `capabilities_within`: its only non-test caller is `verify_ladder` itself.
- ⛔ **`dead_code` cannot see this** — `verify_ladder` is `pub` and re-exported from `lib.rs`, so the compiler is satisfied. MEMORY has carried that warning since `.11.4.5.4`; this is a fresh instance of it, at an admission control.
- 🔴 **AND the ceiling would not refuse tools even if it were wired.** `AllowedCapabilities::dev()` (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/allowlist.rs:44`) is the **only constructor in the crate**, and it sets `tool_support: true`. Rung 5 is `!declared.tool_support || allowed.tool_support` (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/allowlist.rs:140`), so under the one profile that ships, an adapter declaring tool support passes.
- ⭐ **This is `.3.4`'s shape at a security control: a goal line naming a mechanism its own split dropped.** `PHASE-8.4.4`'s Goal reads "the five-rung verification **at the adapter-load path**". Its Done list ships the ladder function, migration `0052_adapter_allowlist.sql` and the `tenant_admin`-gated registry verbs — and no load-path call. The leaf is `done`.
- ⛔ **What this does NOT mean, and the leaf must not overstate it** — the correction I already had to make once here. The shipped adapters are **compiled in**, not downloaded, so no unverified adapter is loading today; `allowlist.rs`'s own header says the dev adapters "satisfy the ladder BY CONSTRUCTION". The exposure is that the control is **inert for the case it was built for** — a downloaded or operator-supplied adapter — not that something malicious is loading now.
- ⚠️ **What actually holds the action boundary today is declaration-side and narrower than the ladder suggests:** every `Adapter` implementer declares `tool_support: false` (`claude.rs:121`, `codex.rs:94`, `scripted.rs:152`, `contract.rs:279`), and the two real adapters pass `--restricted --tools ''` (`claude.rs::EXEC_ARGS`) and `--sandbox read-only` (`codex.rs::EXEC_ARGS`). ⛔ Those are the facts `B3`'s deferral rests on — NOT the ladder.
- 🔴 **Consequence for B3, which is why this sits under `.13.1`.** `.13.1` records B3's deferral as measured. The measurement stands, but its stated ground was partly wrong: the ladder is not enforcing anything. ⚠️ A third-party adapter — exactly what an open-weight local runner would be — is the case the ladder exists for, and it is the case with no enforcement.
- Owns: deciding and recording (a) whether to wire `verify_ladder` into the adapter-load path or to state plainly that no load path exists yet and the ladder is ahead of its caller; (b) whether `AllowedCapabilities::dev()`'s `tool_support: true` is intended, given that no adapter declares it and B3's deferral depends on none doing so; (c) correcting `.13.1`'s B3 text and the book's blocker page so neither cites the ladder as the control.
- ⚠️ **Prefer (a)-as-a-statement over (a)-as-a-wiring until a load path exists.** Wiring a verification into a path that never runs buys nothing and creates a second false assurance. ⛔ But a `pub` control with no caller and no note saying so is the thing that produced this finding — whichever is chosen must leave a reader unable to make my mistake.
- Acceptance: a census of every `pub` item in `reasonbraid-adapter` with no non-test caller (not just these two — scoping to the two with known answers is `.3.3.4.10`'s mistake); a decision on (a), (b) and (c) each with its rationale; if the ceiling stays permissive, the leaf says what would refuse a tool-declaring adapter instead; and `.13.1`, the register and `docs/book/src/blockers.md` stop attributing the boundary to the ladder.
- [x] **THE CENSUS, CRATE-WIDE AND IN A TRACKED INSTRUMENT** — `scripts/census_adapter_public_api.py` (leg 3: the producer is tracked, `--self-test` two-sided). **102 `pub` items; 17 with no non-test caller outside their own file.** ⛔ The leaf named TWO items; the census says **THREE** — `AllowedCapabilities` joins `verify_ladder` and `capabilities_within`, which is exactly why the acceptance forbade scoping to the known answers.
- 🔴 **All three have exactly ONE non-test mention outside their own file, and it is the SAME line** — `crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/lib.rs:43`, `pub use allowlist::{capabilities_within, verify_ladder, AllowedCapabilities, RungRefusal};`. ⭐ **A re-export is not a caller, and it is also the mechanism that blinds `dead_code`**: without it the items would be crate-private, unused, and the compiler would have said so on the first build. ⚠️ A mention-counting census over-counts by exactly one per re-export, and **one is the most dangerous answer** — it reads as "it has a caller", where a zero would have prompted a second look.
- **The other 14 are CLASSIFIED, not published as a defect count** (the anti-pattern `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` names): **1** is test-support (`from_spec`, 6 integration-test mentions) and **13** are over-exposed helpers in `bench/`, `fixtures.rs` and `certification.rs` used only inside their own file — tidiness, not risk. ⛔ Publishing "17 items have no caller" as a finding would have been wrong in 14 cases out of 17; what makes three matter is WHERE they sit.
- **DECISION (a) — state it, do NOT wire it.** Measured: no adapter load path exists — `git grep -nE "libloading|dlopen|Library::new|load_adapter|from_path" -- crates` returns **nothing**, and the adapters are compiled in. Wiring a verification into a path that never runs buys no safety and creates a second false assurance. ⭐ But the leaf's own constraint was that whichever is chosen "must leave a reader unable to make my mistake", so the fact is recorded **at the definition** rather than only in a task tree — `verify_ladder`'s doc now states it has no production caller, names the census that measured it, and explains the re-export's role.
- **DECISION (b) — `AllowedCapabilities::dev()` now declares `tool_support: false`.** It was `true`. ⛔ That constructor is the crate's ONLY ceiling and its own doc line says it describes "the shipped adapters' shapes" — while every shipped adapter declares `tool_support: false`, a fact `check_action_boundary.sh` pins across five files. So the ceiling permitted what nothing declares and the doc line was false about its own field. ⚠️ **This changes no runtime behaviour and is not described as closing anything** — nothing consults the ceiling at run time. It changes the DIRECTION the ladder fails if it is ever wired: closed rather than open, with a tool-using adapter needing a deliberate profile.
- [x] **The refusal is PROVEN, two-sided** — `the_dev_ceiling_refuses_a_tool_declaring_adapter`: a tool-declaring adapter is refused at **rung 5** by name under `dev()`, and the SAME adapter is admitted under a ceiling that deliberately grants it. ⭐ The second arm is what makes it a control rather than something that always refuses.
- **DECISION (c) — already satisfied, VERIFIED rather than assumed.** `grep -c "ladder" docs/book/src/blockers.md` returns **0**, and `.13.1`'s B3 text rests on three measurements (the dispatched payload, the adapters' declarations, the packs terminating in evidence) with the ladder cited nowhere. `.13.1.2` had already corrected this. ⛔ Re-"fixing" a corrected document would have been a change nobody needed, so the census is recorded and nothing is edited.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — `PHASE-8.4.4`'s Goal names "the five-rung verification **at the adapter-load path**"; its Done list ships the ladder, `migrations/0052` and the registry verbs, and no load-path call. The leaf closed `done`. ⭐ `.3.4`'s shape at a security control: a goal line naming a mechanism its own split dropped, invisible because `pub` + a re-export satisfies `dead_code` forever.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `cargo test -p reasonbraid-adapter`: **14 lib tests**, including both pre-existing ladder controls and the new two-sided one, plus 4 + 5 + 8 + 7 + 12 + 2 across the crate's other targets; 0 failed.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-adapter --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` **exit 0, zero diagnostics** (captured in full, per `.11.14.3.3`'s process note); `cargo fmt --all` rc=0; `make gate`; `make book`.
- [x] **FIX / LOCKSTEP** — `allowlist.rs` (the ceiling, the definition's doc, the new control), `scripts/census_adapter_public_api.py`, and this leaf. ⛔ **B3 is NOT advanced and this must not be read as progress on it**: B3 remains an external blocker whose suite lands with the first action-bearing surface, and what holds the boundary today is still declaration-side, pinned by `ACTION-BOUNDARY`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.1.2 — Make B3's deferral trigger evaluable by a script

- Opened and closed 2026-09-15; REPAIR-0201. ⛔ **The deferral is NOT being revisited here — it is still correct.** `.13.1` measured that model output cannot reach an action, and that measurement stands. What changes is that the trigger stops being prose.
- 🔴 **The case for it is measured, not hypothetical, and it is one leaf old.** `.11.4.7.2` found Phase 1's deferral #5 — a fuzz baseline, deferred until "the first untrusted parser (Phase 4's resource packs)". Phase 4 shipped and closed; `fetcher.rs`, `git.rs`, `reasonbraid-extract` and `-browse` now parse untrusted input; `git ls-files | grep -ic fuzz` returns **0**; and the word `fuzz` appears in exactly ONE decision record — the one that deferred it — and ZERO times in Phase 4's. ⭐ **A deferral with a trigger nobody checks is an omission with extra steps.** B3 is the same shape and this closes it.
- **`scripts/check_action_boundary.sh`, registered as `ACTION-BOUNDARY`** — the 11th project check. It pins the four facts B3's deferral rests on, each re-read rather than carried:
  - `claude.rs::EXEC_ARGS` passes `--restricted` and `--tools` immediately followed by the EMPTY string;
  - `codex.rs::EXEC_ARGS` passes `--sandbox` immediately followed by `read-only`;
  - `threads::work_payload` dispatches exactly eight keys — no acquired bytes, no evidence, no derivations;
  - every `AdapterCapabilities` construction declares `tool_support: false`, across 5 files, and exactly 4 types implement `Adapter`.
- ⭐ **The fourth is the one that matters, and `.13.1.1` is why it is pinned HERE.** The obvious place to enforce "no tool support" is the admission ladder — and `verify_ladder` has **no production caller**, while `AllowedCapabilities::dev()`, the crate's only ceiling, permits `tool_support: true`. So nothing refuses a tool-declaring adapter at runtime. ⛔ This gate refuses it at commit time instead, which is a weaker guarantee honestly placed rather than a stronger one imagined.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits, in the script's own header**: it does not prove the boundary holds, only that the four facts the boundary ARGUMENT rests on are unchanged — if `.13.1`'s argument was wrong, this gate is wrong with it. It is textual, so a flag passed through a variable rather than the pinned const would not be seen. And it says nothing about the acquisition packs, which are the untrusted-INPUT side, owned by `.7.2`.
- 🔴 **The gate's first real run FAILED, on my own parser rather than on the tree — and the self-test was green.** `payload_keys` delimited the function with `src.find("\npub ", i)`; the next item is `pub(crate) async fn`, which does not match, so the slice ran to the end of a 5,000-line file and the gate reported **26 phantom new fields** from unrelated functions. Fixed by BRACE MATCHING from the function's opening brace. ⛔ A terminator that depends on how the next declaration happens to be spelled is not a delimiter.
- ⭐ **The self-test passed because its real-file probe asserted "parsed something".** The broken parser returned thirty-odd keys and satisfied a non-empty check happily. The probe now asserts the EXACT key set and names extra/missing on failure. ⚠️ Second instance this session of `docs/knowledge/a-self-test-cannot-be-tidier-than-the-real-input` — there the fixtures were tidier than the file; here the ASSERTION was weaker than the claim.
- **FALSIFIED, five arms against the working tree, each self-reversing:** `--tools ''` → `--tools Bash` rc=1; `--restricted` removed rc=1; codex `read-only` → `workspace-write` rc=1; one adapter declaring `tool_support: true` rc=1; `work_payload` gaining an `acquired_evidence` field rc=1. Restored state proved by `cmp -s` per file and `git diff --quiet -- crates`; positive control rc=0 after.
- 🔴 **A SECOND DEFECT, AND IT IS MINE FROM THE PREVIOUS COMMIT: `SECRET-SCAN` COULD NOT SEE THE COMMIT IT WAS GATING.** Registering `ACTION-BOUNDARY` ran the full enforcer, and `SECRET-SCAN` — installed one commit earlier by REPAIR-0200 — fired. Not on this leaf's work: on REPAIR-0200's own.
  - ⛔ **The superseded claim, named rather than quietly replaced:** REPAIR-0200 recorded `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` rc=0, `no leaks found`, as its ADDRESSED evidence. That measurement was taken against an **UNCOMMITTED working tree**, and `gitleaks detect`/`git` scans **HISTORY**. So it verified the state BEFORE the change, and the value it introduced — `key-delegation-1` — surfaced as a new `generic-api-key` finding at `b6445d1818e0` the moment it was committed.
  - ⭐ **The irony is exact and worth stating.** That same leaf's headline lesson was "a rename cannot reach a HISTORICAL finding, because `detect` scans every commit". The identical fact cuts the other way and I did not turn it around: **a history scan cannot reach an UNCOMMITTED change either.** One sentence, two consequences, and I took only the one that was in front of me.
  - ⚠️ **And the rename was ineffective on its own terms.** `key-delegation-1` scores entropy **3.578**; `generic-api-key` fires above roughly 3.5. It was chosen for readability and never measured against the rule it existed to satisfy. The value is now `idem-test-000001` — still 16 characters, so `baseline == 308` holds, and entropy **2.899**, which trips nothing. The fixture now says BOTH properties are load-bearing, because a future editor checking only the length would reintroduce this.
  - **Fixes:** `gitleaks git --staged` added as a FIRST arm to `SECRET-SCAN`, so the gate reads what is actually being committed — **0.03 s**, and falsified by staging a high-entropy literal (rc=1, naming the staged arm) then restoring (rc=0, `cmp -s` identical). The history arm stays as the second. ⚠️ `detect --no-git` was measured and REJECTED: it walks `target/` and `.project-data/` and did not finish in **120 s**.
  - ⛔ The `b6445d1` finding needed a fingerprint anyway — it is in history now — and `.gitleaksignore` records that it is **my own defect rather than an inherited one**. ⭐ The staged arm means the NEXT one will not need a fingerprint at all, which is the whole point: a finding caught before it is committed is a value you fix, not a line you permanently annotate.
- ⭐ **Measured before registering, the `REASON-CODE-DOC` shape:** it fires on **zero** breaches today, and would have fired on none historically either — because the boundary has never moved. ⚠️ So unlike the licence gate, this one catches no present or past defect. Its entire value is the NEXT change, which is exactly what deferral #5 needed and did not have.
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT do:** it does not write the prompt-injection suite, and it must not be described as progress on B3. B3 remains an external blocker whose suite lands with the first action-bearing surface. This gate only guarantees that the day that surface lands, the commit that lands it says so.
- promotion: declined. Both lessons exercised already have records — the parser-vs-self-test half is `docs/knowledge/a-self-test-cannot-be-tidier-than-the-real-input` and the trigger half is stated in `.11.4.7.2.1`'s acceptance, which owns the general question.
- Verification: `scripts/check_action_boundary.sh --self-test` → `15 audit cases, 3 real-file parses`, rc=0; the gate itself rc=0; `make gate` 18 checks rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0 (no Rust changed — the falsification restored every file).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0201 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.1.2): make B3's deferral trigger evaluable by a script`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.2 — The open external decisions: name clearance and licence

- Opened: `pending` by `.13`. Covers register rows **B4** and **B5**.
- **B4 — ADR-001 public-name clearance.** `ReasonBraid` is a WORKING name on a preliminary exact-name screen, which §2.7 is explicit is not legal clearance. - ⚠️ Both are the director's, and neither has a technical precondition this project can supply — which makes them exactly the kind of blocker that goes quiet. The register is the reason they will not.
- Acceptance: each carries its decision-maker, what it blocks, what it does NOT block, and the trigger; the book states both as open rather than implying either is settled.
- 🔴 **MEASURED 2026-09-15 under the director's instruction to unblock the blockers, and B5's framing is WRONG: the licence is not undecided.** `git grep -rn "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml Cargo.toml` returns **ten** declarations of `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` — the workspace package plus every crate, four of them spelled out literally and the rest inheriting. The Rust ecosystem's conventional dual licence, chosen, written down, and shipped.
- 🔴 **What is missing is the LICENCE ITSELF.** `git ls-files | grep -iE "licen[cs]e|copying"` returns exactly one path, `migrations/0031_snapshot_license_freshness.sql`, which is a snapshot-retention migration and not a licence. **There is no `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE` or `COPYING` anywhere in the repository.**
- ⛔ **The consequence, stated precisely rather than dramatically.** A manifest's SPDX expression is metadata, not a grant. This repository is PUBLIC and must remain so, and absent an accompanying licence text the default position is ordinary copyright: a reader has no rights the licence expression appears to offer. ⭐ The project also enforces a permissive-only licence policy on its DEPENDENCIES (`deny.toml`'s `allow` list, with one narrow file-level MPL exception for `uluru`) while granting nothing itself — a rule applied outward and not inward.
- **The dependency graph constrains nothing**, so the choice is unforced: every allowed licence is permissive (Apache-2.0, MIT, ISC, Unicode-3.0, BSD-3-Clause, Zlib) and the single MPL-2.0 dependency is file-level copyleft used unmodified. Nothing in the tree compels or forbids any licence for this project.
- ⭐ **So B5 is not a decision the director owes — it is a decision already taken in ten places that was never given effect**, and the reframing is the unblocking. Of the work it implies, exactly ONE item is not mine to supply.
- ⛔ **THE ONE THING NEEDED FROM THE DIRECTOR: the copyright holder's name**, as it should appear in the `Copyright (c) <year> <holder>` line of `LICENSE-MIT` and the Apache-2.0 appendix. A legal identity is a fact about the world, not an engineering choice, and inventing one would be worse than leaving the blocker open. ⚠️ Everything else — which licences, their exact texts, where they live, the `README` pointer — is determined by the ten declarations already in the tree.
- Owns: recording the above as a decision record; adding `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE` with the verbatim upstream texts once the holder is known; a `README` licence section; and a check that the manifests and the files cannot drift apart.
- ⚠️ Do NOT change the licence expression to something narrower or broader on the way: **13 tracked manifests** already declare it, `cargo publish` reads it, and a change would be a relicensing act rather than a completion.
- ⚠️ B4 is untouched by this and stays open: the name clearance is a separate external gate, and a licence grants nothing about a trademark.

- The finding **as opened**: `COMMIT.md` names the REMOTE run as the authoritative pre-push gate (`docs/decisions/2026-09-12_checkpoint-gate-authority.md`), and it has never run — so every gate result in this tree, including the full checkpoint pass, is a LOCAL qualification.
- 🔴 **MEASURED 2026-09-17 under the director's instruction to unblock, and the finding is FALSE.** `gh api "repos/rdje/reasonbraid/actions/runs?per_page=1" --jq '.total_count'` returns **41**; the conclusion histogram is **29 success, 12 failure**; and the latest run of each of the three workflows is **success**, all at `c17841c`, 2026-09-11T22:01:27Z. `git rev-parse origin/main` is `c17841c` — **the last commit CI observed IS the remote head, and the remote gate is GREEN.**
- **What that green covers, read from the workflow files rather than assumed:** `doctrines` runs the enforcer; `supply-chain` runs pinned `cargo-deny` and pinned Gitleaks over history; `rust` runs the workspace check, the Python controls with the full owned PostgreSQL collection, and the book build.
- ⭐ **ROOT CAUSE — the row was written from `COMMIT.md`'s cadence note rather than from the remote, and `COMMIT.md` CONTRADICTED IT FOUR LINES BELOW.** That page's push section ends *"Provenance: director instruction 2026-09-11, during the first remote-CI repair sequence."* A remote-CI repair sequence is a sequence of remote CI runs — and the 12 measured failures are largely it: `rust` failed at REPAIR-0076, 0077, 0078, 0079, 0080 and 0083, then went green at 0086, which is exactly the one-repair-per-push pattern `COMMIT.md` describes as its own standing exception. ⛔ `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 1 in its plainest form: a fact quoted from the project's own documentation instead of re-derived from the source, when the source was one `gh` call away.
- **The corrected statement, which is narrower and still real:** the remote gate is green at `origin/main`, and **167 local commits sit beyond the last remotely-gated commit** — inside the ~300 cadence the project documents, therefore not a schedule failure.
- ⛔ **`.13.3`'s original instruction — do NOT fix this by pushing early — STANDS, and now rests on a true premise.** `COMMIT.md`'s standing exception applies *while a remote gate is RED*; the remote is **green**, so the exception does not apply and the ~300 cadence governs. The earlier reasoning reached the right answer from the wrong fact, which is worth recording because the answer surviving is what makes the wrong fact easy to keep.
- ⚠️ **One downstream conclusion was built on the false premise and is CORRECTED rather than deleted.** `.11.4.7.2.3` wrote that the supply-chain gates "live only in `.github/workflows/supply-chain.yml`, which runs in REMOTE CI — and remote CI has never run … it is why two supply-chain gates have been red with nobody able to see it." The supply-chain workflow **ran and was green** at `c17841c`. The true cause is the unpushed gap plus both findings post-dating the last push — which that leaf had already established in its very next sentence. The conclusion survives; its stated cause does not.
- ⛔ **No doctrine check is added, and the reason is stated rather than left as an omission.** Every gate in `check_doctrines.sh` runs offline in a pre-commit hook; a check querying GitHub would fail without network or `gh` auth, turning an unrelated outage into a blocked commit. A gate that cannot run is worse than a documented command — so the command is documented and every claim names the commit it was measured at.
- Acceptance (as opened): the first remote run is consumed, not merely triggered; its result is recorded against the local checkpoint it corroborates; and every place this tree calls a gate "passed" is qualified as local until then. ⭐ **Met differently than written**: the runs were already there to consume, and consuming them is what falsified the leaf's own premise.
- Status: `done`; `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0220`. Register row **C1 is rewritten to what is true** rather than cleared — the row stays visible because the 167-commit gap is real, but it no longer claims the instrument has never run.
- Verification / commit: the four `gh` measurements above, each re-derivable; `docs/decisions/2026-09-17_remote-ci-has-run-and-is-green.md`; `make gate`; `make book`. `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0220`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.5 — The register asked a question about its reader

- Opened: `pending` by the director, 2026-09-17: *"Regarding the Blockers what does Ack? means? who decide that it should yes? To me, it is supposed to be you since I delegated that to you!"*
- 🔴 **THE DEFECT, named rather than apologised for.** `.13` gave the register an `Ack?` column meaning *"has the director engaged with THIS row"*, and a rule that every stopping-point reply re-surface every row whose value was `no`. ⛔ **That is a field whose value is a fact about the READER, in the maintainer's own register.** The register cannot observe it and the maintainer cannot set it, so the only mechanism available was to keep repeating the row until the reader reacted.
- **Measured, not felt.** `git log -S"Ack? = yes" -- docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md docs/book/src/blockers.md` returns **nothing**: from 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-17 the column was `no` on every open row and never once anything else. ⭐ A column whose value has never changed in its lifetime carries no information — the same shape as a control never seen RED, which this tree already refuses everywhere else.
- ⛔ **And it inverted a delegation.** The director had delegated blocker disposition; the column made his attention the precondition for a row to stop being repeated at him. The instrument for *surfacing* became an instrument for *nagging*, which is the failure mode that makes a reader skip the section the register exists to be read.
- ⭐ **THE REPLACEMENT, and it is a different question rather than a renamed one.** The register must answer *"is there anything left that THIS REPOSITORY can do about this row?"* — the only question that separates a blocker the maintainer should still be working from one genuinely parked on an outsider. The column becomes **`Owed here?`**, set by the maintainer from the owning leaf, beside the named next action.
- **The re-surfacing rule that follows from it:** a row with `Owed here? = yes` is **work**, belongs in the frontier and is worked like any other leaf; a row with `Owed here? = no` is surfaced **once per session** with its external party and trigger, not in every reply.
- 🔎 **The replacement paid for itself immediately, and this is the finding rather than the process.** Under `Ack?`, B1–B3 were reported to the director as *"OUTSIDE"* with nothing owed. Under `Owed here?` all three are **yes**: they share one in-repo prerequisite — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.14`'s frozen exposure candidate — which `docs/book/src/blockers.md` had *already named* under "The route out, decided 2026-09-16". ⛔ **The old column was hiding the maintainer's own work from the maintainer**, and the same reply that listed those rows as external also linked the page that said they were not.
- **The corrected values, derived from each owning leaf:** B1 **yes** (the threat model exists; its fitness for review is owed, and `.14` is what a reviewer reviews), B2 **yes** (the scope/environment document, and `.14`'s freeze is this row's own stated trigger), B3 **yes** (it lands with `.14`'s first action-bearing surface), B4 **no** (professional clearance in three jurisdictions — the only row with nothing owed here), C1 **no** and relabelled *not a blocker — a limit on what may be CLAIMED*, C2 **yes** (four gate records remain).
- Owns: the column, the rule that reads it, both copies of the register, and the correction to `.13`'s own acceptance clause.
- Acceptance: the column is one the maintainer can set and defend from a leaf; `.13`'s superseded clause is marked superseded rather than edited away; both the tree's table and the book chapter carry the new column and agree; the measurement that the old column never changed is recorded; and no row is removed.
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT change.** No blocker's substance moves: B1, B2 and B4 still require outside parties, and `.14` remains under its standing prohibition against turning the exposure profile on. What changes is which of them the maintainer treats as work.
- lockstep: README.md unchanged (this leaf changes a register column and the rule that reads it; the README names neither).
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0043`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4 — A corrected claim was corrected in the register and left standing in the corpus

- Opened: `pending` by `.13.4` itself, during the startup read of this session: the book's qualification chapter still stated *"remote CI has never run … the license decision remain open"*, two days and one day respectively after each had been measured false.
- 🔴 **THE SHAPE, and it is the one this tree has now met three times.** `.13.3` (REPAIR-0220) corrected blocker **C1** in the register, the book's blockers chapter, the decision record and the one downstream conclusion it could name inside this tree. `.13.2` (REPAIR-0195) cleared **B5**, the licence. Neither swept the LIVE-DOCUMENT corpus, so the superseded claims stayed readable in the two documents the director actually reads.
- **The census, over the live documents only** — `README.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `docs/book/src/*.md`, which are the documents COMMIT.md holds to CURRENT truth; `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`, `docs/decisions/` and `docs/tasks/artifacts/` are dated ledgers and are correct as history:

```bash
git grep -nI -E "never run|licen[cs]e decision|license decision" -- \
  README.md LIVE_STATUS.md MEMORY.md 'docs/book/src/*.md'
```

  **11 hits, classified: 4 STALE, 7 sound.** The four: `LIVE_STATUS.md:356` (the false CAUSE — "remote CI has never run" given as why two supply-chain gates were invisibly red), `:382` (the register's own description of row C1), `:1541`+`:1543` (the checkpoint paragraph, carrying BOTH stale claims), and `docs/book/src/qualification-review.md:546` (the same sentence, in the book). The seven sound ones are three unrelated uses of "never runs" (a DNS hook, an adapter load path), the two `blockers.md` passages that STATE the correction, and `MEMORY.md:17`, already corrected.
- ⭐ **The classification is the leaf, not the count.** A raw grep returns 11 and publishing that as a defect count would have been wrong in 7 cases — `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §3 leg 2's mirror, that a search hit-count is a population.
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `.13.3`'s acceptance line reads *"every place this tree calls a gate 'passed' is qualified as local until then"*. **This tree.** The correction's scope was the register and the task tree, and it did reach both, plus the one downstream conclusion at `.11.4.7.2.3` it happened to know about. ⛔ Nothing in its acceptance asked what else in the CORPUS restated the claim — which is precisely the defect class `.11.16` owns: a fact restated where nothing derives it. A claim corrected in its owner and left in its copies is the same failure as a number corrected in its source and left in its mirrors.
- **FIX** — the four stale instances are corrected in place and NOT deleted, each naming what it used to say and what measured it false, so a reader who remembers the old sentence finds out what happened to it. The dated artifact `checkpoint-7233122.md` is left **byte-unchanged**: it records what was measured on its date, and the book now says so explicitly.
- **ADDRESSED (verified)** — the census command above, re-run, returns **13** hits (the corrections are themselves text, so the population grows) and **0** of them assert either claim. The narrower probe is the one that closes the leaf: `git grep -nI -E "remote CI has never run|licen[cs]e decision remain open"` over the same four live documents returns **7** lines, and every one is a QUOTED correction — the register's rewritten row, the book's own correction table, `MEMORY.md`'s corrected blocker line and this leaf's own copies — with no bare assertion left. `make gate` 18/18; `make book` rc=0.
- **NO REGRESSION** — documentation only; no Rust source, migration or script changes, so the focused Rust checks are not the instrument for this slice. `make gate` runs the same staged-file doctrines a code commit does, including `DOCPATH`, `TABLE-ARITY-RATCHET`, `LIVE-DOC-CURRENCY` and `INDEX-FRONTIER`.
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT do.** It sweeps two corrected claims, not every claim. Whether a corpus sweep should be MECHANICAL — a gate that fails when a live document restates something a decision record has superseded — is `.11.16`'s question and is deliberately not answered here: the population has to be classified before a rule is proposed, which is `.11.6`'s standing rule and the reason this leaf publishes 4-of-11 rather than 11.
- ROUTING EVIDENCE: the general rule — *a correction is not complete until the corpus that restates it has been censused* — is routed to `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.16`, which already owns numbers restated where nothing derives them. What was measured here is that the shape reproduces OUTSIDE that leaf's original instance: `.11.16` was opened on a doctrine-registry count, and this is a prose CLAIM in two live documents, corrected by two different leaves on two different days. Two instances, two claim kinds, one shape.
- lockstep: README.md unchanged (it names neither claim; `git grep -nI -E "never run|licen[cs]e decision" -- README.md` returns nothing).
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0042`.


##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.2 — Twenty claims from one session re-derived: fourteen hold, and the three that failed are all the same mistake

- Opened and closed by the director's instruction of 2026-09-19, *"ensure the findings hold"* — the second time that challenge has been put, and this time to the eight commits `REPAIR-0292`…`REPAIR-0298`. `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` is the standard: **re-derive · falsify · durability**, three different questions, and every re-derivation by a route that did NOT produce the number.
- ⭐ **THE HONEST PREAMBLE, from §4.1.** *"The acceptance test the author must be able to pass in one word: when asked do you stand by it, the answer is yes, immediately, with no keyboard."* I could not answer in one word for three of these, and the re-audit is itself the evidence they were published before they were earned. What follows is the score, not a defence.

- ✅ **FOURTEEN HOLD, each by a route that did not produce it.**

  | claim | original route | verifying route | result |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | nothing serves the MCP tools | `git grep McpTools` + line positions | **`cargo metadata`'s resolved graph** — 0 workspace packages depend on `reasonbraid-mcp`; its only targets are `lib` + build script | ✅ |
  | …and nothing outside `crates/` serves it either | not asked | swept `Makefile`, `deploy/`, `scripts/`, `.github/` — **one** hit, `scripts/run_pg_tests.py`, the TEST runner | ✅ strengthened |
  | `ask_network` is not exposed | `git grep -c` | re-run at `HEAD` | ✅ **0** |
  | the offline-delivery expiry does not exist | `git grep -ci` | re-run at `HEAD` | ✅ **0 files** |
  | `sse-stream` is not vendored | registry listing | re-run | ✅ **0** |
  | `acknowledged_at` records a transport receipt | read ONE producer (`node.rs` step 4 → step 7) | **enumerated every writer**: 2 in production, both `node_channel.rs`; 2 production callers, `node.rs:315` and `worker.rs:187` | ✅ **strengthened — two paths, both journal before acking** |
  | `PresenceState::Busy` is never constructed | `git grep` | **the COMPILER**: removed `#[allow(dead_code)]` → `warning: variant Busy is never constructed` | ✅ |
  | `presence_state` has 5 production call sites | grep | grep excluding the defining file | ✅ **5** |
  | the book had no MCP surface | grep at working tree | `git show fdd3106:` — SUMMARY **0**, and 5 of 7 tools **0** | ✅ |
  | three chapters render clean | one read | re-read all three out of `docs/book/book/` | ✅ 3/17/0 · 2/11/0 · 6/27/0 |
  | 7/7 in-situ mutations caught | the sweep | re-ran the whole sweep against the COMMITTED bytes | ✅ **7/7**, all files restored byte-identical |
  | the census's `13 trees · 198 comparable · 0 duplicates · 62 · 10` | the census at HEAD | **`--at 5296048`**, its own commit | ✅ all five |
  | 664 vs an independent count of 685 | — | reconciled EXACTLY: 685 − 3 (`TEMPLATE`/`BOOTSTRAP`) − 9 (tree roots + `*-MAINT-N` ids) = **673** | ✅ |
  | **the 23 PHASE rows / 18 pairs the whole adjudication rests on** | the census at `fdd3106` | re-censused with today's instrument | ✅ **23 and 18, and the 18 pairs are the same 18** |

- 🔴 **THREE NAMED INSTANCES WERE WRONG, and §4.1 grades that class exact with no tolerance band. All three are one mistake: a number I inferred and published in the voice of one I measured.**
  1. 🔴 **`node_channel` *40 passed (39 before)* — THE DELTA IS FALSE.** `git show d82482b` adds **no test function**; the test it touches, `the_delivery_ladder_reads_through_the_inbox_state_view`, already existed; and the static `#[tokio::test]` count is **40 at `d82482b~1` and 40 at `HEAD`**. The suite was 40 on both sides — I extended a control, I did not add one. ⛔ I never ran the suite before the change; *39* was carried over from the shape of two earlier slices where I HAD added tests (`mcp_listen` 4→6, the lib 122→127, both true). **A delta is a SECOND measurement, not a consequence of the first.**
  2. 🔴 **`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.8`'s *`rb-server`, `rb-node`, `rb-cli`, `rb-site`, `rb-bench` and `rb-journal` are the workspace's binaries* — there are NINE.** `cargo metadata` adds `reasonbraid-browse`, `reasonbraid-extract` and `rb-release-manifest`; the first two declare no `[[bin]]` because they use `src/main.rs`, which is exactly what my `[[bin]]` grep could not see. ⭐ The CONCLUSION is untouched — none of the nine links `reasonbraid-mcp`, and the resolver says so — but the enumeration was a census published without being one.
  3. 🔴 **`respond` *(5 hits)* in the book — that is 5 FILES.** The command was `git grep -c … | wc -l`, which counts matching files; the hit count is **8**. The prose (*every one about the HTTP verb or its idempotency key*) holds; the unit did not.

- ⚠️ **TWO NUMBERS MOVED, both trajectory-grade, and one of them exposed a real defect in my instrument.**
  4. **`664 leaves / 562 finished` re-derives as `665 / 563` at its own commit.** I ran the census, then wrote the `.11.24.1` leaf, then committed — so the published figure describes a tree that was never committed. ⛔ *Measure, then edit, then publish the pre-edit number* is a leg-1 breach whatever the size of the gap.
  5. 🔴 **`53 stranded deferrals at fdd3106` re-derives as `60` AT THE SAME COMMIT** — because the instrument changed between the two runs (it learned the `- Opened and closed` idiom, which finished three more leaves, whose deferrals then counted). Neither number is wrong; **they answer different questions, and the published pair could not say which.** ⭐ The PHASE subset — the 23 rows the adjudication actually used — did not move at all, so no verdict changes.
- ✅ **AND THAT ONE IS REPAIRED RATHER THAN CORRECTED** (`docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §5B, and its own anti-pattern *"correcting a stale constant to a fresh constant and changing nothing about why it went stale"*). `scripts/census_goal_receipt_gap.py` now prints its own content hash beside every figure — `[instrument 65b213fc97bd]` — and `--at <rev>` prints both. **A figure from this census names a commit AND an instrument, because it is a function of both.**
- 🔴 **ONE LIVE-DOCUMENT FIGURE WENT STALE INSIDE THE SESSION, which is `.13.4.1`'s finding recurring one session later.** `LIVE_STATUS.md` carries *"`transport_received` has **0** hits in `crates`"* from REPAIR-0296 — and REPAIR-0297, the very next commit, renamed a state to it. ⚠️ The block immediately above it records the rename, so the file contradicts itself two lines apart. Annotated, not deleted: it was true at its commit and it is the finding's own evidence.
- ⭐ **THE SCORE ON §4.1'S THREE AXES, graded separately as it requires.** **PROSE: 20 of 20 hold** — no finding is withdrawn, no leaf re-opened, and the headline, the seven strandings and the rename all stand. **NUMBER: 2 moved**, both trajectory-grade, neither changing a decision. **NAMED INSTANCE: 3 wrong**, and that is the real failure, because a named row is the first thing a reader checks.
- 🔎 **THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL THREE NAMED-INSTANCE FAILURES is one habit, not three slips:** each was a number produced by reasoning that *looked like* the output of a command, published in a sentence shaped like a measurement. *39 before* was an analogy; *six binaries* was a grep answering a narrower question than the sentence; *5 hits* was a file count wearing a hit count's units. ⛔ **The tell in all three is that the sentence names a quantity the command I ran could not have produced** — and that is checkable at writing time, without re-running anything.
- Verification: every route above is a command in this leaf; the two cargo-derived facts come from `cargo metadata --format-version 1`; the compiler route is `cargo build -p reasonbraid-server --lib` with one attribute removed and `presence.rs` restored byte-identical (`git diff --quiet`); the mutation sweep is `/…/falsify.py`, re-run to `7/7`. `python3 -B scripts/census_goal_receipt_gap.py --self-test` → **12/12**. `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` green.
- **FIX / THE DECISION:** three named instances corrected at every site that carries them, two moved numbers corrected with their cause, one stale live-document figure annotated, and the instrument-identity defect repaired in the producer rather than in the copies.
- **NO REGRESSION** — one script change (a printed identity) and documentation; no product code, schema or test changed.
- promotion: **`docs/knowledge/a-delta-is-a-second-measurement.md`** — *a before/after pair is TWO measurements; publishing the "before" from the shape of an earlier slice is an analogy in a measurement's clothing, and the tell is that the sentence names a quantity the command could not have produced.* ⭐ Extracted rather than absorbed by `.11.20.2`'s criterion: `a-metric-scoped-to-one-record-ages-silently` is about a number going stale, and this is about a number that was never taken.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0299 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.2): twenty claims re-derived, fourteen hold, and the three that failed are one habit`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.3.1 — The revocation backfill is shipped and no control drives it

- Opened: `pending` by `.13.4.3`, which re-derived `REPAIR-0303`'s claims and found this one unexercised rather than wrong.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT.** `migrations/0077_authority_revoked_at.sql` carries two `UPDATE … FROM administrative_effects` statements that date already-revoked grants and boundaries from the act that revoked them. Every pg suite applies the migration, so the SQL parses and the upgrade path runs — but `git grep -n "revoked_at" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/tests` returns hits only for `node_certificates.revoked_at`, an older unrelated column, and for `.11.24.1.1.2.1.1.1`'s own control, which exercises the LIVE write path and not the backfill.
- ⛔ **So nothing asserts the backfill produces the right instant** — or any instant. A join that matched nothing would be indistinguishable from one that matched correctly, and `migration_upgrade` would stay green either way. That is `.7.1.2.2.1`'s shape (*a green gate is not evidence a suite runs*) applied to a data migration rather than a test suite.
- ⚠️ **What is NOT claimed:** that the backfill is wrong. Its predicate was read against the effect record's shape and its three legs argued in the migration header. The claim is that it is unwitnessed, and an unwitnessed migration is a class this tree has been bitten by before.
- Owns: a control that seeds a revoked row with an `applied` effect record and no instant, runs the migration, and asserts the instant equals the effect record's — plus the negative arm, that a revoked row with NO effect record is left NULL rather than defaulted.
- Acceptance: the control drives the MIGRATION, not the live write path (`migration_upgrade`'s existing fixtures are the shape to follow); both arms present; the `no_op`-outcome exclusion is driven too, since a repeated revocation must not re-date a row.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0306. **The backfill is witnessed, and it was right — six of its nine predicates can be turned red, and the three that cannot are recorded rather than faked.**
- ✅ **THE CONTROL EXISTS AND IT DRIVES THE MIGRATION.** `authority_revoked_at_upgrade_dates_only_what_an_applied_effect_dates` in `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/migration_upgrade.rs` follows `policy_lifecycle_tenant_upgrade_…`'s shape exactly: migrate `through(76)`, assert `revoked_at` is **absent** from both tables at that version (so the fixture cannot be seeding into the post-migration schema and measuring nothing), seed the pre-`0077` rows, snapshot them, `through(77)`, then read the column back.
- **ELEVEN ROWS, EACH WITH ITS ANSWER KNOWN BEFORE THE MIGRATION RUNS, and every effect record on a DISTINCT past instant** — so a predicate that lost a leg dates the wrong row with the wrong instant rather than merely dating one row too many, and an implementation reaching for `now()` fails rather than passes.

| Row | Its effect record | Expected after `0077` | The leg it drives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grt_applied_effect` | `applied`, same tenant | **dated `2026-03-01T04:05:06Z`** | the backfill itself |
| `grt_no_effect` | none | NULL | the pre-`0058` past — *not recoverable*, never *not revoked* |
| `grt_no_op_effect` | `no_op` | NULL | a repeated revocation's instant belongs to the first |
| `grt_refused_effect` | `refused` | NULL | a refusal changed nothing, so there is nothing to date |
| `grt_cross_tenant_effect` | `applied`, tenant `other` | NULL | `e.tenant_id = g.tenant_id` |
| `grt_active_with_effect` | `applied` | NULL | `g.status = 'revoked'` — WHEN, never WHETHER |
| `bnd_applied_effect` | `applied` `boundary_revoke` | **dated `2026-04-01T09:10:11Z`** | the second statement |
| `bnd_no_effect` / `bnd_no_op_effect` | none / `no_op` | NULL | the same two arms on the boundary half |
| `bnd_wrong_kind` | `applied` `grant_revoke` naming its id | NULL | `operation->>'boundary_id'` (measured — see below) |
| `bnd_host` | none, `active` | NULL | the live boundary the grants hang off |

- ⭐ **AND WHICH LEG EACH ARM ACTUALLY DRIVES IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED** — `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason` applied to a data migration. Nine mutations of `migrations/0077` were run against the control, each restored byte-identical (`target/falsify_0077.py`, `target/falsify_0077b.py`; `git status` clean after each matrix). **Six turn it RED**: both `UPDATE`s deleted · the grant statement's `outcome = 'applied'`, `e.tenant_id = g.tenant_id` and `g.status = 'revoked'` legs dropped · `e.effected_at` replaced by `now()` · the boundary statement's `operation->>'boundary_id'` leg dropped.
- ⚠️ **THREE LEGS CANNOT BE TURNED RED BY ANY UPGRADE, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN A HOLE IN THE CONTROL — which is why it is recorded instead of left looking covered.** Dropping EITHER statement's `operation->>'kind'` leg leaves the control GREEN, because `AdministrativeOperation` has exactly **one** variant carrying `grant_id` (`GrantRevoke`) and exactly **one** carrying `boundary_id` (`BoundaryRevoke`) — read off all fourteen variants — so for any record the encoder can produce the id-FIELD leg already implies the kind. The kind predicate is defense in depth against a future variant that adds one of those field names, and no producible row exercises it alone. Dropping `g.revoked_at IS NULL` is GREEN for a different reason: `ADD COLUMN` leaves every row NULL, so that leg guards a second run the migration ledger does not permit. ⛔ **Fabricating an unproducible row to turn those green arms red was REFUSED** — it would have measured the fixture's imagination, not the system.
- 🔎 **THE BACKFILL IS CORRECT.** The leaf opened claiming only that it was unwitnessed; on being witnessed, all eleven rows landed exactly as the migration header argued, first run, no correction to `migrations/0077`.
- Verification: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh migration_upgrade` → **6 passed, 0 failed**, rc=0 (`target/pg537b_guard.log`); the owned cluster stopped and was removed. `cargo clippy --offline --locked -p reasonbraid-server --test migration_upgrade -- -D warnings` rc=0 (`target/pg537_clippy.log`); `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book` rc=0. The nine-mutation matrix above, each arm a full suite run. `bash scripts/check_no_background_jobs.sh` → `handoff: OK`.
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `migrations/0077_authority_revoked_at.sql`: two `UPDATE … FROM administrative_effects` statements with no driver. Measured at `fd483eb`, the parent commit: `git grep -c "revoked_at" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/tests` returns **20 hits across 4 files** — `node_channel.rs` 11, `node_work.rs` 7, `administrative_effects.rs` 1, `node_enrollment.rs` 1, all of them either `node_certificates.revoked_at` (an older, unrelated column) or `.11.24.1.1.2.1.1.1`'s LIVE-write-path control — and **`migration_upgrade.rs` is not one of the four**. The sharper witness is the suite's own stopping points: `grep -o "through([0-9]*)"` over that file at `fd483eb` yields **54, 55, 56, 72, 73** and nothing higher, so no fixture stopped below `0077` to observe it at all. ⛔ WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE: every other pg suite migrates a FRESH database through the last migration, where the backfill's `WHERE` matches zero rows BY CONSTRUCTION — the statement runs, succeeds, and proves nothing.
- **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `authority_revoked_at_upgrade_dates_only_what_an_applied_effect_dates` in `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/migration_upgrade.rs`: `through(76)` → assert the column is absent → seed the eleven rows above → `through(77)` → read the column back, plus the *invents no history* arm (every pre-existing column byte-identical with `revoked_at` removed, and the row count unchanged) and the *WHEN never WHETHER* arm (`status = 'revoked'` still counts **5**). `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh migration_upgrade` → **6 passed, 0 failed**, rc=0 (`target/pg537b_guard.log`). ✅ All eleven rows landed as the migration header argued, first run.
- **NO REGRESSION** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh migration_upgrade authority node_work administrative_effects` → **65 passed, 0 failed**, rc=0 (`target/pg537c_guard.log`): the five pre-existing upgrade controls (6), the authority suite (22), `node_work` (12 — the live `revoked_at` write and the three-terminal prune) and `administrative_effects` (25 — the effect records this backfill joins against). The owned cluster stopped and was removed. ⚠️ The one shared surface a new test in this suite could damage is the fixture's `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE`, which this control reuses unchanged and leaves fully migrated. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book` rc=0; `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` **22/22**; `handoff: OK`. ⛔ No product code, SQL or schema changed: `migrations/0077` is byte-identical to `fd483eb` after all nine falsification mutations.
- **FALSIFIED** — by the six RED mutations, which is the strongest available form: the control is red whenever the behavior it names is absent, and the two GREEN mutations are explained by a property of the schema rather than waved past.
- promotion: **declined.** The transferable rule is already `docs/knowledge/a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason.md`'s, and what this leaf adds — *a predicate no producible input can isolate is documented, not faked red* — is a sharpening of it rather than a second note. Recorded here and in the control's own header; it goes to the note if a second instance appears.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0306 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.3.1): the revocation backfill is witnessed, and six of its nine predicates can be turned red`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.1 — The corpus rule does not reach the retrievable layer, and a promoted note went stale inside one session

- Opened and closed by the director's instruction of 2026-09-19, *"ensure the findings hold"* — the same challenge that opened `.7.1.1.1`, applied to a whole session rather than to one leaf. Eight leaves (REPAIR-0283…0290) had published figures; each was re-derived by a route that did not produce it.
- **THE PASS, route by route. Sixteen claims re-derived; fifteen hold and one was stale.**

| # | Claim | The independent route | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **nothing calls `mcp_listen`** (`.6.2.3.1`) | the COMPILER, not a grep: `mod mcp_listen;` DELETED outright, then `cargo build --workspace --lib` | ✅ **0 errors** — no caller in any crate, including the server's own `src/` |
| B | 21 index-assign sites, one caller-supplied (`.6.1.3`) | a third, wider key over `crates/*/src` | ✅ 64 raw hits, the extra ones `Vec`/slice indexing; the classification stands |
| C | `25/16`, `17 tables`, `residue 0` | recomputed from the baseline TSV by a standalone script, not by the census module | ✅ 25 · 16 · 17 · 0 |
| D | the lineage `30/17 → 29/16 → 27/14` | **today's instrument run in a worktree at each commit**, re-deriving the routes from that tree's SOURCE rather than reading its pinned file | ✅ tables **30 · 29 · 27** exactly; residue — see the sharpening below |
| E | suite counts `19→21`, `5→6→7`, `1→4` | a STATIC count of `#[test]` / `#[tokio::test]` attributes at each parent commit, against the runtime `N passed` | ✅ all seven |
| F | three suites gained `site_audit` (`.6.1.5.4`) | the commit's own diff: `+` lines containing `"site_audit"` | ✅ exactly 3 |
| G | the current state | `--check` on three censuses, `--self-test`, and the four MCP/policy suites re-run at HEAD | ✅ all rc=0; 21 · 4 · 7 · 6 |
| H | `derivations` 9, `resource_references` 12 | recomputed over `docs/decisions/` | ✅ both |
| H′ | **"all 170 decision records"** | counted at HEAD | 🔴 **STALE — it is 171** |

- 🔴 **THE ONE THAT FAILED IS MINE, AND IT WENT STALE INSIDE THE SAME SESSION.** `.7.1.2.2.3` (REPAIR-0284) published *"scanning ALL of `docs/decisions/` — over **170** records"*. `git ls-tree` gives **170 at `d29478a`**, the commit that published it, and **171 from `48ffdfb`** — because REPAIR-0286, two commits later, added `2026-09-19_the-write-quota-counts-calls-not-effects.md`. **I published a corpus size and then grew the corpus.**
- ⛔ **AND IT WAS STANDING IN THE RETRIEVABLE LAYER**, which is the finding this leaf exists for rather than the number. `.13.4` defines the live-document corpus as `README.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `MEMORY.md` and `docs/book/src/*.md`, with the dated ledgers correct as history. `docs/knowledge/` is in NEITHER set — so the stale figure sat in `a-metric-scoped-to-one-record-ages-silently.md`, **a note whose entire subject is figures that go stale**, and no rule said to sweep it. ⚠️ A stale number in a ledger is history and is correct as history; a stale number in a note is wrong every time the note is consulted, which is what a note is for.
- ✅ **THE REPAIR IS MECHANICAL, NOT A CORRECTION.** The note no longer quotes a corpus size at all — the argument rests on the **nine** and the **twelve**, which are properties of the key and do not grow — and it says so, naming its own first draft as the instance. `LIVE_STATUS.md` likewise. ⭐ And `census_shared_registry_writes.py`'s `RESTATING_DOCUMENTS` now includes that note, so the next movement in these figures NAMES it: the note restates the census's lineage, so it is part of the census's corpus by construction rather than by anyone remembering.
- ⚠️ **`CHANGELOG.md` keeps the `170` verbatim** — `.13.4`'s own rule: a dated ledger is history and is correct as history. The task-tree leaf and frontier row are ANNOTATED rather than rewritten, for the same reason.
- 🔎 **A SHARPENING ROUTE D PRODUCED, which is more interesting than the stale number.** `.7.1.2.2.3` wrote *"a metric naming ONE record ages the moment a second is written."* Measured at the two commits themselves: at `4c36840` the residue is **16 against DOC-0029 alone and 0 against DOC-0029 + DOC-0066**, and at `d1ba384` it is **14 and 0** — and **DOC-0066 already existed in the tree at both commits.** ⛔ So `residue 16` and `residue 14` were not *aged*; they were **misleading on the day they were published**. The figures are correct under their stated definition and wrong under the natural meaning of the WORD residue, which is outstanding work. The metric was not overtaken by a later record — it was already behind one.
- ⭐ **That is why the repair had to be the scope and not the number.** Bumping 17→16→14 kept producing arithmetically correct figures about a question nobody was asking any more.
- ⚠️ **Scope, stated: this pass verified PUBLISHED FIGURES, not every sentence.** Sixteen numeric or enumerable claims were re-derived. Prose judgements — *the repair is a direction*, *a clamp not a refusal* — are decisions with reasons recorded at their leaves and are not the kind of claim this instrument answers.
- Verification: every route above, re-run at this commit. `census_shared_registry_writes --self-test` **45/45**, `--check` rc=0; `census_registry_read_reach --check` rc=0 (`29 site-global tables, unchanged`); `census_fixture_write_reach --check` rc=0; `policy` 21, `mcp_listen` 4, `mcp_write` 7, `mcp` 6 — 0 failed. `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` green (21/21). The three verification worktrees were removed and `git worktree list` shows only the main tree.
- **FALSIFIED** — the new `RESTATING_DOCUMENTS` entry is covered by the existing arm *the restating documents are named and tracked*, which fails on a path that is not tracked; the note's path was confirmed tracked by the arm passing at 45/45 with it added. ⛔ Route A is itself the falsification of the no-caller claim: deleting the module is the strongest possible negative, and the build's 0 errors is the observation.
- promotion: **declined, with the extension recorded instead** — the transferable rule is already `docs/knowledge/a-metric-scoped-to-one-record-ages-silently.md`'s, and what this pass adds is that **the note itself was in the blast radius**. That is recorded there, in `RESTATING_DOCUMENTS`, and at `.13.4` as the corpus definition's gap. ⚠️ Extending `.13.4`'s corpus to all of `docs/knowledge/` mechanically is NOT done here: the right mechanism is per-instrument `RESTATING_DOCUMENTS`, which names the notes that restate a given figure, rather than a blanket sweep of 42 notes on every correction.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0291 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.1): sixteen published figures re-derived, fifteen hold, and the one that went stale was in the note about going stale`.

🔴 **The command this caption used to publish that number was wrong, and it had been under-reporting for as long as the `TASK-STATUS` convention has existed.** It matched `- Status: \`pending\`` only. Since `TASK-STATUS` made a leaf's opening line `- Opened:`, a leaf that has never closed may carry `- Opened: \`pending\`` and **no `- Status:` line at all** — 11 leaves do. The caption said 36 where the tree held 46. A leaf's state is its last `- Status:` line if it has one and its `- Opened:` line otherwise, and the command re-derives it that way:

```bash
awk '/^#{3,6} SIGNOFF-REPAIR/{if(h!="")print s; h=$0; s="none"} \
     /^- Status:/{s=$0} /^- Opened:/{if(s=="none")s=$0} \
     END{if(h!="")print s}' docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md | grep -c '`pending`'
```

🔴 **That de-duplication did not hold, and this caption is why it was invisible.** It used to read *“Row 5 is the ONLY entry left from the previous frontier's duplicated pair”* — true when written. A later commit promoted `.4.2.3.1` to row 1 and the pair came back; the sentence went on asserting it was gone until `.4.2.3.1`'s own closure read the table. ⚠️ A prose statement that a class of defect has been removed reads as a live guarantee and nothing re-derives it. The population is **1 unfinished duplicate across all 15 tracked trees**, discharged here, and the rule-or-decline is `.11.22.1` at row 5. A curated list with a duplicate in it invites a reader to work the same leaf twice or to read the second row as a different leaf.

## Commit acceptance — SIGNOFF-REPAIR.3.4.3

- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — the leaf's own question, answered by tracing the clock rather than by reading the comparison. `decided_at` is the SERVER's database clock (`database_now_in_tx` in `api.rs`, `tx.database_now()` on the replay path — the only two writers of `node_inbox.decided_at`, and no request field reaches either), while `is_fresh(now)` is called from `worker.rs` with the NODE's `Utc::now()`. The comparison is therefore cross-clock, and a future `decided_at` is backward node skew and nothing else. Reproduced as a control: a decision received a full window ago and stamped 600 s ahead of the node's clock DISPATCHES on the unchanged code, where it should have expired 10 s earlier.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `CachedDecision::allow` in `crates/reasonbraid-core/src/authority.rs` derived `expires_at` from the server instant alone (`decided_at + 60 s`) and `is_fresh` compared it against a node instant, so with the node behind by `S` the window is `S + 60 s` of node-observed time. The TTL is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: `revocation_epoch` is bumped in exactly two places, both explicit revocations, so a grant reaching its own `expires_at` bumps nothing and natural expiry is bounded at the node by the freshness window alone.
- [x] **FIX** — the window runs from `decided_at.min(received_at)`, the node's own receipt already stored in `commands.received_at`. It binds iff the node received the decision before its clock says the server made it, is byte-for-byte the shipped behaviour for any ordinary receipt, and can never refuse work the plain rule allowed (the window always ends at least one TTL after receipt). `journal.rs` reads the receipt into the decision and refreshes it when a REPLAY delivers a new decision, guarded on the decision having actually changed so a plain poll redelivery cannot re-anchor the window.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py cargo test -p reasonbraid-core -p reasonbraid-node --locked --lib --test journal_cli --test journal_kill_points --test supervisor_budget --test supervisor_codex_stub --test supervisor_fake --test worker_cached_decision --test worker_dead_letter --test worker_retry_policy` returns rc=0 with **10 targets, 116 tests, zero failures**. ## Commit acceptance — SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.2.3

- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — tranche 3's last five records, 1,762 characters, the largest of its three children. Every clause read at the SOURCE.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — 🔴 **`browse.rs::run_browse` waits for the child to EXIT before reading its piped stdout**, and the request it writes sets `max_output_bytes` to 4 MiB against an OS pipe buffer of at most 64 KiB, so any response above roughly 64 KiB blocks the worker's own write, the child never exits, and the loop returns `TimedOut`. Its stdin-error path drops a live `Child` (neither kills nor waits) and its timeout path kills the worker but not the browser beneath it. 🔴 **Four adapter defects, each at TWO sites** because `codex.rs` and `claude.rs` share a shape: a byte slice of a `String` that panics off a char boundary, an unbounded `next_line` under a bound checked before the append, a `children` map that is never removed from, and a `turn.completed` arm that returns without awaiting the drain or waiting the child while the EOF arm does both. 🔴 **A deadline is computed and shipped and read by nobody** — grepping every adapter source and the supervisor returns one hit, the struct field's own declaration. 🔴 **A completed item reaching the retry gate is dead-lettered and auto-quarantined** (`retry.rs:80`'s catch-all `Some(_) => Refuse`, and `worker.rs:275` maps every refusal to `report_dead_letter`), and that report never acknowledges its own outgoing row while its sibling `Node::emit_event` does.
- [x] **FIX** — `RECONCILIATION.md` gains Tranche 3c: **22 clause rows**, 16 `owned`, 6 `attach`, 0 `unowned`. All six `attach` clauses written into `.10.1` (1) and `.4.4` (5) in this commit. ⭐ Tranche 3 is complete at 15 records and 69 clauses.

- [x] **MEASURED, and three of the measurements are stronger than a reading would have been** — (1) a RATIO: 4 MiB configured against a 64 KiB pipe buffer, which says the deadlock covers most of the intended range rather than an edge case. (2) A SINGLE-HIT GREP: `deadline` appears once across every adapter source and the supervisor, which quantifies over all call sites at once. (3) A CONTRAST over a population of two: `Node::emit_event` acknowledges its outgoing event and `Worker::report_dead_letter` does not, so the omission is conclusive rather than suggestive.
- [x] **NARROWED, not confirmed** — `R-6-27-9`'s "`OutcomeUnknown` propagates a fatal `WorkerError` so the retry policy may never run except restart": the propagation is real (`supervisor.rs:358` returns it as an `Err`), and `SupervisorError::OutcomeUnknown`'s own doc says it is deliberate — "a fact, not a retry recommendation". Whether a caller's loop re-dispatches in-process is NOT established, and the row says so.
- [x] **The candidate list is a SUGGESTION, measured** — the narrowest candidate `.10.1` is the OWNER of 1 of this child's 5 records: `R-36-39-8` lands on `.7.3` and three land on `.4.4`, whose Sources line names the two test files two of them are about. The ranking still did its job — it groups records that must be READ together, not records that will be OWNED together.

## Commit acceptance — SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.1.4
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — ⛔ **There is no defect to reproduce, and the leaf says so rather than manufacturing one.** `gate()` commits its quota `use` in its own transaction before `run_thread_command` applies idempotency, and `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/mcp_write.rs`'s module header has always said so. - [x] **FIX / the decision** — `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_the-write-quota-counts-calls-not-effects.md`: the quota bounds **call volume**, not effects, so a call the handler refuses HAS spent quota and an idempotent replay spends it again. ⛔ The argument is the bound's own purpose — the abuse surface is the CALL, and refunding on refusal would hand an attacker an unlimited supply of refused calls, the invitation-storm surface inverted rather than bounded. The heading is corrected to name the split and point at the control that owns it; the semantics are published in `docs/book/src/errors.md` beside `quota_exceeded`, because a client can be surprised by them.

## Commit acceptance — SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.2.1
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — the control in its FINAL form, against the shipped module: `panicked at crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/mcp_listen.rs:232: the newest id is IN the window: first=Some("d-000") last=Some("d-063")`, `test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored`. The window had frozen on the first 64 ids it ever saw; the parent's census had already measured that replaying `d-069` was ACCEPTED and `d-000` skipped.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/mcp_listen.rs`: `next.push(delivery_id.to_string()); next.truncate(DEDUP_WINDOW);`. `push` appends to the END and `truncate` keeps the FRONT, so once the window held `DEDUP_WINDOW` ids every new id was written at index `DEDUP_WINDOW` and discarded on the same line. ⛔ The consequence is a DOUBLE DELIVERY: this function's `true` is what tells the caller to commit the delivery's effects, and its own doc comment says so.
- [x] **FIX / the decision** — `next.push(id); if next.len() > DEDUP_WINDOW { next.drain(..next.len() - DEDUP_WINDOW); }`. ⭐ The array stays CHRONOLOGICAL — oldest first, newest last — so an existing row keeps its meaning and the drain removes from the old end; reversing to newest-first was rejected because it would silently re-interpret every stored row. ⭐ It also HEALS a row that is already over-long, whatever wrote it, which matters because nothing in `migrations/0050` bounds the array's length.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh mcp_listen` → `test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`, rc=0 (1 before this leaf). Adjacent, chosen because they are the other MCP surfaces: `mcp_write` → `ok. 7 passed; 0 failed`; `mcp` → `ok. 6 passed; 0 failed`. `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0.
- [x] **FALSIFIED (in situ, self-reversing, restored byte-identical)** — restoring the shipped `push` + `truncate`, the exact line this leaf replaced and nothing else, reproduces the identical RED: `the newest id is IN the window: first=Some("d-000") last=Some("d-063")`, `1 passed; 1 failed`. `cmp -s` reports `mcp_listen.rs` byte-identical against its pre-neutralization copy; the run afterwards is 2/2.
- [x] **BOTH ARMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO OMIT** — a window that simply grew without bound refuses every replay and passes arm 1, so the repair would be a memory leak wearing a fix's clothes. The control asserts `ids.len() == DEDUP_WINDOW` directly, proves the NEWEST id is refused on replay, and proves an id that has FALLEN OUT is accepted. ⚠️ `DEDUP_WINDOW` is re-exported through `mcp_listen_internal` so the control reads the published bound rather than restating `64`: a test that hardcodes the constant it is testing against stops testing it the moment the constant moves.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — one product file changed, three lines, plus one re-export. ⚠️ The pre-existing two-delivery control is unchanged and still passes, which is the point of keeping it: it was never wrong, it was never wide enough, and a control that does not cross a boundary cannot see what happens at it. `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` green (21/21). ⚠️ `.6.2.2` and `.6.2.3` are untouched and still live — named here because `.6.2.2` COMPOSES with this one: a rewound cursor re-offers deliveries, and until this commit the window could not suppress them.
- [x] **A CITATION I INVENTED, CAUGHT AND CORRECTED** — this leaf's promotion line first cited `docs/knowledge/a-control-is-as-wide-as-the-boundary-it-crosses.md`, a plausible filename for a rule I wanted to point at and a file that does not exist. ## Commit acceptance — SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.2.2
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — `assertion left == right failed: the cursor is a HIGH-WATER MARK and does not rewind; resume_plan reads it as the resume point, so a rewind re-offers everything above it`, `left: 5`, `right: 100`, `test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored`. Recording cursor 100 and then cursor 5 left the stored cursor at 5.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/mcp_listen.rs`: `SET last_cursor = $1, last_delivery = $2`, unconditional. `resume_plan(own_cursor, …)` reads that column as the resume point, so a single out-of-order delivery rewinds it and every delivery above it is re-offered on the next reconnect. ⚠️ Until `.6.2.1` the dedup window could not suppress the redeliveries either — the two defects composed, which is why the parent's census recorded them together.
- [x] **FIX / the decision** — `SET last_cursor = GREATEST(last_cursor, $1)`: a **CLAMP, not a refusal**. ⛔ Refusal was REJECTED with its reason: a late delivery is a real delivery, the dedup check immediately above has already established it is new, and dropping it is a worse outcome than the cursor problem it would fix. The delivery is applied and enters the window; only the mark is protected. ⭐ A second decision rides with it — `last_delivery = CASE WHEN $1 > last_cursor THEN $2 ELSE last_delivery END`, so the pair stays ONE fact, *the delivery that set the mark*, rather than two independent latest-writes that can disagree about which delivery they describe. `listen_state` returns them together as the reconnect's input.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh mcp_listen` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`, rc=0 (2 after `.6.2.1`, 1 before the lane opened). `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0.
- [x] **FALSIFIED (in situ, self-reversing, restored byte-identical)** — restoring the unconditional `SET last_cursor = $1, last_delivery = $2`, the exact clause this leaf replaced and nothing else, reproduces the identical RED: `left: 5`, `right: 100`, `2 passed; 1 failed`. `cmp -s` reports `mcp_listen.rs` byte-identical against its pre-neutralization copy; the run afterwards is 3/3.
- [x] **THE ARM THAT KEEPS IT A CLAMP RATHER THAN A SILENT DROP** — the control REPLAYS the late delivery and asserts it is refused, which proves its id really entered the dedup window. ⛔ Without it, a repair that simply ignored low-cursor deliveries would pass every other assertion in the test: the cursor would read 100, `last_delivery` would read `d-hi`, and the delivery would be gone. A control that only checks the number it was worried about cannot tell a fix from a different bug.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — one SQL statement changed in one product file. Forward progress is asserted unchanged in the same control: a delivery above the mark advances BOTH halves. The two pre-existing controls are untouched and pass. `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` green (21/21).
- [x] **LOCKSTEP** — the task tree (this leaf's closure, the frontier, this checklist), `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/mcp_listen.rs`, `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/mcp_listen.rs`, `docs/TASK_TREE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `DEV_NOTES.md` carry the same scope. lockstep: `docs/book/` unchanged — the cursor is internal durable state with no documented surface; `docs/decisions/` unchanged — clamp-versus-refusal is recorded at the code and at this leaf, and it binds one column rather than a cross-cutting rule.
